My first tea from Dilmah, it has fairly typical Ceylon (Sri Lanka) flavor, but is quite a bit more robust and flavorful  than the typical mass produced black teas.  I'm guessing the grade of this tea is BOP (broken orange pekoe), not whole leaves, but a good grade or so above what you get in teabags. Still, it steeps quite quickly, and a little bit goes a long way.  It has a fresh, rich flavor, not necessarily complex, but full bodied and well balanced with a touch of acidity along with the maltiness and astringency that is typical of black teas of this kind.  It is somewhat individualistic, though, probably due to it being a single origin tea rather than a blend.  A word that comes to mind is "flavoury," sometimes applied to Sri Lankan teas.  The description on the side of the tin says it's "a medium tannin tea with pronounced woody flavours and a medium length finish."In steeping, I use a Teeli permanent filter to allow room for the leaves to expand, and throw away a first quick rinse of the tea before steeping a cup to drink.  Rinsing the tea makes it mellower and less astringent.  A relatively short steeping time of a minute or two is all that is necessary.One correction needed in the description is that there is no foil pouch in the tin, but there is an inner lid, and each tin comes individually shrink wrapped, which probably helps the tea remain fresh.  Considering how little tea you need to make a cup or pot, you get a pretty good deal here with three tins.

My first memory of tea was at my Grandfather's house, sitting at his table sipping tea with cream (the real thing)& sugar.  I was hooked on that wonderful flavor & later dropped the sugar & began taking it with cream or just black.  As we grow our tastes change & it seemed that I would never regain that elusive flavor that I remembered from having tea with him.After many years of trying thousands of cups, I purchased Dilmah Ceylon Supreme in 2009.  At the first taste I was transported back to my Grandfathers table watching him pour cream into my cup, waiting for me to sip & asking me "How's that?"  The year was 1959.Not to astringent, great flavor, so you know you are really drinking TEA, & a nice comforting aroma.  Really something I can appreciate.

One of the best loose tea in the market. Now my mornings don't start without Dilmah. All thanks to Dilmah for bringing the best in the finest and freshest form.  This particular tea keeps me fresh and relaxes my mind and is a perfectly rounded and wel balanced tea with its own aroma.  I am so glad to have found this tea on Amazon. I would highly recommend this tea who wants to enjoy the finest cup of tea.

Single note, strong tea. No discernible citrus taste which is usually typical of high grade Ceylon tea. I think I will stick to Peet's "Buddha Peak Ceylon" loose leaf tea- now that is a great cup of Ceylon tea. Good Ceylon tea should be bright, citrusy and malty with balanced astringency.None of which can be said for this tea. Overall, this an okay-ish everyday drinking tea. I am not re-ordering once I am through with my 3 boxes. Plus, calling the tea "tea leaves" is a misnomer. This is more like tea dust grade, the tea dust is so fine. That is why the fragrance/bouquet of the tea is almost non existent.

I reviewed another Dilmah Tea as perfect for everyday use.  I would also place this tea in the category of "regular use" tea and not specialty top-o-the-line teas.  This incarnation is slightly more expensive because you are paying for the great tea tins.  Buy this kind at least once so you can transfer other teas into the well designed reusable canisters!This tea has a small leaf, and did not oversteep to bitter.  It has a nostalgic taste from the 1970's of pure Ceylon Tea, sadly lacking in today's tea.

Best loose leaf tea I have tried, way better than the others. Takes a short time to steep and you don't have to use very much. The tin that it is packaged in is great the two lid design is excellent.(opened a tin to day that was 1/4 full and was at least a year and a half old smelled fresh as the day I got it and it tasted great)It is slightly more expensive than bulk teas but it is well worth the extra 3-7$ you really get what you pay for here.What ever you steep the tea in needs to have very small holes because the tea is very fine.

The Dilmah is a competent black tea.  There was nothing remarkable about the taste or the experience.  It is very finely ground, so make sure your tea holder has very small holes or you will end up with loose tea in your cup.
Not much to say except that this is an excellent quality black tea with great flavor and bouquet.

Right this moment, i am enjoying my first cup of Dilmah tea...I'm in heaven.  The aroma, the flavor, the texture, it is simply SUPERB! Thank you Dilmah people for all your hard work and dedication, it truly pays every cent of this marvelous tea. Keep up offering such great products.(I dont think this purchase will last long in my house, it is too good).Olga, from Costa Rica.

column9: Dilmah Ceylon Supreme is My Everyday Tea
column10: This has become my everyday tea.  I have experimented with many different types of tea over the past 2 years since I became a loose tea addict.  I don't know all of the official tea drinker's lingo but I will do my best.  The Ceylon Supreme is the nicely balanced tea I was looking for for.  It is smooth but still has a light astringency or brightness to it without being bitter.  This is what I drink now instead of coffee.  It is great hot, cold or at room temperature.  I still buy and try other teas such as Oolongs and flavored teas for occasional drinking but I recommend this one for the morning brew.  I also like the metal container.  The double lid keeps the tea fresh and stays closed so that it is good for traveling.

column9: Great tea for a decent price
column10: This is good quality, strong black tea. The tin is smaller than you'd expect, but each one does hold a full 1/4 pound because the tea is so finely cut. I can't imagine drinking it without milk, and in fact I blend it with Darjeeling for a somewhat milder taste, but all in all, good value for the price.

column9: Go easy if you are used to teabags
column10: This is a wonderful full bodied tea.  I will never buy teabags again.  But, having been a teabag drinker all my life, I did not realize how diluted it was until I tried loose tea.  I would recommend using much less tea than their instructions say.  I make it in a coffee maker which I use exclusively for tea and use 2 teaspoons blended with a teaspoon of blackcurrant tea per 12 cups.  Following their instructions resulted in a tea that was bitter.  Experiment till you find the proportions that suit you.  It is well worth the experimentation.I drink as iced tea and when drinking hot, cream perfectly complements it.

Just had my first cup of this tea today. I use milk and sugar in my tea and while it is a good tea, there is a slight bitter aftertaste. And no, I did not leave it sit on the grounds too long. I wish I could have bought one canister at a time instead of three. Not sure I will be able to go through all that tea.However I do applaud the enlightened owner of the plantation according to the written information which came with the tea. I only would like  to enjoy the taste of the tea more.

so far i have bought the ran and meda watte varieties, as well as the supreme ceylon, several other Dilmah over the counter teas.this tea is more tannic and of lower quality than the dilmah ceylon i can get at our local indian grocery store. its is finely powdered in a nice tin, but its not in a sealed bag. thats a bummer when you have to  buy three and they sit around for a while
We loved the Dilmah Ceylon Supreme Tea and only hope that Amazon keeps it in stock since we want to order more!

My husband and I recently gave these chocolates to our friend for his birthday (ours was in a tin that looks just like a bottle of Jose Cuervo).  We were at a restaurant with all of his friends and family (around 20 people), and once he opened this, everyone wanted to try them.  A couple of people tried them right there at the table and said they were delicious and that they had never seen them before.  It was definitely a unique gift and one that many tried to sneak away with ;o)
A rather strange tasting pea soup. Not at all like any other I've tried.  Not that it wouldn't be bad but it's just too off for me to recommend.

column9: So much easier on my babies tummy.
column10: When we switch my daughter from nursing to eating her first solid foods we started with rice cereal.  The misery that caused will be forever emblazoned on my memory.  Colic, gas, and it backed her up right proper.My wife and I started researching alternatives on the Internet.  We found a bunch of references to how Barley was easier on a tummy.  That Barley soup/broth is often what is given to people recovering in hospitals etc...  I went to every local store looking for some.  Family and friends that had used it used to buy it locally.  I couldn't find it anywhere.  I found it here on Amazon and bought this pack of 12 boxes.We found rather strongly that this was much easier on my daughters tummy.  She continued to eat without distress after we made the switch.  We started using it just as cereal and then as she got older we started using it as a thickening agent and filler when mixed with pureed vegetables etc...  She liked things better when they were less runny and we liked things better when she was happy.We will be ordering more here shortly for the twins that have now joined our family.  For us it worked great.  I really do recommend it as a far better option that rice cereal.

column9: gerber barley cereal - very healthy choice for a baby
column10: Healthy choice for my baby, very convenient package, easy to prepare, my baby loves it, no added milk or fruit, which may either spoil the real taste of the product, or cause allergic reaction. Best choice for busy parents.
These boxes are smaller than the size I normally buy in the store but I think that's a bonus.  They stay fresh longer since they are sealed.  Great product.
I have to say, I'm definitely looking for a deal when it comes to baby food and this is one. Compared to the store prices even with coupons, buying by the case is a great buy.

column9: My son's 2 and this is still his preferred breakfast
column10: I mix cereal, cheese & hot milk, and my son gobbles up his breakfast.I find this to be the best when compared to nutritional value when compared with Rice, Wheat or Mixed grain.

column9: Good Nutrition, Doesn't Like The Taste Much
column10: It's good and filling for my child but when given to him by itself he doesn't like the flavor. I usually mix it with a banana but I have recently started to buy the mixed fruit cereal which is sweet and mixing one pack of each and that seems to do the trick. Plus, the oatmeal is cheaper than the mix fruit so it lasts longer :-)

column9: Easier online, no deal on price
column10: I purchased this product online because I couldn't find it in the stores at that time (2 days later it was in the store also). It's good that comes quick, save a trip to the store, however, no deal on the price; same as Walmart, Kroger, etc.

column9: 50c per box more expensive than stores
column10: I purchased this product online because I couldn't find it in the stores at that time (2 days later it was in the store also). It's good that comes quick, save a trip to the store, however, the price is so much higher than Walmart, Kroger, etc (50c per box more expensive, total 7$ more expensive than the stores)

column9: Gerber is always the best food for baby
column10: My baby loves this cereal. He is allergic to many foods, but with Gerber I can be sure that there are no hidden ingredients. EAsy to prepare, easy to keep fresh, convenient packaging. I highly recommend it to the parents as one of the first foods for a baby.

the only reason I purchased this on amazon is because I could not find it in the stores and the pediatrician had recommended it for my infant grandson.  It does not disolve well and tends to clump up in the nipple.

I keep Gerber 'Mixed' and 'Barley' on hand all the time. The 'mixed' consists of rice, oat and wheat so I mix a box of that with a box of the 'barley' and have a completely balanced breakfast cereal. I don't use it for people: I keep it handy for when the dogs have upset tummies and their regular food is too harsh on their digestive systems and they need soft, easy to digest food that fills them up and is healthy for them.  As their tummies return to normal, I reduce the baby cereal a bit and add in some of their normal foods and as they continue to improve, the baby cereal gets reduced while their normal foods eventually return to full bore.This is good for them, too, after dental cleanings/extractions, surgeries, when they need a little help in the 'bowel' department (fiber), or just as an added treat to change it up a bit in their daily diet.I have used this in place of bread crumbs when making a meatloaf (ok, I was desperate), but didn't care for the texture of the meatloaf once cooked. It was too soft for our liking, but still quite tasty.

The clam chowder actually tastes pretty decent, but it seems to have very small pieces of clam shells or something that gives it a gritty texture. I don't know what it is, but I just can't stand it when I bite into something that feels like glass crunching in my teeth.

This soup has a lot of sand in it.  I could not choke it down when I tried it last week.  It is a quick meal, but it's no fun eating soup'n sand chowder.  They need to improve on their Quality Control or discontinue the product all together.  Avoid this stuff.
Taste is ok - good for a quick lunch.  However if you are prone to heartburn - this brings it on quickly and swiftly!  Better off sticking to chicken noodle if you have issues there...

column9: If you like clam chowder, this will satisfy
column10: It's not gourmet stuff, but this is good clam chowder.  A minute in the microwave, and out pops a good, quick meal.  Add a grilled cheese sandwich, and you have a working man's ambrosia.

column9: Bland, mostly flavorless white soup with potato
column10: This soup has no discernible dairy or clam flavor at all.  There is a bland white base, chemically thickened, with no hint of milk, butter, or cream.  I found mostly chunks of white potato and a small quantity of tiny, hard, flavorless clam fragments. There is a faint chemical aftertaste and a little sand.  Doesn't taste remotely like any clam chowder I've ever eaten before.

Good clam chowder for out of a can. Quick and easy to heat for the office. Amazon's price is way too high as I can buy this product at Winco or Walmart in Portland, OR for $1.62 per container, ($12.96 for pack of 8). Amazon normally has good prices but with Campbell soup they struck out. Sorry Amazon. (It will be interesting to see if they publish this review)

I like the convenience of the packaging.  No dishes to wash either.  It has a decent amount of tiny clam pieces too.  Tastes good, but I have a few comments.  First, it takes longer than 90 seconds to microwave it.  I usually nuke it for 30 seconds, stir it, then nuke it for another 90 seconds.  It's the same with other Campbell's microwavable products like the Firehouse Chili.  I agree with the other reviewer that it's gritty.  Maybe some sand got in the shell of the clams or it has some small shell fragments?  It also has a funny smell after microwaving it.  I think the funny smell comes from the outer plastic packaging and not the soup.  The soup tastes just fine, but needs some Tabasco or a little spicing up.

Thank you Amazon for making this home delivery possible. I love this soup and so many of your products. I broke my ankle on Memorial and am supposed to stay off my feet with foot elevated. Makes going to the grocery store almost impossible (or at least unloading the car to carry all the groceries in and put away). You home delivery is quick and cost effective. Besides, this is great clam chowder! Easy to prepare, just zap in the microwave and its ready to eat! nice serving size!

column9: Campbell's Chunky New England Clam Chowder 15.25oz
column10: I have been buyin the case of these every 2 weeks for the last year. Taste is good, just add pepper.Only had one time that the case I received was bad and Amazon quickly sent me a replacement case and I also contacted Campbells's about it and they acted very nicely and sent me some discount coupons for my troubles.

column9: Not the best but not the worst
column10: These are good for what I needed them for - something easy to bring to work for lunches.  They are good portions and heat up in a little over a minute.  It's not the best tasting canned clam chowder - a little on the watery side and has almost a sour aftertaste - but it's totally fine and palatable for the price.

I really love this product of sencha tea. I'm currently down to one bag..I definitely will be ordering more. The bright green color is mesmerizing and the taste is superb! I first bought this product in New York's China Town and had to have it ever since.

I have tried almost all brands of green tea in the last 15 years or so and with the exception of Stash, the rest taste like warm water. I found an Asian market in my area that had a large selection of green teas but they were equally disappointing, until I found YamaMotoYama. I have been drinking two to three cups of this every morning for the past two years and see no reason to change. Try it, you'll like it!

I had high hope for this tea because of some previous reviews saying, "superior to anything I have tried." It's not. I prefer the one I had before this one(see my another review)While it's not bad, it's no better than average sencha. What do you expect from the lowest priced tea you can find in amazon? Then again, it's a matter of taste, it can be very subjective.But for the price, I'd recommend it to the future buyers.

I drink many types of Green tea, from ones that are ~$40/200g to this stuff (~ $8/200 g), and I have to say the more expensive stuff is better, I cannot deny.  That said, for the money this is a great every day drinking tea that i would recommend, and always have in my tea arsenal.  Important the water be 70 - 80 deg C, and steep for 1 - 2 minutes for best enjoyment, and no astringency.
Make no mistake..this is one big bag of peanuts. Best when purchased on sale in Amazon Warehouse Deals. Get em at a good price and go make some friends.
I have had this plant for over a year. It takes minor work and has stayed very much like the picture.

I'm so happy to find a gluten-free on-the-go option for lunch. Just the other day I was thinking, I wish they made gluten-free lunchables.  I'm sorry that the other people have more unusual allergies that they would like items for, but this is a great start for many people.  It's great to see the calories labeled on each box.  I had the hummus box today and it was great...everything was fresh and tasty.  I plan to order more.  I do wish they were a little bit cheaper since it does get very expensive to eat gluten-free but those of us who have the intolerance don't have it by choice while those who are vegan or vegetarian choose to be so.

I bought these soon after trying a gluten free diet. I should note I'm really not picky, I will eat almost anything. That said, some of these meals were pretty decent, and others I had a hard time finishing.Overall, I enjoyed the GF crackers. Only complaint is that one bag in one kit would have 20 crackers, and the next would have 8. (I also bought a 6 pack of just the pepperoni/cheese/crackers kits, so it wasn't a fluke... there was a wide variety in the number of crackers a single bag contained.)My least favorites were the salmon and tuna. I usually love both, and these were really hard to force down.As always with food, your mileage may vary. I personally have moved onto other snacks and foods, so I won't be buying these again.

I like the variety in the gluten free pack. The packs are great. I take them to work for a quick lunch when I don't have time to prepare ahead of time. They taste great and are healthier than buying fast food. The only issue I have is with the turkey pepperoni meal which is way too salty. I don't have issues with high blood pressure or anything like that, but I find that almost 900 mg of sodium for this meal is a bit much. I order go picnic meals at least 8 times a year either straight from Go Picnic website or from Amazon because they are very convenient and generally healthy. I also recommend them for people with small children, because it's the perfect size for them. People ask me all the time at work where I get these meals from and I tell them.

Thank yo Go Picnic for trying to meet the needs of food allergic kids and adults.  I would like to see more dairy free options though.  I wouldn't recommend the salmon as too many kids with food allergies also have issues with fish like salmon.  Although my son can tolerate tuna, he cannot have the tuna meal due to a dairy allergy.  I'd love to help GoPicnic create more allergy friendly options.

I wouldn't recommend this to a celiac buyer. A few of the products had gluten in it. The sneaky 'this product may contain traces of wheat.' warning was on a number of them and I had a reaction after eating them. Mild but a celiac values staying completely off gluten as long as possible.Celiacs beware!

The Turkey Sticks and Pepperoni , and the Hummis are wonderful. However, I feed stray cats every morning at the high school where I teach and they walked, no ran, away from the Salmon and Tuna. This was after I tried each one and decided I could not consume either. The eleven feral cats confirmed the shock to my taste buds.

Tobin James is an excellent wine, and this one especially!  My husband and I have enjoyed a few Tobin James merlots.  It's difficult to find such good wine at such a reasonable price.  If you ever have a chance to go to the Tobin James tasting room in Paso Robles, I highly recommend it!  Cheers!
Simple and easy.  Try this on your roast chicken and you'll never go back to just salt and pepper again!  Especially good on rotisserie chicken!  Works great for skinless boneless check breasts also!

My wife got some of this to try a few weeks ago. She uses it on her steaks when she broils them. I use it on eggs and hamburgers to give them a bit of a flavor boost.The label says it has salt, dehydrated garlic, spices, dehydrated onion, dehydrated red bell peppers, and red pepper.It is not hot, but it does add a good amount of flavor to my food, so I have been using it pretty regularly.

We've been enjoying this seasoning on our steaks for some time, but this packaging is an great improvement. We first started buying it at a wholesale club where it was sold in a plastic grinder. The grinder was a pain in the wrist to use. I'm so glad that Weber now sells it pre-ground in a shake-on container. Plus, the grill-lid shaped cap is a cute touch. I definitely recommend this seasoning as it's just the right combination of flavors for a charcoal-grilled steak. I'd even use it on chicken or pork, as well.

If you like McCormick's Montreal Steak Seasoning, you'll love Weber's Chicago Steak Seasoning.  Bigger, bolder flavor than Montreal and it seasons perfectly.  I was a "purist" and didn't believe in steak seasoning but after trying Montreal, I was won over.  Then I received a sample of Weber's Chicago seasoning and I had to get to the web to get some more.
I love all the Weber Grill seasonings, but this is my favorite. It's amazing what it does to a steak on the grill.

Several years ago, I went on a tour of the Celestial Seasonings tea factory in Boulder, Colorado. The guide showed us the bales of tea as they arrived, machines that ground and mixed the tea, and a machine that put the tea in tea bags. The tour included a visit to the room where the peppermint tea was stored. Our guide told us that peppermint was stored separately so that it would not contaminate the other teas. He did not tell us what was to come.The doorway into the peppermint room was surrounded by bright red stripes. This should have served as a warning to us. We all innocently strolled into the peppermint room. The smell of peppermint was overpowering. It entered my nose, my head, my lungs, and then my whole being was infused with peppermint. What a rush! The crowd stampeded out of the room in a hurry. For the rest of the day and into the next, all I could smell and taste was the mint.I am now addicted to Celestial Seasonings Peppermint Tea. Every time I have some, I am reminded of that fateful day in Boulder. The events of that day have changed my life forever. Amazingly, the tea is still legal, openly sold in stores and on the Internet. I think that the tea is great, but then again I am not an unbiased observer. On your next visit to Boulder, take the tour. Or go a safer route; buy the tea from Amazon.

This chai latte tastes pretty good.  It tastes more like the kind of drink you get at the convenience store where you push the button and it makes a motor/whirring sound and hot water/mix comes out.  Starbucks, it is not, sheetz/wawa/7-11 crappuccino is more like it.Likes:Yummy chai flavorDislikes:more of an instant mix

We've bought this oil at least a dozen times at an Asian grocery, for $2.19 a bottle. It is absolutely ridiculous to pay approaching seven bucks for it here on Amazon. However, if you can find it cheaper (if you're lucky enough to have an Asian grocery in your town, look there), this is some delicious stuff! It smells and tastes incredible, and is our favorite oil for stir-frys.  Don't expect to get skinny cooking with it... but if you want some great scent & flavor, this delivers.

We've switched our dog to this brand of treats almost exclusively.So many of the treats available contain way too many ingredients, many of which are questionable.I like the fact that they are made in the US and contain at least 90% of what they claim to be.Our dog loves every Plato's treat we've tried.
The filet mignon of doggy treats. Healthy, wholesome, USA made. My dogs go nutso for them!

So these treats smell gross, but I've been able to win over shy and even semi feral foster dogs with these treats. All of the dogs LOVE this salmon! I use it as a treat whenever the dogs go into their crates and they will go sit in the crate staring at the salmon in hopes they might get some extra pieces. It's been wonderful to get foster dogs comfortable with crating because it is so high value, but it is not small enough to use for training. We divide each stick into 3-4 pieces and it lasts a while. Definitely recommend to anyone who wants to spoil their pups!

Breaking or cutting these jerky-like sticks into bite-size pieces allows the trainer to store them in a pocket to use them as rewards for learning a behavior.  They don't stain your pocket and almost all the dogs I work with enjoy them.  One tiny negative is the attempt to sell these treats as brain nourishing.  It was proven years ago that ginko blob had zero effect on the brains of mammals.I do, however, appreciate the fact that the treats are made in the USA as too many treats are made in China; and after the debacle with melamine killing our pets I buy nothing for any of my dogs that is not made here.

column9: These treats are great for training even the most wayward dog
column10: I have an english bulldog. Training my bully outside to not approach every dog without first being calm was often a challenge. I had tried to utilize numerous treats before with limited sucess at getting her to focus on my command. Plato's thinkers are not only made of great quality ingredients, but the smell and taste is something that most dogs find hard to resist. If you are looking for a great training treat I recommend these highly. Just break them up into small pieces either with a knife or by hand.These treats have not only worked with her, but with her fellow friends. I constantly refer folks to get this type of treat, when they are looking for a good training treat. And all my friends who have purchased this for their dogs are happy with their purchase.The larger 24 oz jar is the best because they last longer and the lid prevents them from air exposure which otherwise makese these treats hard.
We continue to purchase these over and over again because our dog just loves them.  We usually split them in half for a quick treat.  At 60 lbs, he loves to get a full length one.  Highly recommend!

My dogs love these treats and all of them know the word "Thinkers" now. Plus, the ingredients are simple and clean--these things don't seem like they've been heavily processed.With all the bad press about dog treats and dogs becoming ill, I'm really careful what I give my dogs as treats and these treats are worth the extra money. I mix them in with their other natural treat, carrots, but they definitely like these better.The only bad thing is be forewarned--these things really smell. Must be why the dogs go crazy when the box arrives, with their keen noses they can probably smell them through the box.

Esther loved them, but they're way too big for all but the largest of dogs.  Breaking these at any point in the stick will lead to a mess.  It's like a pepperoni skin on the outside, but like dried fish pulp on the inside.  So, cutting or breaking will lead to dried fish powder in one hand and the outside of the treat in the other.  Again, Esther loved them, but it's a one size serving - period.

column9: My dog loves these, and they used to be great but...
column10: My dog loves these, and they used to be great but the last batch we got were limp and stale. When I try to break them, they bend instead of snap like they usually do. And when finally after a lot of fighting, I could get it to break (really more by having to rip them), the result was a big crumbly mess. Usually I would go through a jar of these rather quickly. Needless to say, this last jar I bought has been sitting here for a few months, because it's such a pain in the butt to deal with. He still loves them, but I don't feel like having to clean up a mess every time he has some, and I also don't like the thought of giving my dog something that's not fresh. Makes me skeptical to purchase again, because they aren't cheap and Amazon does not let you return food items. So now, instead I just stick to the Plato Chicken Strip Cookies that come in the bag. He loves those too. They are highly palatable, and I love the fact that plato's treats have very few, clean simple ingredients since my dog has had allergy issues in the past. The sticks were just a nice change from the regular old crunchy cookie that most snacks are (the shape and texture and all) but oh well, too bad!
My dogs love Salmon and its great for their skin. These treats are perfect for the two of them. I like to split the stick in two so they last longer because they like them that much.

Don't like the salmon, the smell of fish is to strong and crumbles that my dogs have to eat it outside.  They like the chicken but can not have do to allergic to poultry. I have not seen beef or veggie sticks by Thinkers.
Our dogs just love the Plato Thinkers.  They are good food and treats for our dogs.  We buy them regularly.  They were fresh.  They were just as the dogs like them.  They are their favorites.

We have two hound mixes, and they just love these. I think they are a little big for each girl to have one, so we break the stick in half for them. It helps them last a little longer as well since they are a bit pricey, but totally worth it. It takes a little coaxing to get them to take the salmon flavored sticks, but they love the duck and chicken.
great product.  made in the usa.  the sticks are long but can be easily broken up into smaller pieces for little dogs.

After the dire warnings about pets getting sick and/or dying from jerky treats from China, I had a very difficult time finding ANY dog treats made in the USA.  Yeah, they're more expensive, but my dog is worth it.  These are good, not her favorite, but she loves them all the same.

From a dog perspective, these treats are some of the best.  From a person's perspective, they are some of the most aromatic. Not sure if they improve my dog's thinking, but she will do amazing things when bribed with one of these.
My soon to be 12 year old Maltese, Alexandra adores these treats.  They are a bit pricey, but she deserves them.  I break them in half and she is delighted everytime I give it to her!
My little seven pound pomeranian found these too big to eat - and even when I cut them he was not interested.

Suzie my Westie likes these OK... but definitely not her favorite treat.  The ingredient list looks good.... but she goes more for the freeze dried liver and fish snacks.  She does like these a lot better than the salmon sticks made by the same company though, even though in general she likes fish more than chicken.

Suzie (my 3 year old Westie) loves fish, and especially salmon, so I thought she would go wild for these.  But surprisingly, she has no interest.  She tried one, but since then did not even want to eat them again.  They stink like crazy, which should be a further indication that she'd go for them, but...  sad to say....  no interest.  I am not sure why, the ingredient list looks great.... maybe its a fluke so I am not going to say this is a bad product.  But.....

I just ordered this product and from what I can tell, its not organic chicken. It doesn't say organic on the packaging or in the ingredients list.NOT ORGANIC: The reason I purchased this product is because I thought it would be organic. It is important to me to feed my dogs foods that aren't pumped with hormones and preservatives. Additionally, I choose organic as a animal lover in the hopes that animals raised to be organic are typically given a better quality of life.GARLIC IS AN INGREDIENT: Look at any "Toxic to Dogs" food list, and you find garlic on that list. The toxic level for a dog is large; however I have no idea how much garlic is in these treats. I was looking for something that I could feed my dogs on a regular basis as a training reward...and I can't do that in good conscience not knowing the long term effects of regulary ingestion of the garlic in these treats.Only good note is that my dogs do love these treats, but they also love all kinds of other treats that I as their human care taker know better than to give them.

column9: Not designed as a training treat
column10: I just received my order of Plato's Thinkers Salmon Sticks Dog Treats in the mail and immediately tried them out on my dog. Unfortunately the product is not what I expected. I train my Labrador in competitive obedience and agility and need a treat that can be given to the dog in small pieces to keep her interested and alert in repetitive training exercises. However, the Plato's Thinkers Salmon Sticks Dog Treats are not really designed as a training treat. The sticks cannot be broken or cut into smaller pieces without crumbling apart. The sticks have an outer smooth skin that holds the inner salmon ingredients together but it falls apart when cut or broken and the inner ingredients crumble out. I bought these thinking they would be like the salmon strips product that a fellow trainer shared with me at our last dog agility class which could be broken into small pieces. Unfortunately the salmon sticks are not the same product as the salmon strips.The ingredients may be great and my Lab does like the product, but the sticks are not for serious dog trainers. Get the strips instead if you want to be able to break the treats into smaller pieces - a real necessity for repetitive exercise dog training.

The smell is just to die for! Using it to make my own lotions. Well worth the money. However, I wish there would be a "fair trade" product. If I'd find fair trade cocoa butter, I'd order it in no time!
We love this old fashioned candy and as good as I remember. We received it quickly and in good condition from this distributor.

Great value. I was able to stuff little treat bags with these for my family. Everyone loves Reese's :) I would recommend this product.

column9: If You Need To Splurge, Do It With This!
column10: This is my second time purchasing this product.  It arrives in a styrofoam lined box, swathed with ice packs, which I save for later use, wrapped in plastic in a tin that couldn't leak if it wanted to.  The lid is a bit difficult to get off, but that shows you the delicate eggs are protected. Unlike a lot of other British staples, Twiglets are pretty hard to find in grocery stores in my area, so I'm very glad to see they're available on Amazon. They're the perfect salty, savory, flavor-filled snack and there's nothing quite like them. If you've never tried a Twiglet but happen to know what Marmite tastes like, well: Twiglets are basically crunchy little whole-wheat sticks that are coated in something that tastes very much like Marmite, although they're not actually Marmite-branded and aren't made by the same company. If you know anything about Marmite, you will know that opinions on the stuff are very polarized - you either love it or hate it, and the same goes for Twiglets. You will either think these are to die for, or your taste buds will recoil in horror at the flavor. If the idea of a tangy, salty, crunchy, savory snack appeals to you, I would highly recommend giving these a try for something a bit different.

column10: This is by far the most enjoyable K-cup coffee I have tried so far. Even a large cup tastes great, not diluted. I will certainly continue to buy this brand. Got a great price as well.

Got these extracts for baking and smoothies to add variety in flavor. I put 1/2 capful in Crystal Light Orange and it was way yummy. This is great for those who are calorie conscious or going for a low glycemic way of eating since these extracts create a taste treat without doing damage.
it taste really good as long as you don't use too much of it..if you do its really over powering

I like how thick this sauce is, it really sticks to the meat. I use primarily on chicken, but also like to make pulled pork if I have some leftover tenderloin and cook some cocktail wieners in it for parties.

Sweet, yet tangy, this award-winning sauce is sure to win the taste test with your family.  My grandkids wouldn't touch the brand my daughter brought home from the store after finishing my bottle of Sweet Baby Ray's. Very good barbecue sauce, very tasty and at the same time nothing extra in it, so it just add very good flavor to the meat.
Received in a very timely manner thru Amazon.com.  This is one of my favorite rib sauces. Too much is just enough.

column9: Great packaging of this popular and tasty sweetening agent.
column10: We have tried many sweeteners and find that Aspartame tastes the most appealing to our palates.  In fact, we find it to have more of the basic taste of sugar than natural sugar has. I am not being oxymoronically facetious but, rather, referring the lack of the slightly bitter and sour undertones in natural sugar - as well as less of the many divergent and distracting flavours that raw sugar contains.  We don't want flavour in our sweetener when it is purpose is as a neutral elevator of sweetness.As you may know, Aspartame is delivered to the market as Equal, NutraSweet, Canderel and under its generic name of Aspartame to the food industry (e.g., as used in Diet Pepsi).  We feel its inclusion in diet drinks, particularly, seems rather natural.  We also tried Splenda since it was purported to be usable at baking temeratures but found it to taste very unnatural, even distasteful. We need to do more research but our 1st impressions of the so-called modern-ancient alternatives like Truia, Stevia, et al, may be hindered by their emulating natural cane sugar too well and, as such, inheriting its negative attributes.We find the packaging of Equal in the 4 ounce "spoonful size" bottles is simply great.  You leave it on the counter and take as much as we need as we need it: quart, half, flat, heaping teaspoons or any other amount as needed.  We find all other forms, like bags or pills, an insult to our intelligence.  We are not Lemmings who only do as directed.  We use the specific amount of sweetener to set the sweetness of the food to the specific level that we desire on a case-by-case basis. E.g., a strong coffee will require more, a week coffee, less, and Dunkin Donuts caffeinated water the least.When I make my wife's coffee in the AM, I add a little, sip-test the taste, add a tad more, until it is just right.  Equal in the spoonful bottle allows me to do just that.  Using the bag format is ridiculous.  When my daughter bought some, we ended up with partially filled bags on the counter.  You literally waste 20%-30% of your product that way and are thus hurting Gaia.We never did like the fouler tasting and toxic alternatives like Cyclamates (now banned) and the carcinogen, Saccharin (still available).  There are various anecdotal reports of potential health issues with Aspartame but nothing conclusive after a great number of studies in the last decade around the world.  When it is shown to be more harmful than the toxic aspects of natural sugar, we'll be the first to stop its use.  We refer to natural sugar's diabetic, cardiac, migraine, immune system, CFIDS, and countless other related issues.  And, yes, also not conclusively proven.  We just know from persnal experience.  Yes, Martha, everything has issues, including you.Our only negative sentiment is that the granulated 4 ounce "spoonful" bottles are not as readily stocked as the highly wasteful, inefficient, and environmentally taxing bag format.  Yes, Mable, everything is a burden on our environment, especially you.  Aspartame is also not suitable in acidic foods or those heated to cooking temperature as it hydrolyzes (breaks down) and loses its subjective sweetness.There is also a smaller 2 ounce bottle but we find the 4 ounce is a better value, fits on the counter just fine, and is less destructive to the environment as it defecates less plastic into the environment.  We'd strongly prefer it be sold in a lined paper box so it will biodegrade much better than terrible plastic.So, until we manage to avoid sweetening altogther and until there are subtantive reports to its toxicity, we're happy with the sweetener, Equal.

Love this cracker! It replaces saltines. This is a gluten free cracker that actually tastes good. I serve it with soups, stews, dips, cheeses.  Also good for crumbling over casseroles and crushing in recipes like meatloaf.

I love Taco Bell so I knew I would love this sauce.  I have used it on chicken, veggies, baked potatoes and most recently, I put it on my mashed potatoes.  You can use this in many ways, salads, meats etc.The taste is creamy, rich and spicy but not too spicy.  it has a little kick to it and if you like jalapenos, then you will like this.  I am not a big fan of alot of spices and when I cook, I really cook plain but I do like this product.  It's not too much and not too little.If you want to add a little zest to your every day meals, this is a good way to go.*************************************THIS IS AN UPDATE, 2 WEEKS LATEROk, for me, this sauce is not too spicy, however, I served it 2 times to company.  One time I used it as a dipping sauce for veggies and another time, I used it for a topping on taco night in my house.  Both times, my friends and family said it was too spicy for them.  I personally like a kick but they all found it too spicy but they loved, loved the taste, it was just too spicy.  One of my friends actually started coughing and asked for a glass of water. However, it may be too spicy for those of you not used to it..but it tastes great.

column9: Delicious with a hint of spice
column10: This is another of Taco Bell's sauces that I am enjoying. It's just a hint spicy, but full of flavor (though not necessarily bold). I use it as an alternative to mayo on my sandwiches. I recently switched over to lite mayo which I absolutely detest, but I just can't justify the calories and fat in real mayo. That's where this comes in. Each 1 tbsp is 55 calories and less than 1 gm of fat as compared to lite mayo which is 35 calories and 3.5 gm of fat per 1 tbsp. The sauce has slightly more calories, but is well worth the switch. It's delicious, adds a touch of spice to my sandwich and almost reminds of those gourmet type sauces like those added to certain sub sandwiches from a well known chain. I also like it on fajitas, tacos and other traditional Mexican food. I read in another review that it was nice on a lite salad, so I tried that also, and yes, I agree totally, it's a very nice dressing for such. So, all in all, I'm impressed with these Taco Bell sauces (including the Chipotle flavor) and would recommend you at least give it a try.

column9: Spicy, liked it as a dip
column10: This sauce is quite kicky, but I'm used to milder sauces, anyway, and tend to opt on the mild side. I love jalapenos, however, and you can definitely taste them here. I'm trying this sauce with pretzels, as a dip, and it's very flavorful. I see that there's spinach and parsley here, as well as the red and green bell peppers. There's a hint of cheese. Tasting lots of stuff. It's very creamy. That creaminess has a drawback, of course -- a serving of two tablespoons has 110 calories. But overall, it's nice, and I'll try it with some cooking, too.

column9: not bold, but my teenager LOVES this stuff
column10: I got this for my husband and teenager, who are both big fans of anything jalapeno. My husband was disappointed and pronounced it "just ok". He thought putting cheese in it hurt the taste, and they both said it wasn't at all spicy. My teenager initially thought it was just ok too, but then he decided he LOVES it and has almost finished the bottle already. He put it on a chicken burger last night and dipped his carrots in it, then practically licked the plate. My husband will stick with the Naturally Fresh jalapeno ranch dressing, but Joey is happy with the Taco Bell sauce and put it on the shopping list himself!

This is a sauce that was a big hit in the family.  We have used it on sandwiches, as a dip/sauce for chicken nuggets, and as a sort of marinade.  It has a nice delayed kick.  It works well with many different foods--in a pinch we used it as a dip for veggies and chips.  Very versatile.

column9: strong vinegar taste with a little hot pepper and spicy tang
column10: Taco Bell's Bold and Creamy Jalapeno Sauce's taste was very unappealing to me.  I also didn't like the color of the product.  It doesn't look appetizing.  It has a strong vinegar taste with a little hot pepper and spicy tang.  I really didn't like it, and I usually really like hot and spicy foods.  They also sent me a bottle that had already expired--gross.

column4: Jeff Wignall "The Joy of Digital Photography"
column9: I'm using it as a salad dressing--it's great
column10: Funny to read the reviews of this with some reviewers saying it's not spicy enough, others saying too spicy. I'm sort of in the middle--it seems fine to me but it does have enough of a bite to make it interesting. I think most people will use this as a taco sauce (and I have to tell you, I'm not a Taco Bell restaurant fan, blehhh), but when it arrived I happened to be slicing up tomatoes for a salad, so I just plunked some on and used it as a dressing--and I loved it. Has a very different flavor and the next night I found myself craving it again. So, all week it's been tomatoes, cukes and jalapeno sauce. Not bad.My one complaint about *all* dressings like this is that the jar is too small. C'mon, it can't cost more than a few pennies to make this stuff--all the cost comes from packaging and shipping--so why not make it at least 12-ounces or even more. Again, that goes for all sauces like this, and all salad dressings.By the way, if you have a lactose intolerance (as I do), read the label: this contains whey from milk and other dairy products. I wish that lactose was listed on all labels.Live long and prosper.

column9: Doesn't taste bad but isn't very hot at all
column10: This sauce is like a spicy ranch dipping sauce. It doesn't taste bad but it isn't very hot at all. I was expecting a sauce that was hot but it just didn't deliver. It is good to put on tacos or burritos from time to time but not something that I would use all the time.

column9: An OK condiment if used sparingly
column10: Again, I'm disappointed with the new Taco Bell creamy sauces. I first tried the ranchero sauce, which was not good at all. This sauce, the creamy Jalapeño sauce, is slightly better but the taste is still not that impressive. For one thing, the jalapeño flavoring is quite mild and I prefer a much spicier kick to my food. The best way I can describe the taste is "manufactured". It does not taste like freshly made sauce. Too much of the sauce is overwhelming, not because of the spicy factor, but just because the bottled taste would ruin good mexican food made with fresh ingredients. I'm not against Taco Bell brand  I love their canned refried beans and their original bottled hot sauce). These creamy sauces, however, have not impressed me at all.

I'm a big jalapeno fan, so maybe it's just because I'm disappointed by the mild taste, but to me, this tastes exactly like a sour cream dip one might scoup up with a potato chip. It is not spicy. To taste the "jalapeno" you will need a very vivid imagination.Is it gross? No, I think the sauce is okay overall, and I'm sure I'll find some food to match well with it, but when you get something called "bold jalapeno sauce"  you don't expect to be getting the world's mildest sour cream. Overall> not gross, but not a "bold" original flavor either. And it is NOT "jalapeno", so if you're looking to actually try something spicy - run away from this rip off.

When it has came down to Taco Bell, they have honestly made some great Mexican foods and seasonings to make our food  abit more spicy. But very rarely, there can be a time where they have a food on the maket that isn't as spicy as it could've been. That is the case with their Bold & Creamy Jalapeno Sauce. The sauce didn't taste so bad, but honestly I was hoping for a bit more spice and tanginess to the flavor of the sauce. I have honestly tasted their Spicy Ranchero sauce, and that was much more zestier. It isn't bad, but if you are a huge fan of Taco Bell, I would definitely recommend a much hotter sauce for your Jalapeno spiced needs.Price: CTaste: B-Overall: C+

This Taco Bell Jalapeno Sauce is pretty good, especially if you're a huge taco Bell fan and want to recreate the taste at home.Though it is labeled as 'Creamy and Bold', it is creamy, but not what I would call bold. It's pretty mild flavored. We liked it on (another fast food chain's!) chicken pieces!It's also good as a taco salad topping instead of dressing. We love to make our own taco salads, and none of us are fans of most bottled dressing, and this was actually nice.If you want bolder, try the Taco Bell Chipotle Sauce.

I was hoping this would be the infamous, well to me infamous, baha sauce I get with my Cheesy Gordita Crunches, but when I tried it, it tasted like a ranch sauce that is overpowered with jalapenos. If you like creamy jalapenos with a hint of a ranch taste, then this is the product for you. Not so much for me though.

This is another product that I would not normally pick up to try but am glad I did! This jalpeno sauce is just the right mix of a ranch-type dressing with a little kick added to it. This was great with some homemade mexican food, but would also be very good and fun with a veggie plate for a summer snack. It might be a bit spicy for kids, but adults will love it. Yum!

Taco Bell Jalapeno Sauce is versatile.  Use it as a dressing for salads, a dipping sauce for fish or chicken or as as sandwich topping.  Great on a mesquite smoked turkey sandwich...adds a little zip!  Great flavor.  Not extremely spicy.

column4: DB "Been around for a few years now"
column9: Like it better as a salad dressing
column10: We found the sauce a little on the light side as a taco sauce, you have to use a lot to taste it with the other things on the taco.  Like it a lot better as a salad dressing because the flavor stands out more.  Recommended as a salad dressing with a smaller recommendation as a taco sauce.  If you like this as a salad dressing let me recommend Marie's Jalapeno Ranch, our favorite salad dressing.
This is pretty hot.  It's not the hottest sauce I've had.  You can use it on almost anything that you eat, including taco's, burritos, sandwiches etc.

column9: Not The Best Of The Taco Bell Lineup
column10: Yeah, Taco Bell isn't exactly associated with healthy living. While it may say Taco Bell on the label the sauces are actually manufactured by Kraft Foods. They pay Taco Bell to slap their name on the label and voila you get a more recognizable brand. The sauce is not my favorite of the three I sampled. It's just really a processed taste almost like cheese sauce. The other ones actually have a more bold flavor but this one not so much.

This is all right. I didn't love it, but other members of my family did.  It does taste good on tacos, but it's not anything I would use a whole lot.  The flavor is pretty nice and spicy, though I'm pretty weak when it comes to spices.  Overall, adds a nice zing to your meals without being too overpowering.

This sauce was a nice addition to our Mexican meal the other night.  We used it on soft tacos, hard tacos, and nachos.  It added a nice creamy flavor with just a touch of spice.  It might even be good used as a salad dressing.I received my bottle of this sauce for free via The Amazon Vine program in exchange for my honest review.

I'm indifferent about this sauce. It doesn't taste bad, per se, but I tend to have enough "saucy" things on my Mexican food -- sour cream, salsa, taco sauce -- that one more just makes it messy. This will never replace a good helping of sliced jalapenos.
This can be used on any food or snack that needs a little extra zip. Great on tacos, tostados,and burritos too.

column4: Tracy Foote "College Savings Plan Author, Pho...
column10: The whole family favored this flavor ove the Chipolte one. They both are very creamy. I didn't care for either on beef, but I really enjoyed it on chicken - either on a chicken taco or a chicken sandwich. The sauce does have some kick, but if you like spicey treats, this probably will rate 'medium' for you as far as a level of hotness. I think people who normally stay away from spicey items would actually enjoy trying this. This could easily become a normal household purchase for us.

MMmmmmmmm.....mmmmmmmm; love this Taco Bell Jalapeno sauce. It adds just the right amount of spice. I used it in place of salsa and there was no need for sour cream since the jalapeno sauce is rich and creamy.

I'm not a real big sauce person, but once in a while, I like to try something different (especially if it might have a little spicy nature to it).  So, when I got the chance to try the Taco Bell Jalapeno Sauce, I thought, jalapenos may have a bit of a zing; lets try it.  Well, although the sauce is tasty and creamy, there is very little zing (hence the 4 stars).  Even my 3 year old liked it and she does not like anything spicy. This sauce wasn't my favorite on Tacos, but I did like dipping carrots and celery into it as a little snack.  Cant wait to see what else we use it for.

This Taco Bell Jalapeno sauce was a disappointment too me. With the "Bold" title I expected a spicy jalapeno sauce perhaps cut with a dairy product too make it creamy and palatable too the general public. So not very spicy as I would love. This was more of a buttermilk dressing with just a hint of Jalapeno flavor. I have used it on burritos and as a dip; it works better as a dip. There is no question that if you like the flavor of a good Jalapeno this will disappoint you.As their other 'Bold & Creamy' products two tablespoons of this sauce contains 100 calories from fat and a total of 110 calories per serving size. The serving size is the aforementioned two tablespoons. It taste OK just be aware of its high fat content and calories. When serving size is measured by the spoon full you know the calories are high. I would not seek too purchase this product but would use it again. 3(1/2) Stars.

Okay so I really didn't have high hopes for this product but actually found many uses for it.Let's start with the flavor: it is creamy, very mild but has a nice hint of jalapeno along with garlic and onion...typical Mex style flavor.  It's nice but not epically good and surely not good for you.USES:1. Sandwiches2. *Pizza Sauce: dough, Jalapeño sauce, Mozzarella &/or Pepper Jack Cheese, spicy sausage, onion slivers & bell pep.3. Salad Dressing4. Taco Salad Dressing5. Burger/Turkey Burger Sauce6. Dip for fries7. Sauce over baked potatoesI am on my second bottle since I found so many uses for this sauce and my not so spicy tongued hubby likes it.  It's a nice change, a little spice for life! :)

column9: Rich sauce, a little kick to it, but rather timid
column10: I gave if 4 stars because it's a jalapeno sauce, yet the spicy level is really weak. I wasn't looking for a mouth-on-fire experience, but if they're going to put "jalapeno" on the label, it should at least have an OK amount of heat in there. You won't find much of that in this sauce. That being said, I tried this on a lot of different items, and frankly it tastes good on almost everything. Hamburgers, chicken nuggets, and of course tex-mex foods like taquitos and quesadillas. It's a creamy somewhat thick sauce, so be prepared if you were expecting a thinner style. I'd recommend it, but then again I'm not a real sauce snob (is there such a thing?) It was a surprise though, as I've never had any Taco Bell item with this type of sauce on it that I can recall. Whatever they're putting it on, I'll bet it's pretty tasty!

These sauces are light and have a spicy edge.  They mix well with meats, Mexican food, veggies, and some of them are good in salads.  They are liquid, so blend well with other foods. Jalapeno is the lightest, Spicy Ranchero is like the original Taco Bell Hot Sauce Flavor the most. It goes well as a salad dressing if applied sparingly.  The Chipotle one is the most mellow one, all with a bite.  I will definitely buy again.Taco Bell has outdone themselves.

Taco Bell Jalapeno Sauce is delicious! It is not a tomato based sauce but a creamy, just spicy enough sauce that can be used on a variety of dishes. I first tried it on a sandwich made with chicken, tomato and avocado. It lends a piquant flavor without being too spicy. I tried it on shrimp tacos, chicken and cheese burritos, and finally as a salad dressing on a salad that included corn and black beans. I haven't found anything that isn't improved by its spicy magic. This product will become a staple in my house!

I was pleasantly surprised by the taste of the Jalapeno Sauce.  It is kind-of like a spicy mayonnaise.  I used this sauce in tuna salad, on sandwiches and as a salad dressing.Similar to mayo, almost all of the calories come from fat.  I think it is tastier than mayo and has a nice amount of spice.  You can taste the pepper in the sauce but it doesn't leave your mouth burning.  It's a good balance of flavors.Even if you're not a big Taco Bell fan, this sauce is actually pretty good.

I thought I would like this, since I love jalapeno and spicy stuff, but this just didn't taste good to me.  It's almost like a mayonnaise with a very tart, vinegar flavor and a faint cheese flavor.  It's also not very spicy at all.  Note:  This product contains eggs.

We used this sauce in the place of mayonnaise on a chicken sandwich and it was absolutely yummy.  About the same fat content of regular Mayo you get quite a zest.I am accustomed to spicy hot ... so this was not very intense for me.  However, if you are not accustomed to Jalapeno peppers or hotter, just prepare yourself.  Better to expect something hotter than it is and adjust accordingly.We found this to be delicious, spicy, zesty, cool ... Yummy.  I wonder why it caries the Taco Bell restaurant name but have never seen this in the restaurants?  A delicious addition to a taco, sandwich or whatever.  Be creative, this is a yummy sauce.As with sauces in this genre, completely processed -- but oh so good anyway!

column9: Okay, But Better Sauces Are Out There
column10: Sure this sauce tastes like jalepeno and is slightly spicey, but mostly this is just like other flavored ranch dressings.  This is similar to a salad dressing you could find for the same price and in a bottle twice as big.  My suggestion - try this and then decide, but I prefer many of the brands you will find in the salad dressing & veggie dip sections of your grocery store.  Those from other brands are bolder and packaged for better pricing.  I would consider this more of a novelty driven by the brand name Taco Bell.  This product will most likely be located near the taco kits & canned mexican food, but try shopping in the salad dressing & veggie dip section - you will find more variety for your money.

column9: More like a salad dressing than a taco sauce
column10: I was so hoping this would have a little kick to it - it doesn't. I was hoping it would have the flavor of jalepeno - it doesn't. I was hoping it would add a bit of spice as a dipping sauce for chips - it doesn't. What it does do is resemble a creamy, ranch type salad dressing. The flavor is so mild (almost nonexistant) that it added nothing at all to a taco or even as a dip with an avacado. It was just so bland and soft that all I could think of was salad. There is no heat here at all by the way! So.... it tastes fine if you aren't really expecting much. If you're from Texas and the Mexico border and accustomed to eating fresh jalepenos with your meals, then this sauce will leave you disappointed and possibly disgusted. If you want a slightly different ranch type dressing to a bowl of lettuce then this stuff isn't bad.

column9: Creamy with right amount of spice
column10: This is a good sauce for tacos, fajitas, or any tex mex recipe you may have. The sauce adds a nice spicy creaminess to your favorite dishes, with the right amount of spice. The sauce isn't too salty as a lot of pre packaged sauces are. This is pretty darned tasty.

column9: Very mild but a unique flavor
column10: It's hard to explain what this tastes like. Sort of a buttermilk ranch dressing with just a hint of Jalapeno.It is by no means hot. A 5 year old would not think this is hot. I've tried it on a few different things.I've used it on homemade burgers, Tacos and wraps and it adds a distinct...zing.I had it on catfish tacos last night and loved it. So far I've used it on fish, beef and chicken with great results.I would consider it a guilty pleasure. Sure it isn't the healthiest sauce around. It is high in calories.Used in moderation I don't think it is that bad.

According to the label this is a "bold & creamy jalapeno sauce".  I then expected a hot sauce that would grab my attention.  The flavor is ok but frankly it's neither as hot nor as bold as I'd expect from a jalapeno sauce.  My bigger issue though is the fat content.  110 calories per serving is ok but 100 of those calories are from fat and there are 11g of fat in a 2 Tbsp serving.  The fat content is way too high for me to use this sauce consistently.  And for anyone looking for a true hot sauce this one just doesn't deliver.

A pleasant surprise. Was expecting a real Jalapeno hot flavor, but could easily handle the rather sweet and mild taste. Rate it great for its diverse uses. Love it on various food items, but french fries are my favorite. It's add some zest to your favorite dip items and  chips.

This is a great sauce; it is creamy, spicy, cheesy, and right amount of salt. It is not too hot, but just about right. It is recommended for tacos, but I also used with my garden salad and tasted great. I highly recommend this product.1. La Victoria Mild Green Taco Sauce,15 -Ounce Plastic Bottles (Pack of 6)2. Ass Kickin' Kick Ass Jalapeno Hot Sauce, 18-Ounce Jars (Pack of 6)3. El Rio Regular Nacho Cheese Sauce with Jalapeno Peppers, 15-Ounce Units (Pack of 12)

column9: Yowsers, high fat but it is tasty
column10: This Taco Bell Jalapeno sauce is VERY good!  As for taste, it is excellent. But usually taco sauce is low or no fat but this is sauce is extremely fattening so I won't be buying it.  I believe for 2 tablespoons, it is 110 calories and 100 of those calories come from fat. That's so high! It has a buttermilk base so it has the texture and fat content of a buttermilk ranch salad dressing.  The nutritional value is a dealbreaker for me but if that's not important to you, then you'd love this sauce if you like spicy condiments.

column9: I Like It, I Like It!
column10: I was a bit skeptical trying a jalapeno sauce because I was afraid that all I would get is the burn but this sauce is downright awesome.  Just enough heat so you can still taste your food.  I've tried it on Mexican food but also on burgers and it was yummy!  I would even put this on a salad.  Calorie-wise, it isn't all that great but for 2 tbs. you get only 110 calories - the catch is 100 of those are fat calories.  But hey, fat tastes good.  Sodium's not too bad - 310 mg.  There's only 1 g. of sugar.  So if you want a little zest in your food, give this sauce a try.  It's going to be a regular in my pantry.  I can't wait to try the other Taco Bell sauces.

column9: A mild and creamy sauce that works well for many different types of food
column10: Breaking out of the standard tradition of salsa or hot sauce to use as a condiment on tacos and burritos, Taco Bell's latest super market addition is the "Bold and Creamy" line, which works for a variety of different meals.  Having the consistency of a creamy ranch dressing, with just a dab of jalapeno flavor and coloring, the sauce can just as easily work for salads and wraps as it can for any Mexican themed dinner.Of the different "Bold and Creamy" flavors currently available, the jalepeno version has the weakest flavor and is much more mild than might be expected for something with the word "bold" in the title.  It definitely won't make your tacos overly spicy, and seems to be more about adding a creamy sauce texture to Mexican foods rather than actually upping the heat.If you like your sauces more on the mild and creamy side, definitely give the jalepeno sauce a try. For those that want a stronger flavor, skip this one and pickup Taco Bell's Chipotle flavor instead.

I generally always have some sort of sauce on what i eat. Whether its hot sauce,bbq,mustard,ketchup. I've tried various other sauces so i wanted to try this one out as well. The best way i can classify this is as a spicy ranch sauce. It works well with salads, and adds a moderate amount of spiciness.Of course, like ranch sauces, it is not healthy so you really gotta keep track of how much you put. These sauces are a nice break from the regular stuff, but they really arent good enough (atleast for me) to become a regular.

column9: Good taste, but light Jalapeno flavor, not spicy
column10: We had tacos tonight and I tried out a couple new sauces from Taco Bell.  One of the sauces was the Bold & Creamy Jalapeno sauce.  I liked the sauce on the tacos, but would have liked it better if it were hotter with a stronger Jalapeno taste.  I like really hot and spicy food, so I found this pretty mild.  With that said, it had a good flavor and I liked it.I could see it being used on a variety of foods the same way you would use a ranch dressing.  The main ingredient is soybean oil and 100 of the 110 calories in a 2 Tbsp serving size are from fat, so this is not a diet or light dressing.Bottom line, I liked the taste, but would have liked it to have been hotter with more of a Jalapeno kick.  It is fattening, so don't load up on it.  For a light Jalapeno taste on top of your tacos or other dishes, it is a good sauce.

This is an ok sauce.  The sauce is creamy and a bit "tangy" in my opinion.  I did enjoy the sauce but I prefer regular hot sauce on my tacos.  You can put this sauce on your tacos, fajitas, pretty much anything you feel like.  It works better on tacos when there are vegetables in the taco.  I would buy a bottle to try first if you don't feel like committing to a case.  I can't find fault with it, just that it's not what I would choose first for my Mexican food.

This summer I have been experimenting with dipping sauces, mustards and barbeque sauces in my cooking and with my meals. As I added in Taco Bell's Jalepeno Sauce into my lineup, and I was pleasantly surprised.Really, Taco Bell jalepeno sauce is a creamy condiment with a kick. I like it with boneless wings and chicken nuggets as a dip. I think it would also be good for a little spice in a baked potato, or as a dip with potato chips. It is also good with its desired purpose, namely as a condiment to garnish with mexican foods such as tacos fajitas and burritos. The uses for this yummy sauce are actually quite diverse. I am eager to add it to my Subway sandwich in the near future.This sauce does have a little bit of the jalepeno spice, but I don't consider it that hot of a food. What is tasty is the flavor of jalepenos. If you are a consisuer of chilis and peppers like I am, you will love the authentically ddisticive peppery twist that Taco Bell offers with this fine food.Personally, I think Taco Bell would be wise to include a recipe in its packaging of this item, as it will be fun to figure out how many uses there are for this wonderful sauce.

This Taco Bell brand jalapeno flavored sauce is really good and creamy. Great on tacos, burritos or any type of food that requires sauce on it. Not too spicy, just a gentle flavor of jalapenos. I don't care for jalapenos, but this was really good. Thanks for sending this to me!

This sauce was better than I expected. I didnt think it was spicy but my 8 year old daughter did. Children's taste buds are more sensitive than ours and I do like spicy food so I guess it depends on your taste buds. We tried it on ground beef tacos w a tomato/jalapeno/cilantro mixture I make and on chicken soft tacos w bacon and sour cream. It was good on both but better w the chicken. The cilantro overpowered the sauce with my beef tacos. It was also good on taco salad, which I made from the leftovers. This sauce is similar to a jalapeno/ranch sauce they serve on salads in Chili's. This sauce is delicious but will not satisfy you if you are looking for something spicy.

I tried three Taco Bell flavors (chiplote, ranchero and the creamy jalepeno).  Of the three, this was my favorite by taste alone.  As it sits on your tongue, you sense a creamy smooth texture with a hint of hot.  I tried it in traditional tacos and it was good but the flavor got a little lost.  I preferred it in a taco salad as it had more vegetables and less taco meat with its own spicy flavor.  Also would be a good compliment on nachos in place of sour cream.

This is the spiciest of the Taco Bell sauces which I have tried, so use with caution.  It has a great jalapeno flavor and nice texture.  Not as thick as mayo, but more like a salad dressing.  Aside from the obvious uses with Mexican food, it works well as a hamburger topping and a sandwich spread (but it will tend to run off the sandwich).  The best use I have found is as a steak sauce.  Even leftover steak tastes amazing with this sauce!

Two things I would like to mention:1) It's not really hot. More like Jalapeno was sprinkled on top of this Sour Cream tasting sauce.2) As mentioned by a prior reviewer, it really doesn't go well with chips either.Beware, you have been warned.

column9: A Nice Addition To Most Mexican Food
column10: I had high hopes for this Taco Bell Jalapeno Sauce.  My family and I enjoy most Taco Bell products; both from the restaurant and the in-store products.  I love their Fire Sauce, and wish they sold it in bottle form at the grocery store.  So when I saw this new Taco Bell Bold & Creamy Jalapeno Sauce, I was excited to try it.  I really enjoy just about anything spicy, so my hopes and expectations were high.  Now that I have tried this sauce, I am somewhat disappointed yet find it to be a good addition to most Mexican foods that I enjoy.The name of the product clearly states "Bold & Creamy."  I agree with the creamy aspect of their claim, but feel that the word bold should be changed to something less aggressive, like tangy.  You definitely detect notes of Jalapeno peppers in the sauce, but it is quite subdued and has a somewhat artificial taste.  But I'm not bashing the product or saying that it isn't tasty.  I have found my favorite use of this product is with tacos and burritos.  I add a light amount of the Taco Bell Jalapeno Sauce to my soft and hard shell tacos, and then add generous amounts of Taco Bell Fire Sauce (I hoard packets of that stuff and always try to get as much of it as I can whenever I visit the Taco Bell drive-thru).  The Jalapeno sauce gives the tacos a bit of a sour cream flavor, while also added just a slight bit of Jalapeno kick.  I have tried this sauce with several other things from sandwiches to salads, and even a spicy chicken wrap.  While I didn't mind the sauce with the wrap, I didn't enjoy it at all with sandwiches and salads.Overall I will likely continue to purchase this product going forward, but I think a single bottle will last quite some time.  It doesn't have a good enough taste to stand on its own, as a dip or as a replacement for other sauces that I enjoy.  I don't find it to be nearly spicy enough, but I also understand that making it much more spicy would likely limit their sales to a more specific consumer market.  It is an above average product that is a solid compliment to some Mexican dishes, but I don't see this becoming a best seller among the Taco Bell brand name.  But I don't think the product is the type that most people will either love or hate.  It falls right in the middle, and I think most people will find it to be moderately satisfactory.  Go ahead and give it a try for yourself.  I suggest picking up a single bottle before buying a lot of 6, as they sell on this site, just to make sure you enjoy it enough to consider stocking up with that quantity.  I hope you enjoy it.  =o)

Describing food tastes is highly personal.Everyone has a different palate.The suggested uses for this sauce are tacos, Mexican salads and sandwich wraps. I tried it on a taco and found the taste too delicate to really appreciate.It isn't hot, which is fine. Somehow, I really found the flavor lost and had to taste it alone and it tastes like mayonnaise with spices and cheese.I would not call it "bold" at all.I prefer regular mayonnaise, again this is highly variable from palate to palate.I wasn't too happy with the ingredients. It appears as a very processed food.

column9: mild taste, great on ground beef
column10: I was pleasantly surprised at how good the Taco Bell Jalapeno Sauce was.  It's a creamy sauce, kind of like a thick ranch dressing.  It tastes a little like ranch too, tangier though.  There is very little jalapeno spice to the sauce, although there is some jalapeno flavor.  This reminds me a lot of the consistency and base flavor of the avocado sauce you can get on Taco Bell grilled steak soft tacos at the restaurant itself; in fact, if they made a bottled avocado sauce, they would have my undying love and affection forever.I tried this sauce on ground beef tacos in hard corn shells and it was good.  A little lettuce and monterey jack cheese made it better.  Personally, I didn't like it on tacos that also had salsa or chopped tomatoes.  The sauce is very good on soft flour shells.  I use it on soft tacos that I've warmed up with leftover refried beans and Spanish rice, and it's excellent.  While it's okay on chicken tacos, it's bold enough I prefer it on beef or beans, something with a stronger flavor.The 8-ounce bottle is about half the size of your usual ketchup or salad dressing bottle, and the bottle says a full ounce is a serving, but you can use a lot less.  I've used it at least 8 times and I'm not quite halfway through the bottle.  I will definitely buy this again and in other flavors.

When the Taco Bell "Bold and Creamy Jalapeno Sauce" first arrived, I had pretty low expectations, so it's safe to say that it suprised me. It has a texture more like Sour Cream than salsa, and it isn't super-spicy, but provides a bit of warmth to whatever you put it on. The most pronounced flavors seem to be cilantro and lime, even though neither one is listed on the ingredients label. It adds a nice depth of flavor to any burrito, taco, or even to an ordinary sandwich, and I think I'd order it if Taco Bell offered it in stores.

My family likes Taco Bell and we like this Jalapeno Sauce okay. We eat Mexican-ish style dishes quite a bit at home, so it's nice to have a bottled sauce for a little extra kick. I do like the jalepeno flavor in this particular sauce, but of course, not everyone has the same tastes. I also liked that it comes in a squeeze bottle with a flip lid with a small hole, rather than having to try to pour it out of the larger opening. That makes it convenient for adding just the amount you want. It can be used as a salad dressing, if you like thick dressings... or as a dipping sauce for tortilla chips, or on tacos, burritos, what-have-you.

Unlike other reviewers, I really liked the sauce. Yes, it's a little sweet, but I'm a big Jalapeno fan, so I think it's great. It's good to add to something like tacos or burritos, and you can tell it's a Taco Bell product. It's tastes similar to the other sauces that Taco Bell commonly puts on it's products. It's not something I would use everyday, but I would add to spice up a regular taco night!

column9: Not Bold, but maybe Somewhat Adventurous & Creamy
column10: Taco Bell has introduced a new line of three "Bold & Creamy" sauces. I decided the most straight-forward way to evaluate this sauce was to try it with some of Taco Bell's own products. I went to the local drive-through and picked up a couple of tacos and some chips.Trying this on tacos, I found it to be OK. There is a mild taste of jalapeno and the sauce is not at all unpleasant. To me, however, tacos are beef, cheese, and a little lettuce in a crisp corn shell with maybe a dollop of a red (or green) tomato- & chile-based sauce. Maybe that's because growing up in California in the 1950's and 60's, that's the only kind of taco you found at the family-owned restaurants that were here long before Taco Bell.This is not to say that Taco Bell Bold & Creamy Jalapeno Sauce is a bad product. I've tried it as a dipping sauce with vegetables and chips and as a dressing on a plain hamburger patty. Using as a dip, you get more of both the buttermilk and jalapeno flavors and are more likely to notice the mild (some would say very mild) heat. I also found it to be a nice change of pace from blue cheese, A-1, or Worcestershire sauce on my hamburger patty.All three of the "Bold & Creamy" sauces are based on soybean oil, water, vinegar, buttermilk,  and a few other standard ingredients.
