None of the cracker sheets I got had any visible perforations like the ones in the pictures. Not an issue for me, but if you need a smaller serving size, or perhaps for a party or an event, do take that into consideration. Nutrition-wise, they have 2g of fiber and 2g of protein per serving, 7g of sugars, and 130mg of sodium (5% RDA).[...]To summarize, these exceeded my expectations in terms of taste. I expected cardboard taste, but instead, I got something that I could eat even on its own - accompanied with some water or tea or something like that.

If you're thinking of the regular graham crackers of old, get that image out of your mind. First of all, these new crackers are much tastier. Second, they have a gritty texture that some may like and some may not, probably due to the oat flakes in them. Third, they hold up even better when you dip them into milk.Just remember, while these Golden Honey crackers are whole grain, they are not organic. Two full cracker sheets are 110 calories, not too bad if you can stop there. Now where's the peanut butter?

When I first got these, my wife tried one and her face lit up... she then proclaimed: "Oh, these are the best graham crackers ever!" A pretty resounding endorsement.These are made with all natural ingredients and are of great quality.  I now always get these to have available.I hadn't regularly eaten graham crackers for a long time, but I love Back to Nature's Golden Honey grahams.  I get them all the time!Nice crackers.

column9: Good on quality, not so good on the taste
column10: My whole family tried these Grahams as a snack with and with Coffee even my 2 year old.All of us liked it and the list of good quality ingredients make it even more attractive.  But the taste is not really up to the mark.We regularly buy Honey Grahams from Wal Mart (Great Value) brand and they are better in taste and decent ingredients (they do not contain any hydrogenated oils).Overall - it has very good quality ingredients and ok taste.

These graham crackers have that lovely and distinctive "digestive biscuit" or "sweetmeal biscuit" texture after a crisp crunch, a classic semi-sweet taste and a fantastic very dry feel in the mouth that wants to be enjoyed with tea or juice. They have a delicious warm flavor and a crisp fresh crunch, they lose so much if they are even a little bit stale so take care of them! The are dusted with whole oats, which makes them delicious in appearance but a little messy in practice. We just adored these in comparison to the overly sweet (and terribly American) high fructose corn syrup "cookies" that graham crackers tend to be. Highly recommended for a satisfying snack that's not too sweet. I imagine a pie crust made with these crumbs would be awe-inspiring. This is the good stuff!

column4: Megan Bostic "I am Creative Chaos. I may have...
column10: I really try to buy only whole grain, so I was happy to try and review these whole grain crackers. These are healthier than other graham crackers on the shelf, having been made with all natural ingredients.  The thing I like the most is that there are no hydrogenated oils.  It's so hard to find products these days without them, and they are so horrible for you.These crackers aren't as sweet as the graham crackers you're probably used to, but they're light and crunchy and very tasty.

Back to Nature grahams are among my favorite.  This "Honey Oat" version is not too sweet and maintains a good crunch, rather than the usual soft graham crackers.  Plus the shelf life is lengthy.  I also ate mine with some peanut butter and they tasted great. I think kids would like this product very much. Also great for a quick snack.

I really liked these -- I love graham crackers, and I actually like these better than the traditional Honey Made ones.The whole grain aspect doesn't take away at all from the taste.  I think it adds to it -- it somehow tastes hearty, but not dry and tasteless.Highly recommend!

column9: Prefer them to my "regular" graham cracker
column10: Graham crackers with a bit of peanut butter on them have always been a favorite snack of mine since I was small.  My mother often had that snack waiting for me when I came home from school.  I still will have that combination, along with a banana, for lunch from time to time.  When given the opportunity to try a new and different cracker, I jumped at the chance.After eating this product numerous times, I have to say that I strongly prefer the taste of this cracker to what I normally buy (the major force in the market).  The honey flavor is strong but not too strong and actually adds quite a bit when mixed with the peanut butter.  The honey flavor also makes this more appealing to me when eaten "naked" as a snack.  When you add in the better ingredients and the 100% whole grain, I doubt I will ever buy my traditional graham cracker again, except for use when making s'mores.I am a total convert to this product!

This is my second flavor of Back to Nature Graham crackers and I'm just as impressed with one as the first.  The crackers are simply crackling with flavor and crispiness.  There isn't much to say about graham crackers except that I've eaten all of the major brands for many years and these are the best of the them all.

Our boys LOVE graham crackers, but our youngest does not.  She hates to be left out, but the boys don't want to give up one of their favorite snacks.  The honey oat and cinnamon apple crackers satisfy all of our children.  Our youngest loves them!  I firmly believe she would eat the entire box, or make herself very uncomfortable trying.  These are great for school snacks, picnics, or just to have at the house.  Make sure to keep them sealed, as they seem to get "soggy" very quickly even in low humidity environments.  We will never again buy regular graham crackers!  These are a major improvement and we're sticking to 'em!

Back To Nature Golden Honey Oat Grahams definitely have better ingredients than the popular store bought graham crackers, but they do sacrifice some taste when compared to them. They do taste quite good considering most of the garbage that the average graham cracker contains has been removed. They're healthier too. The texture is a little drier and more brittle than most graham crackers. They also have less taste. I did enjoy them though, and if you're looking for a healthier snack, I would definitely recommend them.

One of my wife's favorite mid-day snack is graham crackers and milk.  Personally, I can take it or leave it but, when I saw "Back to Nature Golden Honey Oat Graham" on the VINE, I thought I'd make it possible for an expert to review the product.  She said that the graham crackers are very tasty and they go well with milk (a requirement for her).  She is conscientious about what she eats and enjoys the fact that Back to Nature IS healthy.  I asked her if she would pay more for "Back to Nature" than the regular brand and she said YES!

column9: Great Taste, Great Packaging, Great Quality
column10: No matter how "good for you" a product might be for me it means little unless the product tastes good.This is a great tasting product.  The cracker is a little bit dryer than standard graham crackers.  However it does not distract form taste or texture of the product.I can read the ingredient list and understand clearly what is in the product.While I am impressed with the taste and quality of the product I am even more so impressed with the packaging.  It is 100% recycled paperboard with a minimum of 55% post-consumer content).  The inks are from renewable sources.  The packaging has a clean / natural look without high gloss or loud colors.Impressed with the product and how the product is packaged!

* No artificial ingredients.  No food coloring.* No high fructose corn syrup.  It's sweetened with evaporated can juice, honey, brown rice syrup, apple juice concentrate, raise paste.* Contains cinnamon, which is believed to help prevent adult onset diabetes.* (BOTH the Apple Cinnamon version of this product, and the Golden Honey version, contain BOTH cinnamon and honey.)* Uses whole grain wheat flour, and whole grain rolled oats.  Whole grain contains more nutrients and fiber than does processed wheat.The taste is okay.  Pretty much like any other graham crackers.  So if you like graham crackers, and what a healthy kind, this would fit the bill.

This is what graham crackers are supposed to be when they grow up.  The texture is perfect, substantial and still crispy.  The actual honey comes through in the flavor profile - along with a hint of raisin and a hint of cinnamon.  Even the appearance is better than national-brands, with cute flecks of oat flakes in the dimpled golden brown crackers.  I was craving graham crackers and had just bought a package of Nabisco grahams, which have lost all appeal to me in comparison with these Back to Nature grahams.

I liked these a lot. They had just a touch of sweetness, not too much, and are a great afternoon or late night snack. I was pleasantly surprised that something that is supposed to be good for you tastes this good. The only reason I gave them four stars instead of five was because the packaging left something to be desired. It was hard to open the inside package without throwing crackers everywhere, and they don't seal back up for freshness. I put mine in a ziplock bag, though, and they stayed fresh that way. Try them, you'll like them!

Graham cracker fans looking for a natural product will probably appreciate these Back to Nature Golden Honey Oat Grahams.I see no strange chemicals listed in the ingredients list, and even the package is made of 100% recycled paperboard.Do I like these as much as the traditional Nabisco Grahams?  Well, not quite as much.  These seem to lack texture -- they're kind of smooth and bland, despite a few oat flecks clinging to the surface.Even the package itself is a little bland and old-fashioned-looking.  It would probably be hard to spot on a store shelf.I'm not sure what Nabisco Grahams are selling for these days, but these seem a little pricey to me at a little more than $3 for a 10-ounce box.  Of course, many things are seeming pricey to me these days, including most snacks except popcorn you pop yourself.So purists and nature lovers might want to try these, but Nabisco fans will probably prefer what they know and love...

This brand of graham crackers is decidedly less sweet than the other types that I have had over the years. I like this less sweet flavor and can see it being paired with toppings that might not go well with sweeter crackers. I also think that these crackers would make a lovely pie crust for those who prefer their desserts on the less-sweet side.

column9: Not too sweet and healthier than other grahams out there
column10: My two kids are graham cracker fanatics - with number of grahams being served in preschool and at relative's houses, I'm not surprised. Unfortunately, most graham crackers are chock full of unbleached flour, hydrogenated oil, high fructose corn syrup, and lots and lots of sugar.  In fact, many other brands first ingredients are unbleached flour, sugar, and riboflavin - graham flour doesn't even show up until the fourth or fifth ingredient.This is where Back to Nature Graham crackers got it right: Graham flour is the first ingredient.  There's no high fructose corn syrup or hydrogenated oil, and there are only whole grains included in this cracker.  In comparison to Honey Maid Crackers, there are less calories (-20), fat calories (-5), sugar (-1), and sodium (-30mg).  You also get +85mg of potassium per serving.  There are less crackers per box, however (4 full cracker sheets) in comparison to Honey Maid.In terms of taste and texture, I found the crackers to taste a lot less sweet than the graham crackers that I grew up with.  Initially, I found the crackers to be not sweet enough and lacking the crisp layer of sugar that most graham crackers have.  Upon eating the second cracker sheet, the missing sweetness wasn't a bad thing - instead of tasting just lots of sugar, I actually found that I enjoyed tasting the graham taste along with the oat taste.  The texture is a lot less crumbly than other graham crackers.  There are oats baked in, as well as some sprinkled on top.  The oats on top tend to come off, but is not too much of a problem because most of the oats are baked in; there are only a few sprinkled on top.  The oats may not be for everyone as you will definitely notice the added texture to the cracker.  I personally like having little bits in the crackers, however my husband found the oats to be annoying.  He doesn't care for the toppings on "everything" bagels either - so "people who don't like added nuts and seeds" beware!That said, I would probably suggest that if you haven't tried this graham crackers before to purchase a single box before buying a 6-pack of these crackers.  These graham crackers most likely taste nothing like the graham crackers that you grew up with.  Having been raised eating Honey Maids and Kraft Macaroni, I was pretty resistant to eating these crackers; however, I found the change to be welcome and am happy that my kids ended up liking 'em.  Recommended.

column9: Good tasting and Good for you
column10: So many times in the past I have tried natural products that turned out to be average tasting or even hardly edible.  Not these.  These taste good.  I can just barely tell the difference between them and regular Graham  Crackers.  These taste like they have more nutritional substance to them, including fiber.My daughter likes them, my grandchildren like them, and I like them.  In fact, a few minutes ago, I asked my grandson how he likes them, and he pulled out a package of from the box to nibble on while he watches TV.Always great when something good for you is actually a pleasure to eat too!  Also, like a lot of snack food. it's hard to quit eating them!Highly recommended.

column9: They're yum yum yummy in my tum tum tummy
column10: These are to graham crackers as are bran muffins to muffins...tasty, flavorful, bran muffins...mmmm.On the end of health:The first two ingredients for these crackers are whole grains. One of the great things about this for me (and for you if you eat them) is that these tasty snacks end up containing a healthy amount of Iron and Dietary Fibers (2g). Another added bonus is that I know (and can easily purchase) most of the ingredients listed on the side of the box. These are sweetened with evaporated cane juice (as opposed to corn) along with a few other seasonings and spices.On the end of taste:I really like the grainy texture of these crackers. There is a satisfying crunch when you chew them and a full mouth-feel experience in eating them. I kind of wonder what sort of magic they're doing with the sugar though as these taste like honey (you know... like the box says) but don't actually have any honey listed as any of the ingredients. My only guess is that perhaps they slightly burn the sugar (along with the aformentioned seasonings and spices) to achieve the taste.My wife loves these crackers, and she has had a variety of graham crackers to justify her experience. I love the value they add as a healthy and tasty snack. I don't think you'd go wrong in eating them yourself!

In the interest of full disclosure:  I am not employed by the Back to Nature Foods Company, nor am I related to anyone who is.  I have received no compensation for this review, other than a sample of the crackers.The first thing that impressed me is the business model.  This is not a 'pseudo' health food company; these folks are serious about offering a healthy product and protecting the environment at the same time.  The box is made from 100% recycled paper.  Right on!Enough about that--the crackers are delicious.  I think the last time I ate a graham cracker might have been when my grandkids--who are now teenagers--were tiny.  I bake my own bread so that I can control what's in it, so I approached these crackers from the viewpoint of a skeptic.  I loved them.  They are sweetened with cane juice and honey--no high fructose corn syrup!  There is a tiny bit of cinnamon, but just the right amount, and I love that they are made with whole grain.  I intended to eat one or two as a snack, but ended up crunching down about six of them with a cup of coffee, so be careful--they're addicting in the most exquisite way!  This is a truly great product.

Those are great tasting, not too dry, not too sweet, great texture Graham crackers. Compared to what's commonly found, they have no artificial preservatives, flavors, or colors, no HFCS, and no hydrogenated oils which are even worse. Even the box is made from 100% recycled material.  I just love them. Highly recommended.Nutrition facts:Serving size: 8 crackers (28g),Servings per container: about 10Calories: 110, 20 from fatTotal Fat: 2.5g (4%)Saturated fat: 0gTrans fat: 0gPolyunsaturated fat: 0gMonounsaturated fat: 1.5gCholesterol: 0mgSodium: 130mg (5%)Potassium: 85mg (2%)Total Carbohydrate: 21g (7%)Dietary fiber: 2g (8%)Sugars: 7gProtein: 2g

I really appreciated this fine sample. I could not tell the difference between this and the original graham crackers I have used for years. At least this one is all natural. Wish I could say the same for many of the other products on the shelf.

column9: The kids like them and that's what matters
column10: These crackers are made of all-natural ingredients, so that's probably good.  The kids all liked them and thought that they had a good flavor, although they said that they like regular graham crackers better.  These were a bit messier than the normal graham crackers that I am used to, as they have oats on them and they tended to fall off and make a bit of a mess.

The only complaint I have is that many of the crackers were broken, as another reviewer mentioned. Well, that is because they sent only one box in a bubble-wrap envelope. With all 6, you get a big box and they will probably, I hope, not be broken. Anyway, they are delicious!! I am very happy with the slight cinnamon and honey flavor, no sugar on top, and extra crunch! In my opinion, Nabisco's are a bit bland and they tend to break easier when you put cream cheese on them. Keebler are better, but these are the best! The price is higher than others, as you are only getting 10oz, but the ingredients are all natural and the sugar is evaporated cane juice, better for you than either white sugar or corn syrup.Ingredients: Graham flour, rolled oats, evap. cane juice, safflower oil, honey, raisin paste, brown rice syrup, baking soda and monocalcium phosphate (leavening), sea salt, cinnamon, vit E for freshness.That's real honey, real cinnamon. If you can afford to splurge on these, I would say do it. They stood up really well to cream cheese and strawberry jam, and probably with your favorite topping, too.And, I was happy to find that the box is 100% recycled materials. Good to show the kids what can be done with recycling.

Having always eaten the Honey Maid Graham Crackers... I was thrilled at being offered a more natural version to try.  I can sum up my experience in one word: Succulent! Wow!  What a great flavor!  You almost feel like you are eating a treat, and not a cracker!  So I took at a look at the ingredients and I was happy with what I found there too: all natural, simple ingredients (and ones that you KNOW what they are!).  If this is what a graham cracker is supposed to taste like, I've been jipped all these years!  I absolutely LOVE the oats in them too... it gives a nice crunch and I have to admit, I am a bit fan of oats in dry goods, so that definitely was a plus in my mind.The only thing I wish was better would be the price.  They are probably about 50% more expensive than the typical brands. But hey, who says I can't buy those "other" crackers for the kids (who could care less), and hide these on the top shelf for me?  :)

These fall squarely into my 'got to try them for free, and will actually actively look for them now' category of tasty foods.They're not excessively sweet, and at the same time they're not too 'healthy' tasting, if you know what I mean?  They are wholesome tasting, and with just enough sweetness.  They have a good crunch to them, not soggy at all, nor are they too dry.  They're a bit firmer than the grocery store grahams, so they don't crumble/crumb quite as easily.Short version: they're delicious!

column9: Best graham crackers I've ever had
column10: Oats are, apparently, what graham crackers have been missing all these years that made them so bland. While I wouldn't exactly call these "health food" because there is a rather significant amount of sugar in them, these are probably the healthiest graham crackers you'll find, made with whole grain flour and oats, and using no corn syrup derivatives (only sugar and honey) as sweetener. They are also, by far, the best tasting graham crackers I've ever had. As snacks go, this seems like a great choice.

I received a 10-ounce box of these crackers through the Vine review program. The crackers arrived with about 95% of them intact. There are three packets of crackers inside the box, each containing seven crackers. Per the box label, a serving is two crackers at 110 calories with 2 grams of protein, 2 grams of fiber, and 2.5 grams of fat. The ingredients are graham flour (whole grain wheat), whole grain rolled oats, evaporated cane juice, safflower oil, honey, raisin paste, brown rice syrup, baking soda, monocalcium phosphate, sea salt, cinnamon, and vitamin E as a preservative. There are no artificial preservatives, flavors or colors, and no high fructose corn syrup or hydrogenated fats.The company who makes these crackers, Back to Nature, has been in business for over 50 years. Their carton is made of recycled paperboard, and Back to Nature states it supports the Nature Conservancy, a leading conservation organization.Now to the main point: How do they taste? Personally, I think they are the best tasting graham crackers I've ever had. I love the crispy texture and the lightly sweet taste. I'm looking forward to using these to make graham-cracker crust with coconut oil. It should be really delicious. This is a product that I'm definitely going to purchase again in the future, and perhaps try some of the other flavors the company offers.

column9: Actually like it (thought I would not)
column10: Alright, how do you review crackers>  Seriously? Well, her eit goes.I liked these crackers a lot.  I expected some brittle flaky crackers.  The taste was sufficiently good enough that I went back for more and in fact ate the whole box.  The honey taste is just right with a slight taste of cinnamon.  The crackers are a little dry compared to other leading (not so healthy) brands like Honey Maid.  There exists a definite whole grain type of texture that I actually find appealing.  I found that I did not need liquid to "wash down" the crackers as suggested by some other reviewers.  For a healthier choice cracker, I am very impressed.I am also impressed with the use of recycable and recycled materials in the packaging, providing a leg up on the competition IMHO.This product does not use corn syrup or regular salt.  Instead you get natural sugar and sea salt with no preservatives or other additives.  The crackers break apart easily, whcih I am personally OK with but might pose a problem if you use a spread or want to make smores. My 4 year old did not like them but my 9 year old did.  They both eat organic and whole foods regularly.Worth a try at the right price in my opinion.  They seem a little more expensive than Honey Maid.  But with food prices going up everyday, who knows by the time you read this.

column9: You're never too old to enjoy graham crackers.
column10: Possibly, many Americans are familiar with Nabisco's Honey Maid graham crackers. The configuration, shape, size, and flavor, of these crackers has been standard for decades. While I do not have any Nabisco's graham crackers on hand right now, for a side-by-side comparison, I can easily remember the characteristics of this product.Now for the review.The BACK TO NATURE oat graham crackers comes in a box of moderate size. I was surprised by its heavy weight, that is, by its density. The BACK TO NATURE crackers seem a bit crisper and crunchier than the Nabisco product which, in my opinion, is somewhat soft and gets softer with storage. Crunchiness is generally considered to be a good thing (though the excessive crunchiness of food products such as Almond Roca can cause damage to teeth and to fillings and such). Even though I received the BACK TO NATURE products in the mail, there was very little breakage. I can conclude that the BACK TO NATURE graham crackers are a sturdy product, and will not likely be broken when toted in a plastic container by your kids, on the way to school.The BACK TO NATURE oat graham crackers are distinguished by the flecks of light-colored bits of oatmeal, which are baked into the top surface. In fact, the color photograph on the box shows a stack of three crackers with an abundance of oats adhering to, or baked into, the top surface of the crackers. This is another good thing.The BACK TO NATURE oat graham crackers have a dotted line that bisects the cracker, to make it easy to divide the cracker into two equal halves. This dotted line is not effective in the BACK TO NATURE product. Instead, the cracker always breaks just to the side of the dotted line, leaving you with two halves, but where one half is slightly larger than the other half. But this is neither good nor bad, unless you have a need to break the crackers into two equal halves, for example, for manufacturing a peanut butter sandwich.The BACK TO NATURE package label discloses that one serving contains 110 calories, 2.5 grams of fat, 21 grams of carbohydrate, and 2 grams of protein. The box informs us that one serving is 2 full cracker sheets.Now, let us compare this with the standard Nabisco Honey Maid crackers: 130 calories per serving, 3 g fat, 24 g carbohydrates, 2 g protein. And now, let us compare this with the low fat Nabisco Honey Maid crackers: 140 calories, 2 g fat, 28 g carbohydrates, and 2 g protein. The differences in these ratios are slight, and are not dramatic. Now (just for fun), let us look at a box of ordinary, unflavored oatmeal. I'm looking now at a box of generic oatmeal from Raley's Fine Foods. A serving has 150 calories, 2.5 g fat, 27 g carbohydrate, and 5 g protein. What does this all mean? I calculated the GRAMS PROTEIN/CALORIES for all of these products. There was little difference between the three graham cracker products, though it might be noted that the best (highest protein content per calorie) was from BACK TO NATURE. But ordinary oatmeal proved to be the best. For ordinary oatmeal, the ratio of protein/calories was twice that of the three graham cracker products. Now what can we conclude from this? If you are interested in the best nutrition, as far as oat products are concerned, then I recommend eating oatmeal right out of an oatmeal box. But in view of the fact that nobody does this sort of thing, I can recommend the BACK TO NATURE graham crackers as the next best way to satisfy your protein requirement.The protein requirement for a young child is 24 grams of protein per day (see my book, Nutritional Biochemistry, Academic Press, 1999). In the unlikely event that you want your child to acquire all of his or her protein requirement from BACK TO NATURE graham crackers, junior would need to consume twelve (12) of these crackers per day. This is not unreasonable. While writing this review, I consumed eight (8) BACK TO NATURE crackers. Just for the record, the protein requirement for the adult baby-boomer is 2.6-times greater than that of a child (aged 4-6).

column9: A treat, great for snacks and desert
column10: These crackers were a big hit at my home; in terms of taste, they are quite delicious, even better than other brands (Nabisco, etc).  We previously purchased the standard Graham Crackers and I expected these to be very similar, but in fact they are much more substantial!  They contain a lot of oats as well as some vitamins, and a single serving (one full cracker) actually is fairly filling if you're having it for a snack.One issue I did have with these is that because of their composition they are very crumbly.  I don't think I had a single cracker break neatly apart, rather they fell into small pieces directly when bitten or snapped.  This can be a little bit of a hassle and you might want your hand-vac around to tidy up afterward!These are fairly calorie dense and VERY sugary, although it's all natural sugars rather than high fructose corn syrup.  However the fiber they contain is pretty substantial, in a snack you could do a lot worse.

I had actually been in the market for better graham crackers (that is, some not made with horrible ingredients), and these certainly fill the bill. No partially hydrogenated oils, high fructose corn syrup, or artificial flavors here! And the result is not the bland slab of wheat some natural foods companies are calling graham crackers; this is a graham cracker that tastes like a graham cracker. It's sweet, albeit in a softer, subtler way than its HoneyMaid counterpart. These are also very crunchy/crispy and therefore somewhat fragile.Still, these are qualified for all traditional graham cracker uses: light snacking, pie crust, S'mores, or (and this may not be traditional outside my family) slathering with royal icing when you need something sweet but don't have a lot of ingredients. Just note that these aren't always the most presentable graham crackers (if that's something you're looking for), as they break easily and you are basically guaranteed to get a couple shattered graham crackers per package.Somewhat disappointing fact: Back To Nature is a subsidiary of Kraft. Sigh.
While a passable adjunct for the original, 'Back To Nature Golden Honey' is slightly harder to chew although the flavor makes things a bit more fun.Good but not stellar.

Back to Nature Golden Honey Oat Graham Crackers are an okay cracker. Nothing special, and far from the best graham cracker I've ever had.The box says there is a "hint of cinnamon". I couldn't really detect any cinnamon flavor, so it must be a pretty small hint. Cinnamon is the next to last ingredient on the label.Here's my real complaint. And this is something I've seen more and more often in foods that are labelled "natural" and "organic". The box says there is "No High Fructose Corn Syrup". That's a good thing. I'm diabetic, so I always check the ingredient list for sugar. And there is none listed on this box! Yay!But wait ... what's the second ingredient on the list? "Evaporated Cane Juice". Excuse me, but isn't that SUGAR???I think it's deceptive of the natural/organic food industry to disguise the fact that there is sugar in their products by calling it something else. Calling sugar "evaporated cane juice" is misleading, and it's wrong.I would have given the product three stars, but they lost one for that.

These are not your normal graham crackers...these are thicker and more to them than the regular ones....but I like these better.  They are much healthier and have a full bodied taste as well as fuller texture.  I like to make the grandchildren smores with them...using nutella and creamed marshmallow.  My husband really likes them also!

column9: Wonderfully crunchy...robust, and just sweet enough
column10: A very nice graham cracker, with a robust oat/flavor. Very crunchy. The "hint of cinnamon" is definitely easy to taste, yet adds a nice flavor that is just sweet enough due to the honey.  This is a cracker that is just sweet and savory enough to serve as a sweet snack, but also was very yummy with cheese or peanut butter.  I love graham crackers and this one is great.

column9: Loved by a picky graham cracker eater
column10: I was a little worried at first about how these grahams would taste.  Just judging from the box, they don't look that appealing.  But I was pleasantly surprised.  They tasted almost as good as a regular honey graham, but with the added benefit of the oats and whole grains.  l liked that all the ingredients were natural and that there didn't seem to be a ton of sugar in them.  My kids thought they were great, too.

I really enjoy eating the sugar laden graham crackers, but I prefer these 100% natural honey oat grahams now. These are satisfying with the oats and the honey adds a slight touch of sweetness. I use these to hold me over until lunch time, but they are a great snack for any time. One pack contains a fair amount of graham crackers and at this price, I think its a great value for six boxes of these delicious grahams. I will never go back to unhealthy standard graham crackers. These oat grahams revived my love for grahams.

If you're concerned about what you put into your body and want to avoid certain ingredients that have been found to be unhealthy, then these crackers are for you. If you want a good tasting graham cracker with some crunch, then these are for you. This product is not only packaged in earth-friendly recycled paper, but the crackers themselves are all natural and really taste quite good. Sometimes the all-natural label means that it tastes like cardboard. Not so with these crunchy grahams. The interior packaging was a little hard to get open, but once I opened it I could smell the cinnamon from the crackers. When I bit into one I was surprised with the crunch and delighted with the flavor. These are really good! No artificial flavors, preservatives or colors, no high fructose corn syrup and no hydrogenated oils. I will be seeking these out again. I highly recommend this product.

These are some of the best grahams I have eaten in quite a long time. They are crunchy and sweet, but not too sweet. They are made with whole grain and not white flour. They are not loaded with sugar. Oh, and they actually have flavor.

column9: Great afternoon snack at the office.
column10: We all know how graham crackers taste like by now.  We've used them in our ginger bread houses back from elementary school building our marshmallow buildings.  Okay if that wasn't you, it's fine.  Back to Nature's Golden Honey Oat graham crackers - they are perfect for the health conscious afternoon snacker.  They're 100% natural (no preservatives, flavors, colors, and no high fructose corn syrup).  They're similar size to your Honey Maid crackers but does taste more natural.  There's more of a crunch to them and you can see the dried pieces of oats on top.  They're slightly less sweet as the Honey Maid brand but overall very satisfying.

Like getting granola in your graham cracker.Crunchy, sweet, but not overly sweet and a good source of fiber.When you eat this, you know you are getting your allowance of fiber from the way this goes down.Enjoy.

These are nice wholesome, fulfilling, filling, crackers. The grahams are deeeelicious. My two and half year old daughter loved them.You can see that they are made from whole grains, the bite is filled with that crunch and substance. They are not very sweet, just the right amount, and that sweetness seems to come from natural sweetenings, not loads of sugar. The serving size is 8 crackers with around 110 calories only, which is quite sinless.They are not as tasty as the fattening ones, but if you are used to eating healthy food, you will see what I mean.Overall a great snack pack for those late afternoon urges for us in office, and for kids to top off with honey or cereal!
These crackers are much more filling than regular honey grahams. You can see the real oats in them and they are flavored perfectly, not too sweet. Really good.

We've now tried both these and the apple cinnamon version and love them both.  They are such a step above traditional mass-market graham crackers.  These stand up to a quick dip in milk (which makes them even better) and they have a better texture and flavor.  They have this really nice grainy flavor and they don't just turn to powder in your mouth.  We didn't like the honey flavor as much as the apple cinnamon but they were still excellent.  We'll definitely get more though we'll lean more towards the apple cinnamon.

i love graham crackers and these were just ok.they were a little dense for me and really didn't have that "graham" taste like the normal ones you find in the store.they weren't horrible but they weren't my favorite.  i would buy them only if the store was completely out of normal graham crackers.i just didn't care for the dense feeling, the lack of "grahamy" taste and just the overall graham cracker feeling.

Really delicious, all natural Graham crackers that Dr. Graham would heartily approve of.  Loads of Graham flavor, great crunch, loads of fiber and not to sweet.  What's not to like?My box was free from Amazon Vine, but I will be definitely be buying these from now on.

Since my kids have been very young, we have strived for healthy eating.  That includes whole grain breads, pastas and snacks.  This is a HUGE hit our family and I'm not surprised.  It's not something out of the ordinary for me to buy this.  My entire family was thrilled with the heartiness of this graham cracker.  It's not loaded with sugar sprinkled on it and the visible pieces of oats make it even look healthy.  Don't be fooled... they are simply sweet and addictive.  Be sure to keep a box in the car for the "after school or sports" snack time!When looking for a hearty snack that can sustain your children, this is a great choice.

These graham crackers may not be for everyone, especially the purists, but I liked them. I've been eating whole grain foods for several years now so I have gotten used to the heartier texture and flavor of whole grains. Most Back To Nature foods are quite good and these Golden Honey Oat Grahams are no exception. They're crispy, not too sweet, and have a lot of flavor. You really do taste the graham and oats. I'd give them five stars but for the price.

I anticipated "healthy cardboard," but was happily surprised.  The box contained 3 packages of crackers - to prevent stale or soggy crackers if not eaten immediately.  The crackers were tasty!  Not very sweet, but rather honey-nutty flavored (sugar content seemed low in comparison to other brands).  The texture was crisp and slightly crunchy. I could see the whole grains.  I enjoyed them with milk, as a cookie kind of snack.  However, I thought these crackers were a great compliment to cheeses. Great snack!

column9: More satisfying that the average graham cracker
column10: I've tried a number of Back to Nature products in the past, and these graham crackers are by far my favorite! Not too sweet, with plenty of fiber. I enjoyed them as a snack and shared them with family members, who liked the taste as well. I kept the open packs in an airtight container and they remained fresh for quite a few weeks before I finished them all.So far I have not tried the other flavors from Back to Nature, but this one is great for a slightly sweet and healthy snack. Definitely recommended for anyone needing a better option to satisfy the occasional sweet tooth.

I was happy to find a graham cracker that was fairly healthy. But it doesn't matter what something is made with if you can't eat it. These were terrible... dry, tasteless, not even very sweet. Basically like eating a piece of crunchy cardboard. My preschooler took one happy, big bite and then looked at me in horror. I gave her permission to spit it out in the trash and then the whole box followed. Simply awful.

These Golden Honey Oat Graham Crackers are certainly good for you. I haven't looked at another box of regular graham crackers but I'm sure that these are a better alternative to them. The serving size is 8 cracker and total intake of calories from those 8 are 110 calories. That's not bad at all when you consider a lot of snacks (even ones that claim to be low calorie or good for you) are smaller and pack as many or more calories than that.The one thing that disappointed me was the taste. It has a taste of a graham cracker but I don't think that it tastes as good as other, more fattening, graham crackers out there. It reminded me kind of a dry flavor and not as palatable. So these are a good diet snack but I don't know if I could eat them more then every once in awhile.

column9: Kids like 'em a lot and I think they are fine too
column10: My kids love these graham crackers.  We tried the other versions of these and this is by far their favorite.  I like these as well but not as much as I like the standard good cinnamon graham crackers.  Overall, for a healthier choice for graham crackers, I recommend these.
These little beauties were a big hit in our busy household... oh..um.. if you get a chance?.. try them with a bit of cream cheese on them. Yumsville!

I love the Back to Nature products I've tried. And as I suspected, the graham crackers land on that life. With a great graham, hint of honey flavor these are terrific as a bed for peanut or almond butter and delicious on their own.However, if you war looking for a natural graham cracker for a crust you will need to go by weight as these little guys are smaller than traditional graham crackers. Also since they pack real old-fashioned oatmeal simple crushing might not give you the results you want. But a food processor or blender should solve that problem.

column9: Such a Tasty Snack for something Healthy!
column10: These Back to Nature Golden Honey Oat Grahams are the most tasty crackers we've ever found. I could have eaten the whole box on my own! The flavor was lighter than a traditional graham cracker- less honey/sugary flavor and more cinnamon. The fact these were made with natural ingredients and not fructose, corn syrups, etc. gives these crackers a huge edge over regular grahams.The only thing I can say I didn't care for was the fact these came fairly broken. I think shipping and handling mangled it too much. For this price, they really need to be packaged better so you aren't paying for crumbs.

What is a graham cracker ? What did I expect when these arrived in the mail ? Well, it was initially not a pleasant process. They arrived broken. Now , I enjoy my graham crackers with a little butter spread on them. Kind of hard to spread butter on broken crackers !However , the taste was unbelievable ! The crackers were crispy and very satisfying ! I enjoyed every cracker to the last bite.

column4: Monette L. Bebow Reinhard "author of Felling ...
column10: I found these to be better than the average graham cracker.  They are very tasty, and they are also gritty, which I think is a good thing because it can help with digestion.  They should also last longer in the system.  I would get these again, and I can see making pie crusts with them as well, which is what I'll try next!

column9: Natural ingredients and tastes fine to me
column10: If you're someone who cares about natural ingredients as well as the environment, this seems to be an excellent graham cracker product to buy. Even the box itself is 100% recycled paperboard. The honey taste is light and pleasant although the cracker seems somewhat dry to me - but perhaps graham crackers are supposed to be on the dry side? (I'm not very experienced with graham crackers.)

Back To Nature Golden Honey Oat Grahams are a decent alternative to their traditional counterparts.  They have a few things going for them.  They provide a very light honey and cinnamon taste much like most standard graham crackers, and soak up milk quite well.  I have not had the opportunity to hold them to the fire (literally) to make s'mores, but I'm sure they would hold up just fine.Where I find them lacking is in the texture of the crackers.  They are stiff and nearly cardboard-like.  Eating them can turn into a task due to their coarseness.  While the oats sprinkled all over the cracker might look good to health conscious adults, they might prove to be a turn off for children.Overall, this is an average graham cracker that suffers from bad looks and texture.  If you're going on the Graham diet (look it up), these are right up your alley.  Adults will probably have no problems with eating these crackers, but I'd stick to the more traditional Honey Maid brand for children.
These crackers are delicious, and healthy.  My 17-month old daughter eats them equally as well as the popular graham cracker brand.  I will definitely buy these again.

I, too, thought that Back to Nature made slight compromises with taste and texture in order to offer only healthy, whole grain ingredients in their Golden Honey Oat Grahams.  However, I didn't find the difference to be any greater than that between, perhaps, a brand-name and a generic "unhealthy" brand.  Obviously, it will depend on your and your family's tastes whether the less-sweet flavor and heavier, more-dry texture is an acceptable tradeoff in order to choose a healthier product.  I certainly felt it was close enough that I would let "more healthy" make the decision.

Back to Nature Golden Honey Oat Grahams were quite delicious.  They taste faintly of cinnamon and honey but have oats in them and are healthier than regular graham crackers.  They are crisp on the outside but soften while you are chewing, so that you get a good mouth feel and a slightly sweet but satisfying taste.  As one who is prone to eat through the entire box, I also liked the fact that they were packaged in a smaller box than regular graham crackers.  These are good by themselves, were surprisingly good with mild cheese (such as gouda or havarti), and would probably make killer s'mores!  (Healthy s'mores...what a concept!)  Oh, and the box is made from recycled cardboard too.I'll be looking for these in my local grocery store.

column9: Best Graham crackers I've ever eaten!
column10: These crackers don't taste like they are whole grain. Just very crisp, lightly sweet, with a hint of cinnamon.  They come in 4 sealed packages, just like the Graham crackers I ate as a child.I have suffered through many whole grain versions of Graham crackers, all of which have had a heavy texture that I thought was a necessary evil I had to endure in exchange for the healthier benefits.  I'm so glad I found these instead, and my family all really likes them.
My kids weren't too into these graham crackers.  They were on the dry side, and my youngest wasn't a fan of the oat topping (some kids just prefer plain).  We'll stick with the competition.

These, as well as the apple cinnamon flavor from back to nature, are really good. Sometimes a little change up is good. What they do with their crackers is add some subtle flavor so that you don't lose the graham flavor. And they do it very well. Nice texture also, crispy/crunchy. Definitely worth a try.

These crackers are labeled healthy and good.  They are definately good.  I was so impressed I did not even care if they were healthy but I would buy them in a heartbeat if I find them in a store or on Amazon.  Crispy, nutty, crunchy are just a few of the descriptive words that fit the item.

These graham crackers are quite good; they are made from wholesome ingredients, and they taste delicious.  They are very thin, almost wafer-like crackers made from whole wheat flour, rolled oats, and natural sweeteners, including honey.  They are relatively low-calorie, with 110 calories per serving, and they are a very good source of whole grains.  If you're not going to buy organic, this is a reasonable alternative, with natural ingredients and produced by a brand that uses recycled packaging and contributes money to the Nature Conservancy (although it is owned by Kraft).  I would have given them a 5 out of 5, but I've had the apple cinnamon graham crackers that Back To Nature also makes, and those are much, much better tasting.  I you are not a fan of apple cinnamon or are looking for the traditional honey graham cracker, definitely buy these.  Otherwise, I would have to recommend the apple cinnamon flavor over these.

I really liked the taste of these crackers even better than regular graham crackers, but I found them to be a little dry. Nothing that a glass of milk or juice wouldn't fix, though. And they didn't always crack along the perforations, so sometimes they ended up in pieces.

column9: head and shoulders above the competition best graham cracker I've ever had
column10: These graham crackers are the best I've ever tasted. I've sampled these graham crackers with other food connoisseurs and they voted for these graham crackers. What makes these graham crackers so good? Before I open the box I noticed the box was smaller but heavier than the competitors. The taste and texture of this product is what really stands out. These graham crackers have smooth rich well-balanced flavor. Mouth feel is a little heavier than a typical graham cracker but is not a distraction, mouth feel conveys more of a sense of richness. The flavor of oats is present and at first might be a distraction. One sampler of the product at first did not take to the oat flavor but eventually came around to favoring these graham crackers compared to the competition. All the graham crackers sample including these had no hyphenated oils. A+

At 110 calories for 8 crackers, this is a healthy (low calorie) snack. I've tried both the Apple Cinnamon and Honey flavors. The Honey flavor tastes like a regular Nabisco (or other brand) graham, but without the artificial ingredients found in those other brands. The box is a bit misleading because it says "no high fructose corn syrup." That's true when you check the ingredients. But it has "rice syryp" which is effectively the same as corn syrup. Nonethless it is a relatively healthy snack. As with other Back to Nature products it is an excellent alternative to other brands.

These graham crackers are great. The taste is rich, the sweetness from honey is very mild and not overbearing. The nutrition aspect seemed to be decent based on the ingredients and the nutritional table. They appealed to the entire family.

Back To Nature Golden Honey Oat Grahams, 10-Ounce (Pack of 6) do not have artificial preservatives, flavors, or colors and  do not contain high fructose corn syrup or hydrogenated oils. They do have whole grain wheat and oats, irresistible flavor, and crispness. They are simple and simply delicious with a hint of cinnamon. One full cracker sheet has only 55 calories with a gram of fiber. Who would have ever thought graham crackers could be so good? My family helped me devour these. Yum!

As a natural foodie I was pleased with the ingredient list. All too often there is one baddie ingredient that stops me from buying a product such as corn syrup or chemical "stabilizers/preservatives" I found them tasty with enough sweetness to tame my sweet tooth. They are a bit dry but all in all it's a reasonable trade off for the lower fat content. A cup of tea on the side or a bit of mashed fruit on top makes this a great between meal treat. I've also crumbed them to use as topping on yogurt and fruit. I will definitely add them to my shopping list.

Really like the inclusion of rolled oats. No artificial preservatives or flavors. The honey adds a nice hint of sweetness in every bite, which is great given most all-natural snacks lack that element. Tastes great served with several types of toppings, and most importantly--as smores!

column9: nothing special - I preferred the apple cinnamon variety
column10: I tried both this flavor (Golden Honey Oat) and the Apple Cinnamon variety.  As far as graham crackers go, there's nothing exceptional about either flavor -- though I have no complaints about either the flavor or texture, either.  I definitely preferred the apple-cinnamon flavor over these, more generic tasting crackers.  If you have an extreme sweet tooth, you might not like this brand as it's less sweet than mainstream graham crackers, but I think they are sweet enough.

I have never been a fan of Graham crackers. But these are good and taste is mild. If you eat one cracker it is just filling for a snack.They are fresh packed in multiple small packages to maintain freshness.

I couldn't find any ingredients listed on the product's description page and, because I don't eat gluten, I was hoping that these might be made with oats *instead* of wheat.  No such luck.  However, my two daughters had wiped out the box within twenty-four hours!  I'd say that means these are pretty tasty.  And, being from Back to Nature, they use more wholesome ingredients than more mainstream graham crackers.  I'm not really sure what the point is of the oats, though, as opposed to plain graham crackers.

First off I like the back to nature brand and buy several of their products. Their peanut butter cookies are the best. These are a really good choice when you want something sweet. Not quite like the ones I grew up with. These are more substantial. There are chunks of grain that require good teeth. Great to dip in milk or coffee.

These crackers are quite tasty and my family loved the taste, crunch and oats on tip.However, a bunch of mine in my box were crushed on arrival, perhaps because my box was shipped in a padded envelope. If you buy in bulk, Amazon will probably ship to you in a box which might prevent breakage.I'd buy them again though because they tasted so good.

My family and I love crackers (they make great snacks at the park) and I was excited to try out Back to Nature Apple Cinnamon Oat Grahams and Back to Nature Golden Honey Oat.  They traveled well in my purse for our daily park outing after school.  They are packaged just like your regular Honey Maid Graham crackers and if you tried passing them off to your kids as such, they'd be none the wiser.  Their are some small oatmeal flecks, but minimal.  They are slightly dry and crumble easily, but the taste is good.  If I were going to sit around and want a sweet snack, I would lean towards the Honey Maid crackers but these make great snacks during the day (and a slightly healthier option).  It all boils down to personal preference but if you are looking for less calories and higher fiber, try these.

For being a natural and relatively healthy food item, I'm impressed by how good these crackers actually taste!  They're not as sweet as a standard graham cracker, but again, very good for what they are.I top them with natural peanut butter and eat them with a glass of milk, yum!

column9: If my HUSBAND loves them, ANYONE can love them!
column10: These graham crackers are a great alternative to the highly processed grahams that we have had since we were kids. Though my husband was skeptical, we have been trying to gradually improve our choices at the grocery store, and this was yet another experiment. He actually loved them and ate nearly the whole box himself (over time of course!).The rest of the family liked them as well, though they did note a difference, and we actually prefer them. They are slightly "dryer" than the average honey graham, but taste just like them, only a bit more natural and ever so slightly less sweet. The oats are in the cracker yet they are not grainy or rough like some health food alternatives can be. However, they are not a health food by any means, they are still a snack food.These are tasty, as are many of the other Back to Nature products (we also LOVE their cookies) so I would certainly recommend them. Enjoy!

I've loved graham crackers since I was a kid but many of the brands just aren't as good as they used to be.  Enter Back To Nature Golden Honey Oat Grahams.  They are crispy with a hearty, whole grain, nutty taste.  They are great with coffee or tea.  They are a bit crispier than your elf or other name brand graham cracker, so they don't always snap apart on the lines but they are very good.  They are a bit pricier as well (10 oz. for about $3 vs. 12-14 oz. for $2.50 - $3.00 for the other brands) but for me, I don't mind paying more for a better quality product.  These crackers have less calories, less fat and more fiber than your typical graham cracker too so what's not to love?

column9: Amazing re-interpretation of honey oat grahams
column10: Upon biting into one of these, I was not only convinced that the product was a good as its less healthy alternative, but found it to be head and shoulders above it. The cracker is amazing and then there are these bits of oats on each of them that give it an extra kick. I will buy this product again and give it my highest recommendation
I love quality, and this product is definitely quality. Tasty, crisp without additives.Put some Nutella and/or marshmallow spread on them and it is a delightful treat for adults and kids. YUMMY!

I really enjoyed these graham crackers a lot more than I ever remember liking graham crackers.For one thing, they are made with real graham flour, something that is generally lacking in most mass produced graham crackers.  I think the oats add even more to the wonderful graham texture.As far as sweetness, I am not a fan over overly sweet things, and this, to me, was just right, a touch on the sweet side; but still very tasty. I will never even bother with the regular "graham" crackers again!

The packaging looks like this should be healthy - its recyclable. However that does not mean that the contents don't also taste like cardboard! Thankfully the cracker tastes wholesome and even though a little crispier than regular Grahams is more flavorful with the honey more distinct. The oats are a welcome addition.The real test is of course - the child test. Have no fear - my discerning 5 year old - wolfed most of the packet. What better endorsement do you want? And I know he's getting good nutrition as well.

Although not as sweet as traditional, I am not missing the sweet and artificial flavor of those.  These taste almost like you made them yourself, by comparison with a much fresher and clearer taste.  Definitely worth a taste!

column9: Not bad, but not great. Probably best for baking needs versus snacking
column10: I was really looking forward to trying these healthier graham crackers, but in the end I was a bit disappointed with the Back To Nature Golden Honey Oat Grahams. As a snack, these graham crackers had a bit of a cardboard texture to them; the flavor was pretty good, but a little understated on the honey. Ultimately, I was not drawn to them as a healthier snack.Where I did end up using them with better success was in recipes that called for graham crackers... they worked very well in my peanut butter balls. I think they would work pretty well as a graham cracker pie crust as well.

column9: Good Graham Crackers with a Touch of Oats and Honey
column10: My immediate family (my wife, my daughter, my son, and myself) all love Graham crackers so I was eager to give these new "Back To Nature Golden Honey Oat Grahams" a try. I'm not crazy about the bland packaging that looks like 90 percent of the boxes in the organic foods section of my grocery store, but you shouldn't judge a food by the box it comes in.The Grahams themselves look pretty much the same as any Graham cracker you've bought before. The only obvious difference to me is the fact that these crackers have bits of oats sticking out and feel a little drier to the touch than the Graham crackers we usually purchase at the store.You can certainly taste the oats and honey in these Grahams compared to typical Graham crackers. It's almost as if you took a regular Graham cracker, sprayed it with a mist of honey and sprinkled oatmeal on them. Overall, I like these a lot and would recommend them as a change of pace compared to regular Graham crackers.

I am very impressed by these.  I'm one of those that actually likes most whole grain products, appreciating the slightly drier crispy texture of many of these products, and this is no exception.  I think the flavor is better than the typical store brought graham cracker, and the texture is really nice, crisp but not cardboard dry.  They contain whole grain wheat as well as rolled oats.  Two full cracker sheets is only 110 calories, making this a good choice for dieters.  They have no artificial preservatives, flavors, coloring or high fructose corn syrup, and the box is made with recycled paper! An excellent product.

column9: Subtle honey flavor & chewy oatiness = best of the pack
column10: Back to Nature Honey Oat Graham Crackers are perhaps the best tasting of all the "natural" grahams I have tried.  There is a subtle natural honey flavor and a slight oaty chewiness to each bite with no strange aftertaste.  The flavor profile is further enhanced by an ever so slight hint of cinnamon.The texture is crisp and not cardboardy like some of the other natural brands and is best suited for out-of-hand eating, rather than pie crust making or conversion to cereal/dunking as it lacks the structural grittiness of regular grahams. [See photo above]Overall a very pleasant and enjoyable surprise and one I will be definitely buying again.
Ordered this a few days ago and just got it last night.Poured a cup this morning - its awesome.Light, but great flavor!

column9: If you LOVE Chicken wing meat...
column10: UPDATE June 2009: They changed the recipe so these are now more tender (good thing), but they got rid of the slight tangy vinegar flavor. Now they don't taste like chicken wings; just spicy chicken jerky. I will probably buy these about once a year now, instead of 1-2 times per month. Back to the Jalapeno jerky, when I can find it!ORIGINAL REVIEW from 11/29/08: I don't eat chicken wings that often any more (90 fat calories per wing, being deep fried and dipped in butter). And I LOVE chicken wings! But if the flavor you crave is that hot sauce & vinegar comingling with a large chunk of tender chicken, then give these a try. If you're looking for the butter, crispy or chewy skin, and deep fried flavor components, then you won't have those here. I don't buy beef jerky anymore (which is also a favorite), I buy these! I just wish they weren't so hard to find locally. Circle K and Walgreens are the only retail locations I know of. Eat 1 bag, and you'll be addicted or nonplussed. There's not really a middle road.

I DO NOT EVEN CARE IF THIS IS OVERPRICED, THESE ARE ABSOLUTELY DELICIOUS. THERE'S NOT A TON OF MEAT IN EACH PACKAGE, BUT IT HITS THE SPOT. GOOD LORD, THESE TASTE SO DELICIOUS, I DO NOT EVEN KNOW WHAT MORE TO SAY.
Best one yet.If you have not tried this one yet your missing out very tender and moist nuggets.The only negative is the 3.25 size bag is much to small.

I bought these to share with the office and the disappeared almost instantly.  They are very good and contain enough protein to keep people going while suppressing that "snacky" feeling.  These are a great snack to carry with you as they are very light (for example, on a flight or road trip).  I highly recommend that you try a few of the other flavors as well.  They have this snack in Chicken, Turkey and Beef in various flavors.

I am an avid consumer of Jack Links Beef Steak Nuggets.  This batch is stale, dry and almost tasteless.  I can purchase these in even remote gas stations and they taste juicy and wonderful. I am too lazy to return them but will never buy them over the internet again.

I can't give these a 5 because the ingredients show they are very processed.  I'm not sure how healthy they are.But the taste is great - very hot  - like about a nuclear on the Zaxby's scale.  If you like hot wings, you'll like these.  Be prepared to not be able to leave them alone.  When my husband buys a bag, we sit there and eat them until they are gone.  Also, have something to drink handy!

I was expected a lot better. i LOVE the beef jerkey nuggets they are so juicy n flavorful and delicious, but when i ordered these just to try them cause i couldnt find them in any store i wasnt too happy. when i tried them they were extremely greasy and not that much flavor.

column9: dry meat and short expiration date
column10: Ordered OVEN ROASTED TURKEY NUGGETS*** for the first time. Meat is dry. Expiration date is too close; received today, SEPT 9, 2011, expiring NOV 21, 2011.In the past, have had very good experience with the Chicken Teriyaki nuggets. Jack Link's used to use dark meat. Jack Link's changed the recipe to white meat and the nuggets do not taste as rich any more.*** Very disappointed with Amazon's approach on linking ALL Jack Link's nuggets together. Meaning: If you post a review for the Chicken Teriyaki ones, you can NOT post one for the flaming chicken, turkey over roasted, etc.?! And the same review will show up under any and all of them. I contacted Amazon and customer service first tried to convince me I was doing something wrong. On the third e-mail, the senior CS guru indicated the nugget products are all linked together and nothing will be done about the issue.

These are the typical red bags of premium beef-jerky you see at the store, only...you get FOUR of them! These four bags of delicious, mouth-watering beef nuggets are a tasty and healthy snack, and I don't feel bad about eating a whole bag throughout the day at my desk.I love all of the varieties Jack Link's has to offer. I've been a die-hard Teriyaki fan myself, so I'm hesitant to sway away from my typical "go-to" bag.If you're looking for a satisfying feel-good snack to take on road trips, sporting events, at your desk, or what-have-you ' you do NOT want to pass this up.

These are pretty good, but a little overpriced - I would only buy if there was a promotion. Some pieces are deliciously tender and seasoned perfectly, but there usually are more that are too dried out and tough, or overseasoned.

column9: Great for snacking or for a small meal!!!
column10: These are great!  They are spicy, but not too spicy.  They taste just like Buffalo Hot Wings but without the bones. I agree with another reviewer who is thinking about microwaving these as I bet these would taste even better warmed up!  I bought an 8 pack of these and keep these at my job for when I get the munchies and want some quick protein and the calories for one bag is only about 280 so that is perfect for a snack or to ward away the hunger pangs.  These would be great for someone doing a low-carb diet or someone who just wants extra protein for their body.  One bag also has just over 30 grams of protein and this tastes so much better than eating just a protein bar.  Bottom line is this... if you love hot wings and can't get enough give these a try.  You won't be disappointed.

I just tried these recently and I can't get enough of them now.  They don't have the texture of buffalo chicken wings, it's more like the stuff you get when you order a buffalo chicken pizza...just chunks of plain old chicken smothered in hot sauce.  Haven't tried it yet, but they seem like they'd be REALLY good warmed up or tossed on a pizza before it goes into the oven.They seem to be a bit more expensive than other Jack Link stuff, but so worth it.  Om nom nom nom nom

column9: Disgustingly salty, in a dog treat shape
column10: I wanted to get some jerky and since I like buffalo wings I tried these. The problem is there is way too much salt, it's disgustingly salty, way more than normal jerky. I can barely eat it. If you eat a 3.25 oz package of these you will have eaten 1840mg of sodium, instant high blood pressure.

I was a bit apprehensive ordering these from Amazon because I had read in other reviews that some of the jerky were moldy. I am happy to say that mine were absolutely mold-free! My family vanquished 2 packets on the spot LOL...
Absolutely love these steak nuggets! Everywhere around here they go for over 8 dollars, so I was thrilled when I found out I could buy these on here. Very tender and the spices are amazing.

Little morsels of moist, pure beef that taste like high quality roast.  I got the Teriyaki by accident - I normally don't like teriyaki ANYTHING - but the only hint of added flavoring on these is a little sweetness.Lean, good cuts of meat with no nasty little gristley surprises.  My only criticism is they must cook these in crack cocaine, because I'm absolutely addicted to them.
I love the steak nuggets (and tenders) even better than their regular jerky.  I swear by all three of the Original, Peppered and Teriyaki Beef flavors.

I'm a big fan of Buffalo chicken and beef jerky, so I thought I'd love the Jack Link's Flamin Buffalo Chicken Nuggets.  I was wrong.  I bought the Steak Nuggets as well, which aren't as good as Jack Link's jerky, but definitely tasted better than the Buffalo Chicken Nuggets.To put it bluntly, they tasted like an old chunk of salty chicken with a slight Buffalo flavor.  They're not very spicy, I was expecting more of a kick.  They also smelled a little funny.  I'd give Buffalo chicken jerky a try, but I won't be buying these ever again. They're OK, but there's so many better options out there.

column9: Jack Links  Teryiaki Beef Steak Nuggets
column10: The beef nuggets are soft and easy on the teeth and tasty. If they are slightly less salty, they will be excellent.Very good snack.Johnson
These were good, but I really couldn't taste the A1 in them.  Tasted similar to the original steak nuggets to me

I would like to say that I have never tried a flavor of jerky that I didn't like...  that was true until a few days ago.  I wanted to try something different and decided to stray from my usual peppered beef.  This was a mistake, I have to say this is the worst jerky/nuggets/meat product I have ever tried.  From the smell to the taste, just not good.  If you really want to give this stuff a whirl, I suggest you find a single pack.  Don't buy 4 of them like I did.  One final note:  taste is subjective, you may really love this stuff, I just didn't.

I find that the buffalo chicken jerky is great for when I'm craving buffalo wings late at night. Sure they're not the saucy goodness of wings at a bar but they definitely replicate the flavor. They are very hot but delicious.

I normally have beef jerkey with my lunch for some easy to transport protein. I decided to give these a try, bought them at the grocery store and they were great. Easy to measure and a lot less stringy than normal beef jerkey.I ended up saving a ton of money using amazons subscribe and save over using the grocery store. Definitely something I'll reorder.
I really like the product.  It was super easy to order online and have it delivered.  Much cheaper than buying in a gas station.  Stocking up is good for long drives, too.

These taste amazing! Best jerky I've ever had. They are kind of expensive, but once in a while Amazon will lower the price slightly and hopefully that happens when they are offering a 10% off Jack Link's products promo code. Anyone who likes jerky or is simply looking for a convenient high protein snack should give these a try.
The bite size chewables are wonderful - 2 or 3 every few hours lets yu diet and never feel hungry.
I purchased these to snack on after my workouts. Now I find myself just snacking on them all the time!! They're really good and come in a variety of flavors.
These are strangely addictive - and a good sugarless snack.  I like this flavor and the original, but the pepper is really strong.  Enjoy!

column9: Love it!  But huge on sodium though.
column10: Flamin' Buffalo Chick + A1 are my all time favorites. The meat is tender, and the taste (based on the ones I've bought) are extreme with flavor. The only problem with jerky is the salt, and these have a ton of it. I wouldn't consume more then one bag a day, but it's your choice and body. I'll definitely be buying more in the future though, because these are delicious.

These are a great go-to snack/meal when you're in a rush and don't want chips or hotdogs.The nuggets are about the size of a stack of three quarters with some smaller ones the size of a couple of nickels.The flavor is spicy with a nice tang.The texture is softer than jerky but not as soft as say summer sausage.Quick comment on quantity - there are three servings, 60 calories each, in the package.  This ends up being a little over a handful for the entire package.Great to have on hand for those on the go times.

This is a nice tasty option that's totally different from jerky.  Convenient on the go just like jerky.  I would have given it five stars if not for the fact that it's quite salty, and that detracts from the flavor.
This is very good just a little too much of the A-1 flavor for us. Next time will order another flavor. If you really  love A-1 you will be pleased with it.

I thought this would be spicy, and coming from someone who eats spicy food all the time and fire sauce on his burritos, this is really only mild. This does not make your nose run, or make your throat burn, ears tingle, which is the funnest part of eating spicy food. Spicy food containing cayenne pepper is very healthy for you and is great for colds and sore throats. With a name like Flaming Buffalo with fire coming out of the name I had high hopes...and sadly this does not live up to the hype in the heat department. It still tastes good. The flavor lingers in your mouth making you reach for another one, after 6-8 pieces or so you get a salty taste that makes you reach for water. I give this 3 stars for taste and convenience. Just in case you don't eat it all in one sitting, the bag contains a zip-lock storage to keep things sealed. It will last 3 days after opening without refrigeration.

They are tasty, well flavored, always premium cuts, nothing tasted substandard.  On top of that high protein and low calorie! Only problem - everybody else thinks the same thing and its hard for Jack Links to keep them in stock.  You may have to wait a few extra days for the specialty orders.

I love this product! Tasty and soft (but not too soft). Very good flavor and it's safe to say, I can't "eat just one!" If you like the jerky, but not the dried up, tough stuff...you might want to give this stuff a try!
These are nice tender jerky nuggets, more tender than the usual beef jerky.  Flavor is very good, great for energy on hiking trips.
The Flamin Buffalo has just the right amount of heat and flavor combined.  I wish I could buy the flavor so I could put them on my wings.  Very good product.

These are really good. Not hard to chew like some other beef nuggets, and they don't dry out so much.They only downside is that the bag stays very moist inside, so it can be a little messy. If you try to eat a bag while on the drive home you have grease all over your steering wheel.....

Ive always been a big Jack Links jerky fan.  I usually buy a couple bags a month, but last month I was in Vegas and they were out of A1 flavor...my personal favorite!I looked around the store and found these!  I opened the bag and had a few on my way to the pool, they were awesome.  Anybody that loves chicken wings should give these a taste.  The chicken is tender and quite generous in size.  I was pretty surprised they even brought a bead of sweat to my forehead, usually store bought "buffalo" flavors don't accomplish that.As another reviewer said these are great if you love chicken wings but don't wanna down 200 calories a piece for that spicy burn.  I do have to say these are impossible to find in WI though, so luckily amazon has them, and at a good price for a pack of 8 bags!

column9: the best "jerky" product on the market
column10: this is the best "jerky" product on the market .... I have tried them all... I hope the company will expand it's production and distribution of it !!

I love the Beef Teriyaki Nuggets and the Buffalo Chicken Nuggets. Now I have a 3rd kind to eat. These are great tasting and easy to eat (important for post bariatric surgery people). I love Jack Link's Nuggets line!
I love em.  I would give this 5 stars but there arent enough in the bag to warrent that.  they are good.

Oh my gosh, these are gross. I bought them because of Hungry Girl's glowing recommendation...and I gotta say, she steered me wrong this time. These are SUPER salty, and they taste like what I imagine dog kibbles would taste like.

column9: Jack Link's Original Beef Steak Nuggets
column10: I actually really love the Jack Link's Original Beef Steak Nuggets, however the 4 pack I received seemed to be old.  They weren't nearly as good as the ones I have purchased in gas stations.  Makes you wonder why that would be. These were tough and much drier then I expected. I have to say I will not order them again through the mail. If they had been fresher I would have rated them as I love them because I really do.

Don't buy these from Amazon Warehouse like I did...total waste of money for these dry hunks of blandness.  I wouldn't know what they are like fresh, it wasn't sold to me that way...but at least my dog had dog chews.  Not sure why Amazon insists on selling worthless food rather than throw it away and risk ticking off customers and/or poisoning them.  I know they are closer to the expiration date buying it through the warehouse but seriously...THROW BAD FOOD AWAY AMAZON!  Sheesh.

All and all it is my fault because I did not pay attention to what I ordered. When I went to the Jack's Links website it advertised white meat 95 to 97 percent fat free. At the time they did not have this product for purchase. So when I received an email saying it was now available I hurried and ordered it. It is not until I received the order did I realize I had ordered dark meat. I did not even know that dark meat was available; therefore, I was shocked and felt deceived. Yet, I had tasted the chicken nuggetts before reading the content and was wondering why was it so salty. I did get a formal apology in writing from jack's links but again it is still my fault for not paying attention. Now I am stuck with many packets of dark meat chicken nuggets. In conclusion, I guess it is still a little bit healthier than the beef. (maybe)

I don't eat beef and having a jerky snack around is nice.  Bag is enormous for what's inside it.  There's basically food in the bottom 3 inches of the bag, and, because of the sauce, if you reach your hand in instead of shaking it out of the bag into your hand, you'll end up with dirty hands.  A much smaller bag would make sense.  I'd also like to see more for the price.  Flavor is good.
these are good but verrry sweet.... they taste kind of chinese sweet bbq sauce... high protein
They have a funky flavour and really get all over you fingers. I bought these to eat while driving it it isn't going to work.

Since this type of yeast is no longer available at any of our local grocery stores, we decided to load up on this find by purchasing (3) packs worth which ends up being (45) individual yeast packets.  Problem is they arrived on 4/13/11 and the yeast expiration date is July 2011!  When we were able to get this product in our local stores, the expiration was minimally a year or more.  Since these packs cost double what the stores charge, this is ridiculous.  I guess we'll be eating pizza for breakfast, lunch, and dinner for the next 3 months before the yeast is useless!
Use any of the very good recipes on the web; this was vile. It tasted like crackers. No more like a pizza than boot soles.

column9: Not bad if your'e in a hurry/
column10: This new pizza yeast provides acceptable results in a timely manner, but remember to let the flour absorb the water for 10 minutes after forming the ball. The recipe on the package says to use flour but using bread flour provides a better product.

I agree with the other reviewer that Amazon's current pricing (as of Feb 2011) is ridiculous, being about double what my local HEB sells the stuff for.
