I am a celiac as well but I will find an alternative crust or not eat pizza. I thought this stuff tasted horrible. It doesn't cook right, even following the directions to a T. Maybe these other reviewers know something I don't. Bought it at a health food store for 8 bucks a bag so at least buy it off here so you can save some money.
My entire family loves this crust. We have celiacs disease and having to give up pizza hasn't been easy. This is the best glutton free crust we have tried.
This is the best tasting gluten free pizza dough.  It is that simple.  I have yet to find a good gluten free bread mix or flour.  But for pizza, get this stuff.

I have to admit I was a bit nervous especially as I bought a case of this as well as cases of the other Namaste products for my son.  His sudden onset of a seizure disorder put me in hyperdrive researching anything and everything I could do to make it stop.  One direction was nutritional.  I basically had 2 choices. . .  ketogenic or GARD diet (dogtorjdotcom).  I went with the Glutamic/Aspartic Reduction Diet which nixed all corn, wheat, dairy and soy as well as peanut and legumes etc.  My son is 8 and has siblings who are not affected in any observable manner from not eating the GARD diet so I did not want him to feel resentful.  He has Everything now.  ..  and we've been Thrilled with Everything . . . the pizza crust (crispy, make sure you precook it sufficiently or it will have a noodle like texture), the pancake/waffle mix (just did it today and Everyone liked it), the Brownie Mix (AWESOME), The Chocolate Cake mix (yes!! He can't wait for his birthday) . . . we have been Ever So Pleased with the Namasate line of foods and with their customer service. . .  they'll gladly send you coupons, recipes, etc.  Like I said to them in an email, "Whoever you are and whatever you went through to make this product available, THANK YOU."  It is a godsend.

My family did not like this crust.  It came out a very gummy texture.  We like the crispy pizza crust.  The waffles in this brand were wonderful.  We were hoping we had found a winner, but we will have to keep looking for GF pizza crust.

Agree with some other reviewers, that this crust didn't cook up right and was gummy. We had to throw the pizza away, it was inedible. We had gone ahead and put the toppings on before we realized the crust was gummy in the middle. I did notice the recipe had been revised and used a lot more water to mix ratio. Something is not working right for me. I emailed the company and hope they respond.

This is an excellent gluten-free pizza crust.  When I decided to go gluten-free I knew I would miss pizza the most, but this crust is a great replacement.  I'm quite picky and I highly recommend it.  The ends seem to curl up quite a bit, but that is minor.

While I love having the opportunity to make my own gluten-free pizza dough from an easy mix, I found the end result a little gummy and chewy...a common problem with gluten-free dough mixes. I much prefer the pre-made, frozen gluten-free crusts.

column9: Worked fine but had a huge bubble!
column10: This does not taste anything like wheat pizza dough, but it was easy to follow the instructions.  It came out very crispy on the edges with a huge bubble the size of the pizza rectangle, so I had to punch holes in it before I added the toppings.  The toppings are what make it taste even somewhat like pizza.  I am not gluten intolerant (as far as I know), but I wanted to test it out. I found it at TJ Maxx for $3.99.  I would recommend this mix for those with gluten intolerance or Celiac's.  It is a good substitute and it's fine if you need a way to make pizza for a family that needs to accommodate different diet requirements.  I like that you don't have to let the dough rise first.  It takes at least 30 to 35 minutes at the very least to make a pizza since you need to bake the crust first and then add the toppings.  You will also need an electric mixer to beat the dough mixture.
We haven't had any problem with the baking instructions or soggy top that others have mentioned. The dough is weird at first - does look completely like cake batter, but it cooks up delicious!
I just did not care for this product at all!  It tasted weird.  I wish I could return it back.  It's simple...

column9: Big namaste to Namaste Pizza Crust Mix
column10: This is THE BEST pizza crust.  Not just the best gluten free pizza crust, but the best pizza crust ever.  I followed the recipe that a previous reviewer gave (less liquid).  The only problem was that my veggie pizza the crust got a little soggy, but that's a problem I have with most crust, but the edges were still crunchy.  The pepperoni/olive was perfect, crust was thin and crisp, and of course oh so tasty. Can't wait to try it again, next time I'll grill the veggies to get out some of the moisture.  Namaste!

I used this product this evening for my family, and it was delicious!  I wasn't sure how I would like the seasoned crust, but it was fine.I used a standing mixer to mix the batter, and -- beware -- the splatter guard is necessary.  If you don't have a splatter guard, you should mix slowly at first, until the water is well incorporated.The only problem with the crust is that it came out somewhat gummy in the middle.  I think I should try to make it thinner next time, or use less sauce, or cook it longer, or invest in a pizza stone rather than using a cookie sheet.  Suggestions based on your experience are most welcome!!
Definitely requies electric mixer.  The only ingredients required are oil and water.  Nice herbs.  I used North American Herb and Spice, Garlex. Oil of Wild Garlic, 1 oz as my teaspoon of oil.

This is the best allergen free pizza crust that we've tried, and we've tried a lot.  No worries about the top 8 allergens!  My little boy, who has several severe food allergies, loves this crust and he is a very picky eater.  We also use it to coat fish and pan fry it.  Excellent, excellent, excellent!!!!!

column9: Namaste Foods, Gluten Free Pizza Crust Mix
column10: This is the best and easiest pizza crust I have ever made. It is so simple to make and tastes so good. I put the whole package in to make one large thickpizza. Then I top it with goat cheese and ground turkey mixed with green salsa.This pizza crust has all the flavor and great consistency in the crust. I willcontinue to buy this product. It is the best I have ever made.
We recently needed to switch to gluten free foods and finding something to replace pizza has been our biggest challenge.  This product is perfect.  Thin crispy crust that is tasty and easy to make.

Blows all other GF pizza crust mixes out of the water.  My friends and family are more than happy to mow down on it over their traditional flour crust.  It is definitely important to spread the crust thin, as it will be a bit gummy if spread thick.  Namaste Foods has made pizza eating a joy all over again.
Gluten Free cooking can be quite a chore at times. Namaste pizza mix goes in the oven with little work and taste very good.I freeze leftover and heat up in oven.

This mix was an answer to a prayer for a frazzled mother of a 2 year old who was recently diagnosed as gluten sensitive and possibly celiac.  Of course pizza is one of his favorite foods.  The mix takes an extra step, but is worth the wait.  He loves it--in fact the whole family does.  It is more flaky like a pie crust, but the three boys don't mind.  It's all we use for pizza now.

This is the best gluten free pizza crust I have found. I am new to Celiac's disease and have been very disappointed with other crusts. This one has a lot of flavor and a relatively normal texture. I have yet to find another that comes close.

We are totally delighted with the Namaste Pizza Crust: the herb mixture adds a wonderful flavour burst, and the results from the oven let us enjoy pizza again after not being able to find a good gluten-free mix for a while.Bravo!  and Thank You! to the people at Namaste who offer this healthy and delicious product to us.

Since being diagnosed with Celiacs Disease, it's taken quite a while to find something that taste close to normal when it comes to pizza crust.  Namaste fits the bill.  Best I've ever had.  Thanks for providing a great product.Dan

I appreciate Namaste's line because the allergens they leave out are specifically the ones I'm avoiding, however, this pizza crust leaves A LOT to be desired.  The first three or four bites are pretty good at fooling you into thinking it's tasty, but as the crust cools it get gummier and less and less palatable.  I've tried it several times and will be throwing out the remaining mix.

My only complaint about this pizza crust is my family loves it as much as I do, and they're not required to follow a gluten-free diet. It's texture is wonderful, and the spices in the crust give my homemade pizza even more flavor.
If you are gluten free and missing pizza, this is your key.  It's great, you need to try it.

This is my family's favorite pizza crust...just made it tonight in fact and my 6 year old said it was the best pizza ever! But another way to use it is to batter chicken to make strips or nuggets. The recipe is on the side of the package. They are SO delicious!
We love this pizza crust.  It is the best mix we have found.  It has a focaccia bread taste because they put it some italian seasoning.  So good!

Needed a pizza dough which was gluten-free, dairy-free and yeast-free.  Most gluten-free included yeast.  I bought this hoping to "dress up" with enough toppings to overlook the limitations of the crust.  It is hands down the best mix of pizza crust we've ever had (gluten notwithstanding). I was growing tired of my regular oatmeal routine, and saw this on my grocer's shelf yesterday while shopping.I LOVE chocolate, but generally steer clear of most instant oatmeals because they lack that chewy, whole oat texture and are typically loaded up with things I'd prefer to not eat.This oatmeal has it all... a great texture, perfectly balanced dark chocolate flavor (with real chocolate morsels), an ingenious self-measuring pouch (for the water), and a terrific price point.I'm hoping Amazon will carry it soon, as I am already addicted to this delicious product!

I've been eating some of the BetterOats oatmeal options for the last several months.  When browsing on Amazon one day, I found that such a thing as chocolate oatmeal existed.  My heart nearly stopped.  How could it be that I had never heard of such glory?  BetterOats makes some delicious oatmeal options, however, after finally tasting this product, I can say that the the dark chocolate oatmeal is good but not great. If I had been unable to find this in a local grocery and I knew what it tasted like, there would be no way that I would purchase it for 13 to 17 dollars (as most Amazon vendors are commanding) for three boxes.  Some things to consider:1) Finding the product:  If you are flirting with the idea of buying this stuff online, I will say I was in the same boat.  I was tempted about three times to purchase it from vendors commanding quite a premium.  I held out hope I would find it for less and finally I did.  Meijer sells a box of five packets for 1.99 (look in the hot cereal section).2) The consistency of the product:  One thing I love about BetterOats is that all oatmeal products are packaged in a bag that has a fill line. The user uses the bag as a device to determine how much water is needed for the oatmeal. I'm one of those folks that always uses too little water, which leads to a gluey, unsatisfying mess. If you use the bag to measure the water you need, your oatmeal will never be dry or soupy.3) The flavor:  It's good.  It's not overly sweet and definitely not bitter.  I guess I expected more chocolate morsels, which a person could definitely add on their own.  It simply was not as decadent as I had hoped for.  I actually prefer the company's chai or peaches and cream options, which have relatively vibrant flavor profiles.4) The nutrition:  The calorie content surprised me in a good way.  A lot of the BetterOats options have 160 calories per bag.  The chocolate oatmeal also has 160 calories.  The ingredients are predictable for a chocolate oatmeal.  The first ingredient is whole grain rolled oats and the second is sugar.5) Power to satisfy:  I did not find this oatmeal to be as filling as other options offered by this company.  It really only held me over for two hours.  The company's other options usually get me through three - four hours.Ingredients: Organic whole grain rolled oats, sugar, chocoalte chips (sugar, chocolate liquor, cocoa butter, lecithin, vanilla), cocoa, flaxseed, salt, natural flavor, guar gum.

column9: McCormick Seasoned Meat Tenderizer a great product that is becoming hard to find.
column10: McCormick Seasoned Meat Tenderizer is one of the best meat tenderizers on the market. It has been around for countless years but as of late is becoming increasingly harder to find. It has many uses when cooking on the B.B.Q.! It is a key ingredient for making my meat come out great. I am constantly being asked by my friends and family why does my meat always come out so tasty. I tell them I always use McCormick Seasoned Meat Tenderizer. I have tried other brands but with much less stellar results.There is a special taste that is created by the use of McCormick Seasoned Meat Tenderizer. The key to success is to allow the meat to rise to room temperature then apply the tenderizer to both sides of the meat at least 20 minutes prior to grilling. You can either rub it on or sprinkle it on the meat and pierce with a fork like tenderizing it. I also like to add fresh cracked pepper and other spices then grill it to desired wellness.Another great use for McCormick Seasoned Meat Tenderizer is with B.B.Q. corn. My technique requires the following: 1/4 teaspoon or less McCormick Seasoned Meat Tenderizer, a pat of butter (cut size to taste), aluminum foil and a fresh ear of shucked corn. First tear a strip of aluminum foil long enough to wrap the corn at least two times around. Next cut the pat of butter and place it at the end of the strip of foil. Then sprinkle the McCormick Seasoned Meat Tenderizer over the butter. Finally take the freshly washed still dripping corn and place on top of the butter pat with tenderizer and roll up in the foil. Twist the ends shut and your are ready to B.B.Q. the corn. It is very important the corn be dripping wet. It is the moisture of the corn plus the little bit left from washing and butter that steams the corn as it cooks on the B.B.Q. I usually cook the corn turning every few minutes at least 5 to 10 minutes. You want to hear it sizzle as your turn it. It can burn so don't forget to turn if frequently. Be careful as you open the foil is is steaming hot and can burn!This method also works well for mushrooms, peppers and cut zucchini.Please ask your grocer or other shopping source to stock McCormick Seasoned Meat Tenderizer it is a really great product that there is truly not a good substitute for the unique taste it creates. It has been becoming increasingly more difficult to find lately so please ask of it.

column9: Good tasting hard candy, 90-95% like the fruit.
column10: Lychee [aka Litchi chinensis] is an Asian tropical fruit with a thin peel-able skin that comes in bunches like grapes.  The fruit itself has a diluted transparent milky white color and is very sweet with a slight hint of sourness.  The skin and the pit of the fruit is not eatable.  Kasagai has made this hard candy to taste 90-95% like the fruit, in my opinion.  This candy contains no actual fruit or fruit juice, unlike their gummy candies.  Bear in mind this is a hard candy, and is not a gummy candy, which they also make (that taste really like you're actually munching on fruit).  These are usually available in your local Asian Grocery stores, but can be a nice find from Amazon if you don't have one close to where you live.On the back of the actual plastic candy package, it is labeled "Manufactured on shared equipment that process MILK ingredients".  It is FYI for those of you with milk related product allergies to consider.The candy does taste good, and if you have a chance to taste the real fruit, you should give it a try, but until you get to eat the real fruit, this is a good alternative.

column9: Excellent Way to Stretch Budget, Improve Health
column10: Although I've been a vegetarian and even vegan at times in my life, currently I'm not.  I was so happy to find this great price on Bob's Red Mill TVP.  It's less than half of what I'd pay at my local grocery store--and only one of the stores in my area regularly even carries it.If you worry about both health and price, TVP is a great addition to your diet. I use it in conjunction with ground beef.  I rehydrate it using beef stock, and then add it to my ground beef.  If you're new to TVP, I'd start with rehydrating 1/4 to 1/2 cup and adding it to one pound of beef.  You can go up to a 50/50 blend--and most people will not be able to tell the difference, especially in things like chili and meatballs.  My kids and husband have no idea. :)If you buy the 80/20 ground beef--by mixing it with no-fat, high protein, high fiber TVP, you will halve the fat you eat per serving.  Because it doubles the amount of beef you get, you can also use this as a way to buy free-range or lower fat meat for your family.  Although $4 or $5/pound is a lot for many families--by cutting it with TVP, your true cost is $2-$2.50.  Much more affordable.I really recommend giving it a try. You can buy one cup at the bulk foods section of many health food stores to give it a try. Definitely hydrate it with beef stock for added flavor.  If your family likes it, then buy it on Amazon.  Good luck!

This is my first time using tvp. Tvp is really easy to prepare and inexpensive when compared to ground meat. It is very nutritional and it tastes good depending on how you prepare it.  The neat thing is it really does have a texture of meat when prepared as such...  I read a recipe the other day where someone made it taste like oatmeal... Very versatile... Great survival item to keep in your pantry or take camping... Soak in water until tender and use it any way you like...

I've never used TVP before this, so I wasn't sure quite what to expect when I purchased this product. So far I've used one whole bag and I couldn't be happier with it. My whole family enjoys eating the food I've made with TVP instead of ground beef, and so far I haven't noticed any stomach issues in anyone, even the baby. (And though I was a little unnerved by another reviewer's comment on the smell, I didn't really notice anything more than a subtle grain scent when I put my nose in the bag.)The first thing I did with my TVP was to take the liquid left from making a pot roast in my crockpot, skim away most of the fat, and use the liquid to rehydrate the TVP. It made a really delicious meatloaf-tasting crumble that we ate in sandwiches with ketchup. A few days later, I made a homemade spaghetti sauce with TVP simmered right in, and that turned out great too. I did notice that the TVP made the recipe just a little sweeter than it would've been, but I compensated with extra spices. I would leave the sugar out of the sauce recipe next time I make it with TVP. And last night, I rehydrated the last cup of TVP in the bag with water I'd mixed a packet of taco seasoning into. It made a very serviceable taco meat substitute for beefy taco macaroni and cheese.Just from my one bag, one quarter of my order, I got three meals for my family, which works out to less than seventy-five cents of TVP per meal. I don't know that I'll ever try to actually make a hamburger with this, but I just love it for any recipe calling for ground beef. Instead of defrosting and cooking a pound of beef, rehydrating a cup of TVP is fast and simple. I will definitely buy this again.
I add reconstituted tvp to ground beef.  There is no difference in taste.  It is a great way to add vegetable protein to our diet.

So I got this because a friend of mine mentioned it and I was all like, let's do this.  Well, the TVP Black Bean Enchiladas were the bomb!  If we hadn't told our other friend, I'm pretty sure he would have never known it wasn't beef or turkey.You have to use a recipe with some flavor in it.  We made ours with vegetable stock, but beef stock would help, if you are a meat eater just supplemented or reducing.  It makes a lot though.  One bag was half a bag too much for us, so watch your measurements, you might try a little less than it calls for.This is a great substitute for meat in things like enchiladas and spaghettis sauces and stuff.  Haven't tried combining it with real meat in a meatloaf or something to cut down on meat in stuff.  Maybe that's the next experiment...

Anything from Bob's Red Mill is great.  TVP is a great product to know how to use.  A great way to stretch your hamburger for tacos, meatloaf, etc.  Instead of adding plain water to soften, use a broth,  Extra flavor means great taste.  A healthy way to add soy to your diet.  This is a dried product and goes a long way, well worth the cost for the health benefits.

this stuff is nasty if you don't add a flavored liquid, like a stock or bullion cube.  in recipe, it takes on the flavor of soup, chili or stew and and i could not tell it was not meat.  my family ate it without question.  i have a case of this now and will add it to anything i cook using ground meat to add protein and texture.  just don't try to eat it reconstituted with hot water, not palatable by itself this way but i had to check what i was putting into my food!

column9: A staple for Vegetarian newcomers who still crave meat
column10: T.V.P., three wonderful letters known to most vegetarians. Let me say that I still eat meat (*gasp!*), but I am trying to transition to a vegetarian diet. Rather than going cold turkey (or cold tofu maybe?), I figured I'll try to work in one or two vegetarian meals into my week. That isn't so easy when you feel like there's nothing to satisfy that chew, that texture that only meat seems to exhibit. Enter Textured Vegetable Protein. When I first heart of it, I thought "what a weird sounding product". But reviews said it provides a meat-like texture in meals, and it was cheap, so I figured why not. While TVP may not look too appealing (soylent green anyone?), and the smell when raw is a bit unpleasant, it is a wonderful product. It really does have the texture of ground meat when reconstituted in boiling liquids. And just like tofu, it's a flavor sponge, adapting to any spice or flavor you throw at it (warning: throwing spices at something could be a messy affair). I've made tacos, chilli, used it for spaghetti and meatballs, and made some pretty good veggie burgers with it. I also took the suggestion of using it to extend the ground turkey I had in my house, so even my meat meals are turning vegetarian!I know I'm barely cracking the surface of what this stuff can be used for. I just want to say to any meat eater considering going the vegetarian route, it's not all gloom and doom. TVP will help you out. In fact, you can say TVP = The Vegetarian Pathway (I just made that up while typing, but it seemed fitting!). The value is great too; with Subscribe and Save, amazon's price is much cheaper than what I find at my local grocery store. This will be a staple in my pantry for quite some time. I'm already on my third order in fact.

I have to say that I am a bit biased when it comes to Bob's Red Mill products. I love everything they make and this TVP was no exception. This by far is the best deal around because I would pay far more at Whole Foods for the same brand. Quality means a lot along with taste, and Bob's Red Mill has both! Use this in place of all your ground beef/turkey recipes. I'm vegan and my family is not, they can't tell the difference when I make burgers, spaghetti or sloppy joe's. That's a good thing! Full of better nutrients than any meat could ever provide and this is much better for you. Do your own research then give this TVP a try. You will be satisfied. I liked this so much, I now have it on the "subscribe and save" here on Amazon!

column9: good protein source at a great price
column10: I used to purchase these at whole foods but found a much better price at Amazon

column9: Great Product, Easy to Add to Many Dishes, at a Great Price!
column10: I live in an area where vegetarianism is a rare thing, so it is difficult to find vegetarian products, and even more difficult to find them at a good price.  I was so glad I could find a great deal from Amazon and have it shipped right to my house! No more searching the spendy health food store for me!TVP is a wonderful product and much less expensive and more versatile than the pre-made vegi "crumbles" in the freezer section.  I can flavor this however I want, just throw it in some chili, make "taco meat" with it, make "BBQs" with it, and so much more.I haven't purchased TVP from other companies, but can say that I do like this brand of TVP, so I haven't really needed to search for any other kind.

Excellent product which I just discovered.  My family is not vegetarians or vegans, but can use this product as a meat extender. It's more healthful and a little meat mixed with this goes a long way. I made a spaghetti sauce with just the TVP, but something seemed lacking in flavor so I added a little bit of ground meat and the flavor improved. It was like a meatful spaghetti sauce, but actually it was a blend of about 80% TVP mixed with 20% beef. Now we can eat more healthy by reducing our meat consumption. I'll be thinking of more ways to use this product and will definitely keep this in my pantry.

This is a great price and product for small quantities of TVP. One meal per week using this as a meal stretcher will save the average family $10 per month on this product alone versus ground beef.Great in spaghetti, tacos, chili, and a wonderful way to add protein to soups and stews. I put a case every month inside my food storage program. To substitute for beef, redydrate with Beef Bouillon. FOr chicken,use Chicken Bouillon. If you're a vegetarian,use vegetable broth! LGW
I've been eating/using vegetarian products for years - this TVP works well, is healthy, and is inexpensive.  I use it in chili, soups, etc.

column9: Pretty good if you do it right.
column10: The product came promptly and as advertised. I have used it a few times once it was a mess and barely edible but that was my fault for not heating the water I used to soak it in. Not a bad product but nothing I would crave eating. It does a good job of adapting to the flavor so if you are looking for something that looks and feels like ground meat this fits the bill but do not expect it to have an outstanding flavor on its own you need to season it with hot broth or water on your own.
This is a great product for bariatric patients! A great source of protein in a small amount of food. When you can only eat a small amount of food and need a lot of protein this is great.

column9: Good way to get protein while cutting down on meat
column10: We're trying to eat less meat - but still love dishes like meatloaf, meatball soup, etc.  I've been using this TVP (plus some additional seasoning) to substitute for half the meat in some favorite recipes and both of us eat them happily, though it's taken a bit of experimenting to get quite the same taste and texture.  I look at dishes that call for plain TVP but am not so sure I'm ready to try them yetWhen a dietician told me I should to add more protein to my breakfast and suggested adding an egg (ugh - really don't like eggs), I tried adding a couple of tablespoons of it in my morning oatmeal.  It needs a bit of flavoring (cinnamon and/or raisins plus some stevia for sweetening) to keep from tasting like dog kibble, but with the flavoring it tastes great and I can really tell the difference in the amount of energy I have in the morning.

column9: TVP - alternative to meat and starchy carbs
column10: This stuff is amazing for my blood sugars and keeping them down when pasta, rice, bread make it skyrocket (unless eating less than 1/4 cup).  It's fun to experiment with it by adding spices/herbs and challenge myself with different recipes.It is also a great thing to replace with meat (since 99% turkey grounds can cost up to $7 a lb).  This stuff is cheap and 1 cup dry makes a hell of a lot of food.I use it so much I had to up the amount I purchase from Amazon.

I'm not a vegetarian but I do like to use TVP to extend and sometimes replace meat.  I've tried beef-flavored TVP from another company which I really like but the unflavored has the advantage of being very low sodium.  I've used Bob's Red Mill TVP in chili and tacos and both came out great.  I've tried a meatball recipe and I loved it, hubby not so much.  He likes the flavored stuff better, but I will keep some of this on hand to flavor any way I want.

column9: Great way to make ends meet.
column10: I thought it was too go to be true but I tried anyway. I made a meatloaf, chilli, hamburgers, and tacos with half burger and half TVP. Could not tell the difference. Glad I tried it. Easy on the budget and good source of fiber.

I rehydrate 1 cup of TVP with 1 cup of hot beef bouillon and move on with my Ground Beef "creations".  TVP handles savory and spicy additions very well ranging from Spicy Tacos, Robusto Tomato Sauce for macaroni/spaghetti, Red Beans and Rice, Rice Dressing... I'm so glad it's available on Amazon :)

This is something to always keep in your cupboard, this can be used to fix most crumbled beef recipes, such as stuffed peppers, meat loaf, chili, taco's etc. When seasoned properly and (I use beef bouillon or banquet bouquet), follow directions on package. This will cut your fat from meals, you can also use half ground beef and half TVP. The next day it tastes even better, and most people can't tell the difference. Just use your imagination and enjoy.I found this on Amazon at a very good price!

I bought this before finding out about how it is manufactured (using hexane). I need to do a bit more research before I decide whether or not I'd repurchase. That said, I really like the product itself. It is incredibly cheap (1 cup dried TVP + 1 cup boiling water or broth = about 3/4 pound) and has a slightly chewy texture that is reminiscent of meat, in my opinion. It really absorbs the flavor of whatever you cook it in, unlike tofu, which can be terribly bland if not marinaded. As a vegetarian, I like the versatility this affords me: basically any recipe that calls for ground meat can be made using an equal weight of hydrated TVP. I made sloppy joes with it the night it arrived, and hardly missed the meat. Veggie burgers, vegan chili, meatless bolognese, etc., are other good options. I have read that some eat it as sort of a breakfast porridge, and I can see how it would work (since the product itself is fairly flavorless), but I stuck with savory options.

First off, I was very apprehensive about trying this product, because I had tried the Harmony House brand of TVP (Beefish Bits), and I wasn't that pleased with it,  but their dehydrated veggies were just fine.  But, on to this review, Bob's Red Mill TVP is amazing :)  I tried my best to find something wrong with this TVP when I made some sample recipes like soy burgers and chilli, but I couldn't find anything wrong with either meals, and flavor and consistency was pretty spot on and tasted very good.  I still can't believe that this stuff really takes on the flavor of whatever you throw at it.  I'm happy I tried it and I plan to stock up on this TVP and keep some for emergency food supply.  I wish I had tried this months before now.  Could have saved me lots of money.  Thanks to all of you who left really detailed reviews that prompted my purchase.  If you're on the fence, just try it out, I'm certain you would like it very much.

I've made chili and spaghetti and both were really good.I rehydrated and added plain cocoa powder for the brown color,and Bragg's liquid amino acids for the beef flavor.Very good! Hubby even liked it : ) !

This is basically just soy flour with the fat removed. The result is textured vegetable protein, a great vegan substitute for ground beef (especially in light of the pink slime scandal), sausage, etc...We mostly use this for tacos and burritos in our home, and cooked into pasta. It is as simple to prepare as just throwing some in a hot skillet with water and whatever seasoning/vegetables/starch you are going to use and cooking until hot. For the subscribe & save price of under $9 for 4 packages, i also consider this to be a great deal. Things like TVP really make a vegan diet far more comprehensive and accessible. I love the stuff.Enjoy!

I used to get this in the grocery store, but it seems to be unavailable now. I am happy to find this product again. TVP - texturized vegetable protein - is a good protein substitute for any recipe calling for ground meat. It can be seasoned as you would any meat product. It is an economical replacement for meat, or can be used in combination with ground meat to reduce the fat, and the cost. We are  not vegetarians, but choose to eat more plant based meals for many reasons.  We enjoy using this high quality product. It is soy based.

Delicious in chili, spaghetti, tacos and anything you would put hamburger in.  It took about 1/4 of one bag for an entire pot of chili.  That's way less expensive than a couple pounds of hamburger.  We are now 100% plant-based diet and feel better than we ever have before!  My husband got to go off his cholesterol medicine and his counts have stayed low.  He also lost 10 pounds and we both feel great!!  Wooooohoooo!!  Thanks for having this great product so easy & inexpensive to buy!

Was so excited to receive this product. Living in a small town, it is hard to come by here, but now my meat loving husband requests this product instead of hamburger meat. I also love that it is ready in just a few short minutes. Taco meat is wonderful. I also haven't tried it but like the idea of stretching a buck by mixing in with hamburger meat. Recommend to everyone!

column9: An aid for healthy living and eating!
column10: Since the new year I have made a vow to start eating  for a healthier lifestyle. My doctor last year told me I am morbidly obsese and  a BMI near 50. I am tall, but there is no reason for me to be this big. As apart of my new lifestyle,I adopted a low carb lifestyle CHANGE not DIET . I have replaced my cabinet with coconut flour, almond meal and have eaten shirataki noodles to replace my noodle fettish. Most recently after reading the review, I have purchased this product from my grocery store. I had TVP before and it was good, but just didn't know the name of it and that it was so readily available as it is. I am cooking my TVP (first time)  with my shirataki noodles as I am typing this. I sampled this and it is delicious . As a result of a month on this low carb diet, I have lost nearly twenty pounds. Get this product, it is low carb as well as it adapts to any dish. It is essential to healthy living, and it is cheap if not cheaper as getting ground beef,or chicken breasts from the store and it doesn't have that saturated fat. I look forward to updating my review to say that I have successfully trimmed my carbs and fat from my diet.

My local Whole Foods decided not to carry TVP and after my initial dissapointment, was thrilled to find this at Amazon-I like this brand of TVP because it workd well with everything- I add it my dog's home made food,homemade granola, vegetable or tofu dishes- it takes on savory or sweet seasonings and holds up well

column9: Bob's has very good TVP quality
column10: I have always found Bob's products to be high quality. The TVP is a great addition to my vegan chili and it works well. I am satisfied, but don't use too much or it will overwhelm the dish. As a supplement to dishes where you need some protein, it fits the bill perfectly.

I tried it the past weekend in Yosemite to cook with Kitchen of India's vegetable curry paste.  It tasted fantastic! No yucky soy taste at all and super fast and easy to rehydrade.I also bought Santa Fe Bean Company's instant fat free refried black beans.  I can see what a great backpacking dinner it will be combining half a cup of TVP and half cup of instant beans.I can also see it being used in ground meat, added in canned soup, and in any dish that requires a bit of thickening.  It soaks up flavor very well.  Such fast and clean protein should be in everybody's pantry, just in case, you know?

This is a great replacement for ground beef. It is very reasonably priced. My family of 4 gets 3 meals out of each bag and Amazon has the cheapest price, especially when you subscribe. This has reduced our meat intake significantly, as we no longer buy ground beef. I only wish Bob's Red Mill would make TVP chunks so that we could have a diced chicken replacement. Are you listening Bob?

I was very pleasantly surprised at how good this is.  I am not vegan, but use this many times in place of ground meat as it picks up the flavor of what it is placed in to regenerate from a dry to moist product.  Bob's Red Mill scores another one.

I adored this product years ago when I was looking for low-carb sources of protein as an alternative to meat - I tried a lot of tofu products & soy protein products.This was a great way to make an easy meal or snack with texture & versatility (all you do it soak it in hot water, then add whatever else you want). Low-fat, low-carb, high-protein. I thought soy was the bee's knees until I learned it inhibits thyroid function, which I already have a problem with.If you have normal thyroid function or are even high-thyroid, enjoy TVP! If you have low-thyroid problems, reconsider your consumption of soy products. :( Sadly.

column9: Makes a very good  hot cereal
column10: I'm just starting to eat low carb and I was getting tired of eggs already.But I stumbled across this recipe at [...] for TVP Oatmeal and I find it to be quite good. Very easy to make and I'm a very lazy bachelor.I made a full batch and now can just add some extra soy milk and reheat it in the microwave. Jazz it up with lots of cinnamon, etc.Update. This also works very well as a filler for your low carb meatloaf. I add one cup to the recipe.

I became a vegetarian in July of 2010 and thought I would never have Meatballs, sloppy joes, chili, tacos, enchiladas or any of the other hamburger dishes i have loved all my life.  I suffered for about two months and then I found TVP and WOW now i'm a happy girl again.  I love getting it from Amazon. Very fast delivery and very nicely priced.  I didnt believe it would ever compare with ground beef, chicken or turkey but boy was I wrong. In fact I honesty can say i prefer TVP over anything else.  I just hope Amazon never stops carrying this product.  Highly recommend :-)

Plain TVP, without flavoring or other ingredients added, really doesn't vary so much between brands. It's always going to be on the mushier side if you try to, say, make a burger with TVP alone. And it's going to absorb the flavor of whatever broth, seasonings or other foods you're cooking it with.I try to keep this product on-hand because it's a quick, easy and inexpensive way to keep protein around. Added to rice with seasonings, a splash of oil, broth and a bit of hot sauce, it's a quick, easy and relatively complete meal. Add veggies, extra broth and eggs, and you have a hearty, flavorful soup. It's versatile and the price here is excellent.

column9: Bob's Red Mill TVP (Textured Vegetable Protein), 10-Ounce Bags (Pack of 4)
column10: Bob's Red Mill TVP (Textured Vegetable Protein), 10-Ounce Bags (Pack of 4)- fast delivery with amazon prime- extremely high quality TVP, great taste- good price

Perhaps it speaks to my cooking skills, but so far this product has been just meh to me.  I can't seem to liven it up.  It just seems like a rubbery intrusion in my soup or pasta dishes.  I will raise my rating if I can get better at incorporating more flavor into the soy beads.

TVP does not have much flavor (slightly nutty) on its own but the texture is important and the Bob's Red Mill is as it should be.  Prepared according the the label instructions, the TVP has a very ground beef like texture.We use it for taco's, burritos, and as a meat substitute/filler when making meatloaf for my boys.  They don't even realize it is in there.The prices seems right compared to other sources.

This is truly a universal product. I am not a vegetarian, yet my girlfriend is. It is a great substitute for ground beef in dozens of meals I make. I pour it into my chili, make tacos with it, and it is great in spaghetti sauce. Very easy to make and very filling, also, a great price!

First, I would like to note that this is an all soy product, so those with gluten issues should find it readily digestible.  It is made from defatted soy beans, so it is also fa free - if that is an issue for you.  I have used this to make sloppy joes, chili, taco filling, bbq sandwich filling, and burgers.  My 74 year old mother, who never eats vegetarian, had one of the burgers and loved it.  The four pack is an excellent value.  Each bag provides about 12 protein servings.  I have found that I get the tastiest results re-hydrating the granules with Better than Bouillon vegetable base and/or mushroom base (available here on Amazon).  Tomato juice is another excellent option.  The dry granules are more or less flavorless - so using a well seasoned liquid gives a much better final result.  Even if you don't eat vegetarian or vegan, this is still an excellent product to use.  Rehydrate one cup of granules and mix with 1 pound of ground meat and mix up as for a 2# meatloaf.  But don't bake it in a loaf pan - you get a better result by making individual patties or more of a broad flat slab.  Baking in a loaf format everything cooks thoroughly but tends to be too soft to be truly satisfying.  There isn't a lot to say about this product except it is wholesome economical and very easy to use.  If you are trying to lower your grocery bill, this is a very good option.
I mix this 1 to 1 with Bob's Red Mill Organic Oat Bran Hot Cereal and it makes for a winning breakfast combo. Everyone who tries it at my house loves it.

column9: Great Adkins Diet Replacement for Oatmeal!
column10: There are many recipes out there for using TVP as a replacement for oatmeal if you are an oatmeal lover and on a carb restricted diet - such as I am.  Is it perfect?  No but darn close and I use alot of cinammon, splenda and ALmond Milk / cream - it's great!!

column9: Great product for a great price!!
column10: I used this to make my own lower-fat version of turkey italian sausage and hamburger crumbles. For both, I hydrated the TVP before mixing with the meat.  For turkey italian sausage, I added 2 cups of warm water to two cups of TVP, then mixed with two pounds of ground turkey. To this I added minced garlic, italian seasonings, salt, ground pepper, and fennel seed.  You can also add dried red pepper if you like a hot version.  I let it sit in a covered bowl in the refrigerator overnight so the flavors could blend.  The next day, I browned the whole lot and divided the mixture into 5 quart sized freezer bags.  When I want to make a dish with crumbled Italian sausage, I just pull a bag from the freezer.  For ground beef, I also did a one cup TVP to one pound ground beef mixture, browned with a little garlic powder, salt and pepper, and stored crumbles in the freezer.  This lowers my grocery bill for meat, makes throwing something together for dinner a lot quicker (which keeps me away from the fast food places), and lowers the fat content of our meals.  What could be better than that???

column9: Easy Vegan Substitute for Ground Beef!
column10: TVP is one of my 'OMG I have to make supper in 10 minutes' saviors!  I can whip up a quick batch of TVP tacos in no time flat.  So fast and easy plus I love the taste!  I sometimes have a hard time getting my kids to eat my healthy vegan cooking, but they love my vegan tacos.  Definitely a must have for any vegan mom!  Subscribe & save pricing is excellent.

This stuff makes a great filling meal. I eat a lot of vegetable soup which I really like but it just isn't that filling. Now I just add a cup of tvp to my soup and it becomes a hearty stew. I also like adding this to my pasta sauce. I am vegetarian and I find this a great alternative for meat. The texture is great and if you hydrate this with some type of sauce or bouillon it takes on a great flavor. Super easy to cook with and turns out great.

column9: An Essential Ingredient for Vegans who miss Ground Style Beef
column10: Before I became a Vegan I had never heard of Textured Vegetable Protein, now it's my favorite ingredient!  I use it in a lot of recipes from my favorite Vegan Cook Book, The Happy Herbivore Cookbook: Over 175 Delicious Fat-Free and Low-Fat Vegan Recipes.  Makes great TVP Tacos, TVP Ground Beef and Bacon Bits.  My Wife and I went through the whole case in 6 weeks!

column9: Better than the Whole Foods Version
column10: I used to buy TVP in the bulk section at Whole Foods, but I use a lot and the price was too high.  Bob's Red Mill makes excellent TVP, and it even tastes a little sweeter (very subtly) than the other brand I used.  I love it and the price is right!  Great vegan staple and YUMMY in baked ziti!

Good product with discount for standing repeat order and free shipping from Amazon is a premium opportunity. I have always been treated extremely well and if any errors arise are always treated with quick courteous corrections.

TVP or textured vegetable protein is not a meat product but has protein 12g per 1/4 cup no cholesterol, 7g of carbs per same 1/4 cup of TVP and of course fiber as TVP is made from soybeans. Rehydrated, with whatever liquid you choose, this product is cheaper than ground meat, and can be used in nearly every recipe one would use ground meat.Costs of TVP are better than ground meat in the stores. As it has a great shelf life there is no extra cost of refrigeration or freezing.  Since TVP has a great shelf life and is therefore a good traveler. May be used camping; add some to a stew of veggies or when meat might be low or scarce in the pot. I enjoy TVP in chili and as "hamburgers" made with TVP and beans of my choice. Find your own great recipe and try some TVP.

I have purchased Bob's products for years and enjoy all of them.  They are high-quality! I eat oatmeal everyday and use Muesli as an add-in to the plain old-fashioned type. It is generously packed with almonds, raisins and dates. Yum! I've also eaten it cold with Almond milk and enjoy it that way too.

column9: Peanut and Tree Nut Allergy Sufferers Beware
column10: I can't say anything about the quality, taste, texture, touch, smell, substance or general quality of this product. Unfortunately, I found out only after ordering and receiving this product that it was "manufactured in a facility that uses tree nuts and soy." While I appreciate the fact that the manufacturers mention this on the packaging, it would have helped me greatly to have this information noted on the product information page. I just now checked the Amazon page again and there is no mention of this incredibly important information. For those of you without family members that suffer from peanut and tree nut allergies, go for it, but for the many of us that do live with these challenges, steer clear of this product. I would also hesitate to purchase any other products from this manufacturer without first verifying with them that product was not manufactured in a facility that uses tree nuts. !!!Wait!! Just checked their website and there's not a single reference to allergens (other than gluten) in their products. Actually, they seem to have a rather ample offering of products of gluten-free goods, but this does little for those with other allergies. Lastly, I don't expect every product to be free of peanuts and tree nuts, but I do expect the manufacturer to make it known to me if they have these ingredients in their products or are using a facility where these ingredients are used in other products. Unfortunately, Bob's Red Mill has done neither for their website or for their product page on Amazon. While I could return the product in another box (original one was already thrown out), it is too much trouble/hassle to do so. Thanks Bob!!

column9: I haven't smelled anything like this since leaving the chicken farm
column10: I've heard a lot of good things about TVP and have enjoyed other Red Mill products, but if all TVP is this horrid then it'll never find a place in my pantry again. The directions called for rehydrating 1 cup of TVP with 7/8 cup boiling water. As soon as the boiling water hit the TVP a smell exactly the same as chicken poo came wafting up from the bowl. All the bowl contained was TVP and boiling water but the smell made me gag. I covered the bowl with a plate while the TVP soaked for 10 minutes as directed on the package. When I removed the cover the smell burst forth like chicken poo from hell! I hoped the smell would go away when I added the TVP to the pasta, red sauce, and mushrooms but it didn't. Eventually I had to add a lot of extra oregano, basil, rosemary, and Parmesan cheese to only barely cover the smell and taste of the TVP. This has got to be one of the worst things I've ever tried and this is from a guy who cooks and eats June bugs!

column9: For The Best Cup of Brewed Tea Ever
column10: Bushell's tea is superior to all the others. It is a strong black tea with rich flavor. Because the leaves are finely cut, a little goes a long way. With a little half and half and a sprinkling of sweetener, your worries can be driven away by a cup of this great tea.Paula

column9: Make this your only stock and store
column10: Once upon a mid-day sunny, while I savored Nuts 'N Honey,With my Tuscan Whole Milk, 1 gal, 128 fl. oz., I sworeAs I went on with my lapping, suddenly there came a tapping,As of some one gently rapping, rapping at the icebox door.'Bad condensor, that,' I muttered, 'vibrating the icebox door -Only this, and nothing more.'Not to sound like a complainer, but, in an inept half-gainer,I provoked my bowl to tip and spill its contents on the floor.Stupefied, I came to muddle over that increasing puddle,Burgeoning deluge of that which I at present do adore -Snowy Tuscan wholesomeness exclusively produced offshore -Purg'ed here for evermore.And the pool so white and silky, filled me with a sense of milkyArdor of the type fantastic of a loss not known before,So that now, to still the throbbing of my heart, while gently sobbing,I retreated, heading straightway for the tempting icebox door -Heedless of that pitter-patter tapping at the icebox door -I resolved to have some more.Presently my soul grew stronger; hesitating then no longer,'This,' said I, 'requires an extra dram of milk, my favorite pour.'To the icebox I aspired, motivated to admireHow its avocado pigment complemented my decor.Then I grasped its woodgrain handle - here I opened wide the door; -Darkness there, and nothing more.Deep into that darkness peering, long I stood there wondering, fearing,Doubting, dreaming dreams of Tuscans I had known beforeBut the light inside was broken, and the darkness gave no token,And the only words there spoken were my whispered words, 'No more!'Coke and beer, some ketchup I set eyes on, and an apple core -Merely this and nothing more.Back toward the table turning, all my soul within me burning,Soon again I heard a tapping somewhat louder than before.'Surely,' said I, 'surely that is something at my window lattice;Let me see then, what thereat is, and this mystery explore -Let my heart be still a moment and this mystery explore; -'Tis the wind and nothing more!'From the window came a stirring, then, with an incessant purring,Inside stepped a kitten; mannerlessly did she me ignore.Not the least obeisance made she; not a minute stopped or stayed she;But, with mien of lord or lady, withdrew to my dining floor -Pounced upon the pool of Tuscan spreading o'er my dining floor -Licked, and lapped, and supped some more.Then this tiny cat beguiling my sad fancy into smiling,By the grand enthusiasm of the countenance she wore,Toward the mess she showed no pity, 'til I said, 'Well, hello, kitty!'Sought she me with pretty eyes that seemed to open some rapport.So I pleaded, 'Tell me, tell me what it is that you implore!'Quoth the kitten, 'Get some more.'

He always brought home milk on Friday.After a long hard week full of days he would burst through the door, his fatigue hidden behind a smile. There was an icy jug of Tuscan Whole Milk, 1 Gallon, 128 fl oz in his right hand. With his left hand he would grip my waist - I was always cooking dinner - and press the cold frostiness of the jug against my arm as he kissed my cheek. I would jump, mostly to gratify him after a time, and smile lovingly at him. He was a good man, a wonderful husband who always brought the milk on Friday, Tuscan Whole Milk, 1 Gallon, 128 fl oz.Then there was that Friday, the terrible Friday that would ruin every Friday for the rest of my life. The door opened, but there was no bouyant greeting - no cold jug against the back of my arm. There was no Tuscan Whole Milk in his right hand, nor his left. There came no kiss. I watched as he sat down in a kitchen chair to remove his shoes. He wore no fatigue, but also no smile. I didn't speak, but turned back to the beans I had been stirring. I stirred until most of their little shrivelled skins floated to the surface of the cloudy water. Something was wrong, but it was vague wrongness that no amount of hard thought could  give shape to.Over dinner that night I casually inserted,"What happened to the milk?""Oh,"he smiled sheepishly, glancing aside,"I guess I forgot today."That was when I knew. He was tired of this life with me, tired of bringing home the Tuscan Whole Milk, 1 Gallon, 128 fl oz. He was probably shoveling funds into a secret bank account, looking at apartments in town, casting furtive glances at cashiers and secretaries and waitresses. That's when I knew it was over. Some time later he moved in with a cashier from the Food Mart down the street. And me? Well, I've gone soy.

column9: Chateau du Lait Blanc, watch out!
column10: One should not be intimidated by Tuscan Whole Milk. Nor should one prejudge, despite the fact that Tuscan is non-vintage and comes in such large containers. Do not be fooled: this is not a jug milk. I always find it important to taste milk using high-quality stemware -- this is milk deserving of something better than a Flintstones plastic tumbler.  One should pour just a small dollop and swirl it in the glass -- note the coating and look for clots or discoloration. And the color -- it should be opaque, and very, very white. Now, immerse your nose in the glass and take a whiff. Tuscan transports you instantly to scenic hill towns in central Italy (is that Montepulciano I detect?) --- there is the loamy clay, the green grass of summer days, the towering cypress.  And those gentle hints of Italian flowers -- wild orchids, sunflowers, poppies. Then, one takes in the thick liquid and lets it roll across and under the tongue -- what is that? perhaps a hint of a nutty Edam cheese?  With Tuscan, you feel the love of every dairyperson involved -- from the somewhat sad and deranged farmhand shovelling steaming cowpies to the bored union milk maiden dreaming of leaving this soul crushing life behind for a job waiting tables for obnoxious American tourists in Siena.  But not too fast -- sip gently, slowly, or one is in danger of not only missing the subtleties of the milk's texture and its terroir, but -- if chilled too long -- also of giving oneself a blinding ice cream headache. Nay, savor the goodness that only dairymen and dairywomen working at the apex of their craft can deliver. Tuscan is best drunk young -- no, no, don't cellar this gem -- I guarantee you'll be sorry if you do.  I recommend pairing with freshly baked macadamia nut scones. Milk Expectorator gives this one a 92.

column10: I approached the Airport Security Gate and fed my bags into the x-ray machine."Sir," said the TSA agent, "is this your bag?""You know it is," I replied."There's no need to get testy sir," he said.The agent escorted me over to a side table."Do you mind if I search your bag?"  he asked."What will you do if I say no?" I asked."I'll take you in the back room and we'll strip search you," he replied."Then by all means, go ahead and search," I said.The agent opened my bag and peered inside."What do you call this sir?" the agent asked holding up a pair of nail clippers."Those are nail clippers," I said."I'm going to have to confiscate these," he said."That's alright," I replied, "they sell them for a dollar in the store next to my departure gate."The agent looked at me with hate in his eyes.  He looked back into my bag and pulled out my gallon of Tuscan Whole Milk."Sir, you can't take this on the plane," he said."Why not?" I asked."Because, if you have more than three ounces of a liquid you could use it to blow up the plane," he said.I was astonished. I had no idea that Tuscan Whole Milk was so powerful."May I drink it now?" I asked."Yes," he said, "liquids are harmless once they are inside of you."I drank the entire gallon of Tuscan Whole Milk that I had purchased on Amazon.com while the people behind me grew increasingly inpatient.It was delicious.I did not blow up.

column9: PRETTY GOOD, BUT NOT LIKE PIZZA CRUST
column10: BOTTOM LINEIf you are expecting a rising pizza crust, such as what you might get from standard pizza dough, then you'll need to look elsewhere.  That being said, these are pretty good in their own right.TASTEI rather like the way these pizza crusts taste after being toasted up.  They soak in flavor from sauce or cheese well, without becoming soggy or wilted.  They have a good bread flavor on their own, also, and make a good base for a BBQ chicken or BBQ pulled pork pizza.TEXTUREI think the texture is the only thing I can complain about with these - the Schar Crusts are a little more dense than I would like.  However, this is a usual complaint about all gluten-free items.SIZEThese are definitely personal pizza sized.  With sauce, cheese, and toppings on this crust, I can usually eat about 1/2 to 3/4 of a pizza on my own.USES/ VERSATILITYIf you can expand your mind beyond making just pizza with red sauce and mozzarella, then these crusts are quite useful.  I personally love them with some BBQ sauce and chicken.  They make a nice bread/ carb base for anything I might otherwise eat on flatbread.  As a gluten-free option, these crusts are a wonderful thing to have at your disposal.

This tea is excellent. It's strong, malty, and robust. I was looking for a strong black tea with which I could mix milk and sugar. This is it. It's ground very fine and dry. I pay about $5/pound at my local Indian market, so it's a great deal. Much better than Twinnings or other black teas that you find at the local supermarket.
all was good they even send me a bigger bag of tea for the same price. thank you for good service and good tea ..luis e from florida
This is a very good product even for those without diabetes. I like the taste of the wintergreen flavor, also the smell when you open the bag. Great price and good shippingcost.
These are among our favorite treats! We keep themon hand at all times, in the car, in the purse,everywhere. They taste so good you can not tellthey are sugar free. We love them!
These individually wrapped items are just so Fresh,,,and the Wint-o-Green are  very minty and cool .like a Winters Snow.I will definitely purchase this product again.
These are so freaking delicious. I hope they never switch to Sucralose(which ruined the Fruit Flavor ones for me). The Sorbets were amazing too but they discontinued those.

My husband and I love the sugar free Wintergreen Livesavers but we have by them by the small pack and they are not that cheap if you use at least one pack a week.  I happened to see this product on your site and was thrilled because it saves us $7.00 and I don't have to buy it every week.
These are also great for low carb dieters when you are craving that sweet candy!

sugar free lifesaver mints in peppermint or winto/spearmint are great for snack instead of eating what i really want to eat - which would inevitably be overly-caloric. Aside from that, they taste good, are nicely-protected by good packaging, and are at a reasonably-good price from Amazon
These were purchased for a dibetic. The price was right, cheaper than the Super Market.  Very satisfied!

column9: Love these & they are Sugar Free!!
column10: Sugar free and sensational! Try them! You can't tell them from the ones with sugar.

I've enjoyed the flavor of witer green since I was young. Finding these mints in a sugar free product is great. There are several individually wrapped mints in each of the several bags in this order, and they should last me quite awhile. I consider this to have been a very good purchase.
These are great. I cannot even really tell the difference between these and regular sugar ones. A great little snack.
I had a problem finding these sugar-free products locally for awhile and ordered them from Amazon.  The order was quick and I had no problems.Thank you
I finally found something tiny enough to use as a male pleasure toy. They also leave a super tingly sensation on my male part... oh yes.

I am addicted to this product and was so happy that I could get it through Amazon at a great price ($19.50) and it was eligible for free shipping. Now the price has gone up almost $3 and it is no longer eligible for free shipping because now it is shipped and sold through ABC Wholesale and not Amazon. However the 5 flavor and Pepomint flavors are still the lower price and still eligible for free shipping. Now I am back to buing this product at Target!

I'm not sure why everybody else rated these so high. The taste and texture is like Certs, crumbly and unpleasantly overpowering. They may or may not have wintergreen oil like the originals(natural flavor can mean just about anything) but if they do, I sure can't taste it. I was really hoping these would be like the originals and be so hard they almost break your teeth when you bite them and have such a strong wintergreen flavor that they burn your tongue. Didn't happen. I'm very glad I bought one bag of these to try instead of buying the 12 pack on here. I'm guessing all the other reviewers haven't had the originals in a VERY long time. That's the only way I can see giving them 5 stars. I gave it 3 only because they are still edible, if you like Certs. I don't.

column9: Ok, but Jade can be so much better
column10: This is an okay tea. A good enough everyday oolong for casual drinking. Compared to other teas, I'd even say it's pretty good.But it is by no means a fantastic delight of the senses, as I've come to expect from jade oolongs. Rishi Jade Oolong is my favorite, with a heavenly flowery aroma and flavor; most all jades I've sampled are better than SerendipiTea. This tea looks very pretty, a healthy green that brews a yellow liquid, the tiny curled leaves that open and get a lot of volume (a pleasure to watch), but it doesn't smell like anything (well, it does a little, if I sniff inside the cup) and the flavor is nice enough but bland. Nothing to write home about.I'd try something else instead.

I like this tea very much.  It has a soft, quiet flavour - exactly what I want at times when I reach for this tea over other, more dramatic teas.  I'm also enchanted by the tightly wrapped full tea leaves as they unfurl in the hot water, a visual as well as olfactory pleasure.
Got a bag with a few bad ones in it. They were really bitter. Overall they taste about right. I've had better organic almonds, That cost more. The texture is perfect.

column9: Best black olives in brine I've ever eaten.
column10: I'm glad they have them in my supermarket in South Florida because the price here is a bit high and the shipping/handling charge is unbelievable.  My supermarket sells the 7.4 oz. jar for $3.59 and I would probably pay even a tad more than that, they're that good, but $10 seems a bit much.The black olives come from Peru.  They are large and plump and nicely solid, not at all mushy or wrinkled.  Packed in a saltwater brine, they do have a sodium content that's a bit high, and lactic acid and potassium sorbate are added as preservatives, so if you're a purist about your food these may not suit you.  I'm usually careful about what I eat, but these are so good and I'm such an olive lover that I don't think about the sodium and preservatives when I eat them.
At first was not sure about roasted peppers in can,that did not have an Italian name.So i took a chance bought them.Love these roasted peppers.

My 100 pound standard poodle developed A-Typical Addison's Disease and quit eating dog food...even Blue Buffalo. With this disease, they can lose a lot of  weight so I was feeding him anything I could make to help him gain weight.  He would turn his nose up at any dog food I brought in.  He was eating better than my kids.  I finally found this and he is back to eating dog food.  It smells fresh and for me, though it is a bit expensive, he likes it and it saves me time cooking or making raw food for him.

I was concerned that I would receive boxes of broken crackers, but they were completely intact. These saltines have a lighter consistency than most ... more delicate and less course salt on the tops. Very nice!

Disappointing- crackers were shipped in a box without any protective packing either on bottom or top, just on the sides.  Cracker packages arrived slip open and thus crackers were both stale and broken.  Amazon usually does a better job than this.  Not a bargain when the crackers can't be used.

I debated a while before ordering these because they are kind of fragile, but my shipment had no problems. Ha, maybe I'd trust Amazon and UPS more than the people they've got working down at the grocery store.Another reason I debated ordering was of course, the salt, and of course being "SALTines", there's a bunch of it. I haven't compared a lot of other snacks, but strangely enough these have less salt that other alternatives. I guess because there's no other tastes that they have to mask, the little bit of salt the do have comes right on through. I don't normally worry about such things as health and nutrition, but 12 boxes is a lot, and I tend to chow down on a lot of them because they're so good!Plenty of time left on the expiration date, 8 months from now, so that's not a worry.Prices, as with everything, fluctuate, but I got a good deal.

column9: It seems to be what it says it is.
column10: This is the first bottle of cola syrup that I have purchased.  I used it with DIY carbonated water to make a standard "cola beverage".  I'm not much of a cola drinker, so I can't tell you that it tastes like some product or not.  Overall, the taste is undeniably "cola" and there is something magic about turning tap water into bubble cola in my kitchen.  The cane sugar and the no caffeine factor are each a bonus.

I received this cheese as part of my igourmet cheese of the month membership.  There have been some amazing offerings from them in this collection, however this was not one of them.  I often find goat cheese to be a hit or miss product, but I've never tasted one as bad as this.  In all honesty, I found it borderline inedible.  I will never try it again if at all possible.  Truly, shockingly bad.

These treats are perfect for any dog, because they are pure and natural. Nothing in them but the sweet potato. My dog has severe food allergies, and they're about the only treat she can have. Fortunately, she loves them, and tolerates them well. They were very fresh too; the sweet potato smell that wafted out of the package when I opened it was just like freshly-picked produce. The best part is that I got them for half what I paid for a smaller bag at the big chain pet food store, shipping included! I'll be buying from this seller for a long time to come.

column9: My 4 month old puppy loves these. His favorite.
column10: These are great chews. Healthy and fun for my puppy dog.  Wish they lasted longer because they are quite expensive.
I found a bottle deep inside my closet with a best use date of July 10 2008.  It is now Sept 28, 2011.  It was still good and still tasted great on my fish sticks.

column9: Awesome - healthy - not high sodium or sugar at all
column10: Know how you have to sacrifice carbs, sugar, salt at unacceptable limits in exchange for the "fat free" brand or even sacrifice taste? Not with this product. I love love love this -- plus you don't need tons to get the flavor you seek if you are a true tartar sauce lover and enjoy having it on sandwiches, in salads or accompanying your favorite seafood, this is a fat free version you can enjoy as much as your favorite full-fat/unhealthy brand. Just try locating it in your grocer tho... a whole other story. I've was disappointed that I can no longer find it along with several other favorite foods in my local grocers... I guess they expect us in the south to succumb to the high salt, high fat foods "only"...sigh.

i guess its due, at least in part, to compensate for the fact that they are the low fat varieties, but it seems like fat free salad dressings and sauces tend to go overboard with the amount of flavorings they add. this is no exception. i like dipping or stirring in a little tartar sauce, and thought might as well get the fat free kind... tastes more like tartar sauce concentrate!
$7.09 for one piece (as of Sept 2011) can only be an error, I hope. I love this product but usually get mine in Germany for like $0.80 per piece. I hope this gets corrected soon.
Guess for all those desparate Germans living in the states - get it in Germany @ less than one $
This is a great product for making your very own schnitzel (breaded pork tenderloin) at home. Easy to use, directions are in German, but fairly easy to translate.

column9: Really Good Sugar Free Candies - Recommended!
column10: Being diabetic, I am always on the watch for sugar free snacks. The "GoLightly Hard Candy" is a great addition to my snaking list.At only 45 calories and 0 Net Carbs for 4 pieces, these do not impact my blood sugar levels or ruin my diet. These are sweetened with Splenda, so they are slightly less sweet than regular candies, but do not cause the "laxative" effect other dietetic candies can have.There are serveral types of available and they are all good!Highly recommended!

I'd been given a couple of the chocolate mint Golightly candies by a friend, and was surprised at how good these sugar-free candies were.  When I found them available on Amazon I couldn't decide which of the flavors to buy, so I went for the chocolate assortment.  All the flavors in this assortment are great.  It's hard to believe this candy is sugar-free -- slightly less sweet than sugary candy, but very a very satisfying snack.

column9: GOLIGHTLY Sugar-Free  Just Chocolates Hard Candy
column10: These sugarless candies have wonderful, true chocolate taste with no nasty aftertaste.  Very refreshing and satisfying.  I highly recommend these to anyone who wants something sweet without sugar, like myself.

column9: Great flavor and no added sugar!
column10: As a recently diagnosed diabetic, and as a pastor's wife who occasionally fasts from sugar for spiritual reasons, I have become an avid label reader and sugar avoider. To my delight, there is no added sugar in this product, and the flavor is great.  We have used it as a seasoning dressing for pasta salad, cowboy caviar, and other recipes utilizing italian dressing, all with good results.  On a regular lettuce salad, it is delicious. I pray they never keep making it! Ingredients (not in order of label) are water, red wine vinegar & distilled vinegar, olive oil & extra virgin olive oil, soybean and/or canola oil, onion, salt, spice, garlic, lemon juice. 60 calories in 2 Tbsp., 50 from fat, 1 gram sugars, 260 mg sodium, 0 cholesterol, 0 carbs, 6 g total fat, 1 g sat fat, 0 g trans fat. Enjoy!

I absolutely love this dressing!  I've even started eating the $1 salad off the McDonald's menu because this dressing is soooo good.  Yikes...Up till now I never tipped my salad bowl to get the last remaining dressing, but I found myself doing it.  ;o)

This item is actually "Light Italian" dressing and there is nothing about "Limone" in the name when you get the bottles. The photo is misleading.  Don't order this thinking it is like the Lime Vinaigrete, or like a lemon juice based Italian.

As I said in my review of their lumache (which Amazon misspells "lamache" as of May 2011), I discovered the Cavalieri brand through a marvelous Italian movie named Loose Cannons (Mine vaganti). My five-star review of the lumache was slightly tentative because I was not sure the quality of the product justified its being ten times as expensive as supermarket pasta, but - Oh, my! - I have no such reservations about the spaghettoni.The list price of Benedetto Cavalieri pasta seems to be around ten dollars per 500-gram package (a little more than a pound), although it is somewhat less expensive here at Amazon. I would not think ten dollars for a pound of steak was exorbitant, and this pasta is better than steak. Besides, pasta more than doubles in weight when boiled, so it is actually less than five dollars for a pound of edible pasta.I have to boil it slightly longer than the instructions prescribe (about 18 minutes instead of 15-16) to get it to what I consider al dente (which means it is chewy but does not crack when I bite it), but that is an insignificant complaint. Maybe true pasta connoisseurs expect it still to be hard enough in the center to crack when bitten; I don't.I also have only tried Cavalieri pasta with a little butter and salt, because that is how I like pasta best. If I were going to smother it in a sauce, even in a mild sauce like Alfredo, I probably would use Wegmans excellent store-brand pasta (seventy-nine cents a pound) instead. It would be a waste to mask this pasta with ANYTHING.I hereby officially join the chorus of those who sing the praises of Benedetto Cavalieri pasta. It is worth the cost. It is the most delicious pasta by far that I have ever eaten, and it one of the most delicious foods on earth.

This is real authentic pasta that's very hard to find in America. It is thick spaghetti, traditionally called vermicelli in Italy, that cooks aldente and also healthier with more fiber and less triglycerides. FDA guidelines in America require pasta be fortified with vitamins and minerals, especially ferrous sulfate, ferrous lactate and folic acid to pretend to help the inner city indigent. This ruins the natural wheat product and has made it almost impossible to find good pasta in America. This pasta is expensive, but you need to take into consideration the quality as well as special costs of obtaining this upper out of sight product. Respectfully submitted.

One of the reasons I order Spaghetti at my local Italian restaurant is the extra thickness of the strands.  This pasta is not only thicker than spaghetti but as a bonus, it is the best I have ever cooked for myself.
Ordered this pasta from Amazon and it was received promptly.  I like thick spaghetti, but beware, this is really, really thick.  I really like it, but it's a little too much for my wife.

dried chestnuts are used frequently in macrobiotic cooking, providing a somewhat sweet balance to more salty flavors.  while not organic, these nuts are a great value.  they reconstitute quickly and are very flavorful.

These chestnuts were very bitter & seemed like they were not fresh.  They remained hard, even after being boiled.  They had a very starchy taste & not the nuttiness & sweet taste they had when I used to buy them years ago in a Brooklyn Italian Grocery Store.  I would not recommend this product.
Very hard consistency, and the chestnuts do not taste good when softened with water. Perhaps they would do better in a soup.

I don't understand the negative review as these are the closest thing to homemade granola that you can get.  They are dense, chewy and full of oat, nut and date flavor. I think there is batch variation as some have been tougher than others.  Perhaps that is why the other review called them "greasy". I find them very satisfying for breakfast and they aren't sugary sweet like commercial granola bars you buy in upermarkets.

This product is good.  I was a bit skeptical with all the health claims on the box and the packaging.  Generally if it is good for you it tastes bad.  However, big suprise!  The bars have a nice consistency, a lightly sweet flavor, and are much better than the cheaper granola bars I have had before.  Would buy this version again, and will probably buy a box of the chocolate and cherry ones today!

I just ate my first bar, and was thinking to reorder.  But I'm concerned that the Omega balance is unhealthy.  Omega-6 is 1200mg, in one bar, and Omega-3 is only a third of that... at 410mg.  (Omega-6 starts inflammation, and Omega-3 stops inflammation.)  Other than that, this bar is delicious, and is more than 91 percent organic, with all ingredients coming from California.  This bar is preferable over an afternoon bag of chips from the snack machine.

column9: There's a reason why it's called 18 rabbits
column10: I really like these bars, there's a good mix of nuts and fruit; I particularly like the sesame seeds.  The reason why 18 rabbits is such an apt name for these bars is that you need to eat them like a rabbit - nibbling.  For some reason, I've found that it's easiest to eat these in small bites rather than the huge bites I usually prefer.  I think it's probably got to do with whatever is binding it together, and it's not necessarily a bad thing, just something to note.  Buying them here is a lot cheaper than buying individually in the store, great deal!

I am a big fan of the 18 Rabbits chocolate cherry granola bars, which is why I ordered the apricot ones.  Sadly, there is no comparison.  These were flavorless, not a hint of apricot or any other ingredient.  I was disappointed and will not buy this flavor again.

I recently discovered 18 Rabbits granola and now I realize that the granola bars in the grocery store are total junk in comparison.  These are DELICIOUS and healthy, and cost more at my gym, so I'm excited to buy them in bulk online for a better price.

sorry to say this because I like to support small companies but these are terrible!  They have a greasy coating and very earthy taste.  The sweetness does not even have a good sweet flavor.  I wish I could have tried these first because I would never have bought them!

Good for a snack in the car/on-the-go. Good value; easy to store.Only 4 stars because I don't know about quality, pesticides used in Czech Republic where they are made.  Would prefer organic.
