The dense consistency doesn't crumble anything like standard rice cakes, so there is less mess.  My girls use them as the bun for a hamburger or to eat a "sandwich".We also put honey on them as a dessert.  Paskesz also makes these in the small rounds which are just great, as well.Thank you thank you thank you, Paskesz!  We really dread when Amazon lists them as out of stock!

column9: Crispy thin tasty cakes, rice cakes that is
column10: I wanted to compare the price of rice cakes on Amazon to what was in the stores and I stumbled across these. Always intrigued with new and different products (especially those not found in my local stores) I snagged myself a case of them.Price wise these are about the same price (a little more or a little less, depends on if you can find them on sale) then the regular Quaker Oats rice cakes in stores.There are many things that makes these stand out from other rice cakes. First off is the fact that they are compressed, so they are much crispier/crunchier then other rice cakes out there. The other is that they are square, not round. So because of them being compressed/thinner and square this makes them that much easier to store which I really like.Taste wise, I find them nuttier and toastier. I think the process that they use retains more of the brown rice flavor then the other brands.Add in the fact that they have no salt, are kosher, and only 20 calories per cake make these my new favorite snack BY FAR. Add a little bit of homemade jam, some natural peanut butter, Nutella, or pretty much anything to them for a really tasty snack with some variety (I like mine with some Tabasco Chipotle).Just love them!

I have ordered one case, finished it and this is my second case. This garlic powder doesn't have that strong, bitter taste (and aftertaste), that many do. It is a good substitute when you have no fresh garlic for making garlic bread. However, they're awfully pricey -- at my local grocery store, they're about $3 a packet, and some online sellers are charging twice that.I won't buy them often, but they're a nice treat that's fairly healthy and something that's fairly easy to pack in the diaper back (that's not the standard Cheerios!).

I bought these for my son and he didn't care for the berry flavor, he did eat the peach. They are a little sour and while they do dissolve, it kind of sucks all of the moisture out of their little mouths quick so have juice handy. Also, they get a little gross in humid weather so use an airtight container or be sure to close the bag tight. My son will eat them, but prefers gerber's apple chunks or a real cup of yogurt.

As they're a little expensive, I use them to 'buy' myself some time when making dinner. Have each kid sit at the table and give them a small handful to work on while I work on what I need to. Even my son (who usually crashes through food) sits quietly and eats these one at a time until they're all gone. Instant silence!Definitely a staple in my pantry. I like to purchase these on Amazon when they fall to a price low (~$20) to save a bit of $$$.

The baby likes these as much as the happy melts, but when I read the ingredients I noticed they contain gelatin, however the label does not say from what.  So, if you are kosher or halal, you may not want to get these ones.

This is a great product and my daughter loves them. She's been eating them since she was 9 months old. However, this is extremely overpriced. They're $2 a pack at Publix. $6.24 a pack is nuts.

There are quite a few foods I like better than sardines but I eat a tin now and then because they're (supposedly) healthful and very convenient.  I've tried most of the common grocery store varieties and found these to be the best of them, primarily because, as the box says, they are "meaty portions cleaned and scaled."  Compared to others, there's less icky bits in the tin, and they do have a nice meaty texture that reminds you more of a real fish meal and less of leftover bait.  The marinara sauce is expectedly watery and flavorless; I add hot sauce or other spices.  Yes, the ad copy all over the box is hyperbolic but presumably you're not buying them for reading material.

Are we talking about the wild sardines?Uh-uh. We're talking about me, who as of this writing has lapsed into Amazon reviewer oblivion, with a ranking of 1002. Seeing my name appear without that little "Top 1000" moniker makes me feel vulnerable and exposed.What to do about it? Submit yet another review of a tin of sardines. I can't think of a better means of clawing my way back to the top.This time it's Wild Planet Wild Sardines in Marinara sauce. I already did the ones in olive oil, as well as those with a dash of lemon juice.So, here goes...There's nothing really wrong with these sardines, though as noted below I don't particularly care for their smoky taste. My problem is with the marketing, which attempts to justify an inflated price with a dissertation of a long list of purported benefits. Problem is, most if not all of these benefits apply to all brands of sardines, not just these.For instance, what about the whole concept of "wild" sardines? I'm not aware that the sardine has been domesticated, and the lowly pilchards that swarm the seas in massive schools sometimes visible from outer space are not amenable to aquaculture.On the other hand, qualifying these sardines as wild, notwithstanding the fact that there's no other kind, does confer a seemingly significant though clearly misplaced credibility. No doubt this will boost sales to a gullible buying public.Read the packaging for these sardines and you can't help but feel you're saving Mother Earth as you chomp on your sandwich. But digging down beneath the surface, there's not so much to be excited about.For instance there's the matter of what happens to these fish after they're "sustainably caught along the California coast". The small print provides a clue in that these bad boys are "processed in Viet Nam". So what's really going on is that our diminutive sardines take on a heavy carbon footprint, travelling as they do from the west coast to the far east and back again, presumably to harvest the otherwise mutually exclusive benefits of buy-local chic and low labor costs. Nonetheless, we read that, "These sardines are considered a `Best Choice for Sustainability' by a consensus of environmental organizations".There are other issues as well.The health benefits of chowing down on this product are highly touted. For instance, "Ounce for ounce, Wild Planet sardines provide 3 times more calcium and phosphorus than milk...". OK, fair enough. But is this, as implied, unique to the Wild Planet variety only, or is it once again a characteristic of all sardines? Unfortunately, it's the latter.We also learn that these "delicious meaty portions" are "cleaned and scaled". Buyer beware: this is quite different from "skinless and boneless". "Cleaned" in this context must mean something other that what is commonly expected by the use of this word in conjunction with fish. Be prepared to either eat the vertebral column and various entrails, or to remove (clean) them yourself.How do they taste?Not bad, if you're into schmaltz herring. These babies are smoked and have a characteristic smoky, salty taste. Dunking them in marinara doesn't do much to change this.But don't worry. It's not just any smoke, but "aqueous natural smoke" that they're treated with...
I tried this type after trying some at an fish restaurant, and was not the same thing.  I am not saying is a bad product, just it doesn't justify the price with the quality offered.

It was fragrant. My house smelled like basmati rice for hours.The cooked grains don't have that fragrant smell though. This cooked really quickly - a lot quicker than expected.I'm happy with my purchase.

I bought this product since it was Indian basmati rice, I thought the grains would be longer and it would have a basmati rice fragrance to it, none what so ever.  I will say it cooks quicker than most brown basmati rice I have eaten.  I have definitely had better brown basmati rice.

There's nothing really wrong with this rice, but there's nothing really special about it either.  It's serviceable.  I cook it in my rice cooker and the basmati aroma is indeed very pleasant.  I did think, based on basmati brown rice I bought from a Safeway store, that the fiber content would be higher.  It's actually 1g (4% of the RDA) per 1/4 cup.  That's not high, although it's a step up from plain ol' white rice.  Other nutritional details: 180 calories, 38g carbs, 3g protein, plus calcium 2%, iron 6%, thiamine 13% and Niacin 8%. Although not listed on the product label, B vitamins are also found in Basmati brown rice.In case you're wondering, the rice is not theoretically loose inside the burlap bag (which is double-sewn shut and has a zipper) because there's a inner plastic bag.  The plastic bag is cheap and flimsy though, and somewhere along the way a lot of the rice left the bag I got (assuming it started in it) and was just loose inside the burlap. I emptied it all into ziplock bags to store in the freezer.The expiration date is Jan 2014. I paid just under $15 and expect to be eating this rice for many months to come. Make that many, MANY months to come.

column9: Grown in the fertile soil of the Himalayan region
column10: I ordered this rice after the great arsenic scare of 2012, and I am not disappointed. For those that are not aware, US rice carries "1.4 to 5 times more arsenic than rice from Europe, India and Bangladesh. As I write this, I have a pot of lentil Dahl cooking, and I'll eat it with this rice.I was quite happy with rice grown in America, but they decided to grow it in ex-cotton fields that had been sprayed with arsenic...and even used chicken poop that contains arsenic to fertilize *organic* rice crops with (It seems feeding chickens arsenic allows them to grow faster. Your health doesn't matter, it is all about the benjamins).My favorite rice is a Lundberg organic, brown/wild rice blend. Is this rice as good as Lundberg's rice? Probably not, but the bar is set pretty high there. However, this is a good solid rice and I plan on getting more in the future.If anyone would like to know what the tag attached to the bag says (you can see it in the picture), this is what it reads:Bombay Original - Basmati Rice is grown in the fertile soil of the Himalayan region. the cool clean mountain air, abundand streams and rainfall create the perfect growing conditions that give this premium Basmati rice its special flavour and firm texture. Basmati rice is low in calories, contains no sodium, and no cholesterol. Enjoy it in good health.

I love brown rice, especially cheap and delicious brown rice. I'm not a rice snob by far, but I do appreciate good rice. This rice is very aromatic and seems to be of a good quality. (Not fancy, but great for every day consumption.) The packaging on this is really clever too! It is packaged in a burlap sack that is lined with a bag and zips with a normal zipper on the top! I will definitely reuse this packaging.
love this rice! its very delicious and the aroma is outstanding. grain length are perfect, I had no issues. We always buy basmati rice!! Will buy again !

column9: Rice itself looks to be of good quality, but packaging is terrible.
column10: I purchased this brown basmati rice after trying a small package purchased at a grocery store. The price certainly is good, 10 lbs for under $15.00 which is really good for basmati rice from India. When I received the shipment, which was delivered promptly, I found that the burlap sack it comes in has a zipper at the top, but when un-zipped it is stitched shut and needs to be cut open. This is not a problem, as the sack says it is "tamper proof", however the inner plastic bag containing the rice was already open and small particles of burlap threads must have fallen onto the rice whilst cutting open the sack. Not to mention a large quantity of rice had already spilled outside the inner bag. When I attempted to remove the inner plastic bag it burst open and about half of the rice fell all over the floor. So I had to spend the next 20 min. cleaning up this huge mess of rice. I can't believe how tissue-thin the inner plastic bag is! Now I have to go buy a large container to transfer the remaining rice into. The rice itself looks to be of good quality, and I will probably end up ordering more of this rice in the future because the price can't be beat. But be forewarned about the packaging.
They are not too hard not too soft, they are just right.I guess they would be nice warm, but they taste so goodwho has time to wait.  This is a great bargain and thereare plenty to share.
Perfect taste and crunch. I'm hooked. Hard to find in stores, I'm so happy Amazon carries them. Also try the banana.

The first sentence on the back of the box urges consumers to not "confuse vanilla with ordinary".  It seemed a strange emphasis for an organic cereal filled with all of the current "right stuff" and after tasting "Crunchy Vanilla Sunrise", I understood the need to convince people that what they were eating was something special.  The predominant initial flavor is faux vanilla, followed by a bitter, lingering aftertaste. Overly sweet and artificial, this cereal tries to be all things to all people, managing to satisfy few.  There are better alternatives on the shelf.

column9: Great organie and gluten free product
column10: I am very glad to see more and more organic and gluten-free products coming on the market - finally! Nature's Path products are excellent, and this cereal is one of their best.Picture the less healthy but highly bought versions of Kix, Rice Crispies, and some kind of flakes all thrown together in one cereal - only much better - and you have Crunchy Vanilla Sunrise cereal.There are medium sized round balls, large flakes, and several different small puffed grains all combined into one wonderful crunchy treat. This cereal tastes great! It is very sweet tasting, but has only 7grams of sugar. A 2/3 cup serving is only 110 calories, so even if you bump it up to 1 full cup, it will still be just 155 calories, which is well under what most cereals are.This has only 1g of fat, 130 mg sodium, and also has 2g protein. This is a great cereal, but it is also wonderful on yogurt and as an ice cream topping.It is fully organic and gluten free: corn meal, brown rice, quinoa, flax, buckwheat. HOWEVER, it is made in a facility that uses peanuts, so that might be a problem for some people.

column9: Almost great but a little too sweet and a little too much vanilla
column10: This cereal has a lot going for it: gluten-free, multigrain and a good crispy texture. I'm not gluten-intolerant myself but I do like to include grains other than wheat and corn in my diet, and this cereal certainly does that by combining corn, rice, flax, quinoa, buckwheat and amaranth.The reason I'm rating it 3 stars is for some nitpicky issues with the flavor. First, it's just a *pinch* too sweet. The nutritional sugars count is fairly low at 7g, but I feel like they could lower that 1-2g and that would be the perfect level of sweetness. The other issue I have is in regards to the vanilla flavor. The vanilla in this cereal is fairly strong, which at first bite is nice, but where it fails is that you get a little bit of a bitter aftertaste. If it wasn't for this bitterness and the slight oversweetness, the cereal would be just about perfect.

I'm not a fan of any kind of dry cereal when it comes to a truly healthy diet.  Such are treats and I don't even pretend that they are healthy, even when they are organic or gluten-free.  This one is no exception.  I didn't get it because I wanted a healthy breakfast cereal, I wanted a cereal gluten-free snack option, which tend to be very limited.The taste is a light vanilla which is quickly lost to just an overall sweet flavor.  It stays crunchy for a bit in rice milk, though if it sits for a few minutes turns to mush.  The variation in the textures is nice, though I can see how it would be too much in one bowl for some.  It has virtually no native nutritional value, with most of its vitamins sprayed on.  In that light it doesn't fall any more short than any other cereal on the market, and is likely better than most.If you're looking for a healthy gluten-free cereal this isn't it, but it is very tasty and not at all reminiscent of the grit and twigs often found in most gluten-free cereals.  Take a bite or two and you won't know it's gluten-free, let alone "healthy."  As it's priced, it's no more expensive than most other cereals.  I'd buy it again.

Tasted good right out of the box and also with milk. Not too sweet, pleasantly crunchy and reasonably nutritious. Extremely young kids liked it instantly right out of the box, along with adults. It works as both a snack and as a centerpiece for a meal with milk, especially breakfast.

This cereal was a hit at our house.  Kids and adults all loved it and the box was gone quickly.Likes:- Texture:  Stays crunchy.  Think Kix meets Rice Crispies meets wheaties with a mild vanilla sweetness.- Sweetness:  Sweet enough to get the kids hooked but only 7 grams of sugar.  Our other favorite, Pops, has 10 g sugar.- Nutrition:  Moderate sugar, very low fat, a little protein (2g) and a good amount of fiber (12g).- Gluten Free:  Another tasty option for gluten sensitive folks.  We are not but would eat this anyway.- Organic Ingredients:  the ingredients sound very natural and minimally processed.Dislikes:The box was empty this morning.  :-(Overall highly recommended.

While I am not generally a cereal fan, this one won me over.  The different grains had a nice texture to them, even after sitting in milk for a while, and the flavor was great.  Nice and light vanilla, not way overpowering.  My kids even enjoyed eating this straight out of the box!

column9: Natural, organic ingredients, but artificial-seeming result
column10: The Nature's Path product, Crunchy Vanilla Sunrise, comes in a relatively plain package with the words nature, whole grain, and organic abundantly displayed on the package. To its credit, it contains two of my favorite grains: amaranth, and quinoa.  Quinoa was apparently a favorite for South American pre-Columbian civilizations.  The cereal's number one ingredient is corn meal.  This is ok.  I have consumed many boxes of Kellogg's Corn Flakes.The texture is indeed crunchy which is nice in a cereal. The taste is on the sweet side, if you are used to unsweetened cereals.  The cereal does live up to its middle name, vanilla.  The vanilla flavor is quite apparent.  This is to bring back memories of "cookies fresh from Grandma's oven."My big disappointment is that this cereal is almost one-quarter sugar, e.g., 10.5 grams of sugar of a total of 45 grams per cup. This is almost as much sugar as there is in a tablespoon of granulated sugar which comes in at 13 grams. By contrast, Kellogg's Corn Flakes has 3 grams of sugar per cup, Cheerios has 1 gram of sugar per cup, and Shredded Wheat has zero grams of sugar. The sugar comes from cane juice. It is real sugar, not the fake high-fructose stuff. It may not be corn syrup, but it certainly is not wholesome. Sugar has been associated with diabetes, obesity, hyperactivity in children, and may be addictive.It seems to me that Nature's Path has gone to a lot of effort to use organic, natural ingredients to create this new cereal.  Amazingly, the result is a product that appears to be totally artificial.  This may take a lot of skill, but the effort would have been better used to create a cereal that takes advantage of its natural grain ingredients rather submerging them in sugar and vanilla.The two stars are for the amaranth and quinoa.

column9: Better for a snack than for breakfast
column10: First, I really like the taste and texture of this cereal.  While other reviewers did not care for the vanilla taste, I personally like it.  "Natural vanilla flavor" is 8th in a list of 14 ingredients.  For me, the flavor is just right.Second, I frequently choose Chex mix as my "snack of choice" while watching TV in the evening.  This cereal would be a much better choice for me.  Comparing the 1/2 cup serving of Sweet'n Salty Chex Mix to the 2/3 cup serving of Crunchy Vanilla Sunrise, I find that:* Vanilla Sunrise is Gluten Free, Chex Mix isn't (or doesn't advertise that it is)* Vanilla Sunrise has 1 g of fat (no trans fat, no saturated fat), Chex Mix has3.5g of fat (no trans fat, .5g saturated fat)* Vanilla Sunrise has 3 g of fiber, Chex Mix has 1* Vanilla Sunrise does have more sugars: 7g to Chex Mix's 4 gFinally, as a breakfast cereal, this fails when compared to most of the vitamin- and mineral-rich breakfast cereals that are out there.  Even the kid-friendly Cap'n Crunch has more to offer when it comes to vitamins, A, C, and iron:* Vanilla Sunrise has 0%, 0%, and 4% of vitamins A, C, and iron, respectively, compared to 10%, 10%, and 25% in Kellogg's Frosted FlakesSo, Vanilla Sunrise wins as a snack, but loses as a breakfast (depending on what you look for in a morning meal)

I must confess upfront I am not a nutritional nut when it comes to cereal.  If I ate cereal every day I would be more selective I suppose.  But truthfully I only eat cereal on occasion when I get the hankerin' for it.  So I pretty much go with what tastes real good.  That being said I am not immune to the idea and benefits of a nutritional breakfast cereal, especially if its both good for you and full of flavor.  Unfortunately this Natures Path blend doesn't cut it for me in either respect.  There are not only cereals out there that are better for you, but I also have to agree with many of the other reviewers here that say that this cereal carries a sort of sour aftertaste.  In fact I will even go as far as to say it starts out with one.  The vanilla flavor is so abundant that it tends to create an artificial taste that is not at all pleasant in my opinion.  Also, this cereal seems to take an abnormally long time to soften as well.  It stays rather overly crunchy right up till your bowl is just about empty.  That doesn't help the cheap, overpowering flavor of the vanilla or whatever it is since it remains undiluted through most of your meal.  In conclusion, although the price of this stuff is not all that bad as good-for-you cereals go, I would opt for Honey Bunches of Oats or some other brand over this stuff if nutritional cereal is your favor.  This Natures Path stuff is unfortunately a no sale for me...

column9: ok, not as healthy as the box would have you believe
column10: Nature's Path wants to lead you to a better breakfast, but better than what?  If you eat fruit loops, than this is probably healthier.  If you eat oatmeal in the morning, then this is not a better bowl.Let's start with VALUE:This is a primarily a puffed cereal with some flakes.  The side of the box says a serving is 2/3 cup, but since it is mostly just puffs I think 1 cup is a better serving size to provide closer to what one needs to make it a couple of hours without your stomach growling.  Dense cereals like granola or Grape-nuts are an ample breakfast in a 2/3 cup serving but this is not.  So following that logic you don't get 10 servings in a box, you get about 6-7 -- so figure 1 box will last a week.  So about 55 cents a meal, not too bad.NUTRITION:There are 7 grams of sugar in a 2/3 cup serving, so almost 10 grams for a cup of cereal.  I was shocked that this cereal didn't have more vitamins, the only thing it had was 4% iron.  It doesn't have gluten, but this is a moot point if you don't suffer from a legitimate allergy or condition were gluten makes you sick.  Gluten-free is so trendy right now I feel like this product is hitting a lot of buzz words but not hitting the mark on nutrition.TASTE:The second ingredient is sweetener, and you can really tell.  I was shocked it tasted so sweet for being touted as a healthy cereal.  To me it tastes like a vanilla flavored  kid's cereal.  It is a mix of large corn puffs, seed-sized puffs that I assume are flax and flakes.  The texture is nice and crunchy but it doesn't hew up the roof of your mouth.  It is not good to eat dry because of the teeny-tiny sedd puffs, they get everywhere.  This might be good used to spruce up other cereals, like add 1/3 cup of it to half a bowl of bran flakes or something.  Or you can feed it to your kid as a breakfast treat.  My toddler LOVED a bowl of this cereal, but I wouldn't give it to her every morning.OTHER:This stuff worked great in some homemade granola bars I made.  I cut out 2/3 of the sweetener and added this cereal in hopes of making them less dense and it worked great.  Gave them a bit of a "Rice Crispy Treat" texture.OVERALL: This cereal gets 3 stars because it does have decent fiber (4) and protein (almost 3) for a cup of cold cereal that doesn't taste like twigs.  I would want it again to add to my granola bars.  It would be good for kids who want a "sugar cereal" fix, but remember to give them some fruit with it since this isn't sprayed with vitamins.  Not great, but not horrible.  I guess if this was marketed as a kids cereal with a silly cartoon bear on the box we'd all be amazed at how good for you it is compared to Captain Crunch.

This Nature's Path cereal tastes a lot like vanilla Kashi cereals that I've eaten, but is lighter.  Still, it remains impressively crunchy in milk and the texture is an interesting mix of big shapes and tiny spheres.  Overall, a nice earthy blend with light sweetness and a good amount of vanilla.  It is very simple, but not bland.I am surprised to see some reviewers say it is cloyingly sweet.  To me, the sweetness was pretty subtle.  More akin to health brands than Lucky Charms.  For the record, I like both!  In terms of vitamin content, yes, it looks worse by the numbers, but that is the result of it being a simple mix of organic ingredients rather than a synthetic assembly with supplements added to make us feel better about eating it.Why not 5 stars?  While I like it, as a breakfast I do not think it would carry me far.  This could be helped by eating a large bowl, but these small boxes would not last long that way.  If you instead prefer a very light breakfast or want to eat this as a snack, I think it is a good option.

Nature's Path Crunchy Vanilla Sunrise might be a "warm and delicious gluten free breakfast cereal" but the first ingredient is organic whole grain corn meal, in other words, sugar, the second ingredient is evaporated can juice (more sugar) the third ingredient, organic brown rice flour which is fine, and the fourth  ingredient, yellow corn flour (more sugar again). Ingredients after that get more healthy.So while the product may be "gluten free" it's loaded with sugar - you won't have side effects if your gluten intolerant, but you may end up on the ceiling if you don't handle sugar well.

This is a really tasty cereal with a great blend of textures and flavors. It's a combination of flakes, and what look like rice and/or quinoa puffs and corn puffs. The flakes start to soften in milk while the corn puffs remain crunchy. It tastes sweet but not overly so, and there is a hint of vanilla flavoring.This product is gluten-free so it would be good for people with celiac disease, and it's got 3gm of fiber in every serving. It has grains like quinoa, amaranth, rice and corn, as well as flax seed in it, and everything is organic. The calories, sugars and sodium are relatively low, so I would consider this to be a fairly healthy food.My only quibble is that I wish it had a slightly more pronounced vanilla taste, but I can live with it as it is. I ate it plain, but this cereal would taste great with some raisins or chopped dates thrown in.Without even realizing it, I ate half the box! I would definitely buy this again. Recommended.

column9: Strong vanilla taste; first ingredient is corn; cereal very sweet
column10: This cereal has a nice vanilla flavor but is very sweet to me.  It tastes more like a satisfactory dessert than cereal.The box claims this is gluten-free, a good source of fiber, omega-3 (0.15 gram which is 11% of daily value) and full of whole grains.  In particular corn (ingredient 1 & 4), rice (3), flax (7), quinoa (6 & 10), buckwheat (9) and amaranth (12) are highlighted as ingredients.  Most of these ingredients can be considered healthy if they were in its natural form, weren't so far down on the ingredients list and the cereal was not so sweet.The label claims you get 10 servings per box with a serving being 2/3rd cup at 110 calories plain (no skim milk).  Well 2/3 cup is not much at all since about half the cereal is puffed. For me, this box only contains 4 servings.There is no saturated fat which is a plus; in fact only 10 calories come from fat.  There are 2 grams of protein per serving as well as 25 grams of carbohydrate (sugars 7 grams).The ORGANIC ingredients in order are:1. Whole grain corn meal2. Evaporated cane juince3. Brown rice flour4. Yellow corn flour5. Inulin6. Quinoa puffs (the puffs take up a lot of space in the 1/3 cup serving)7. Flax seeds8. Natural vanilla flavor (one of the few ingredients not preceded by the word Organic)9. Buckwheat flour10.Quinoa11.Sea salt (one of the ingredients not preceded by the word Organic)12.Amaranth13.Molasses14.Tocopherols (natural vitamin E) (another one of the ingredients not preceded by the word Organic)This cereal is produced in a facility that uses peanuts, tree nuts and soy.In summary, "Nature's Path Crunchy Vanilla Sunrise" tasts pretty good to me and has a strong vanilla flavor I like but should be considered as a low-fat dessert instead of a healthy breakfast cerael.

column4: Glenda Boozer "Live, live, live! Life is a ba...
column9: Light, crunchy and just sweet enough.
column10: Nature's Path Crunchy Vanilla Sunrise is light and crunchy, rather like other puffed cereals I've tasted, but it is lightly sweet: a pleasant breakfast or quick snack that isn't just like eating sugar. I like it with soy milk.

column9: Great idea, not so great execution
column10: I try to avoid gluten, so cereals have pretty much become a thing of the past for me.  I was very excited to try a gluten free cereal.  If you only care about the taste, then this cereal is fairly enjoyable.  However, it is advertised as a health food and this is where I run into issues.  The first ingredients are whole grain corn meal, evaporated cane juice, brown rice flour and inulin.  They are all organic, but corn is one of the worst things that you can put into your body and it appears to be the bulk of this cereal...well, except for the evaporated cane juice! (aka sugar).  The package advertises is as a good source of fiber and omega-3.  There are only 3 grams of fiber (not bad, but not great) and only 1 gram of fat.  How can this be high in omega-3 fatty acids when there is only 1 gram (or possibly less) per serving?  Then you look at the nutrient profile: Vitamin A- 0; Vitamin C- 0, Calcium - 0.I guess this is a step up from normal junk food cereal, but I think it falls short of what it advertises.  I do not think I will purchase any more.

column9: Nature's Path Crunchy Vanilla Sunrise Cereal
column10: I was looking forward to trying this cereal, because not too long ago I was able to try a wonderful granola cereal by Nature's Path, which I liked very much.So, I expected to like this cereal too.  Unfortunately I don't!  I poured alittle bit of the cereal into a bowl.  On my first bite what I tasted seemed salty to me.  I also do not really taste a vanilla flavor, or much of a vanilla flavor.I love the flavor vanilla, especially if it's real vanilla flavoring, but there is also another mainstream brand of cereal that also came in a vanilla flavor that so many people also seemed to love, and I didn't really care for that cereal either.It does look interesting when you pour the cereal into your bowl, different shapes, which consist of corn, rice,flax, quinoa, buckwheat and amaranth.When I read the nutrition facts, except for the fact that this cereal is organic, which to me is major, the health benefits really are no better than even alot of mainstream cereals, this cereal is no higher in important nutrients.The total carbohydrates per 2/3 Cup serving is 25 grams, which is 8%,dietary fiber is 3 grams, which is 12%, and sugars is 7 grams.  The sodium level is only 130 mg, which is only 5%.  There is only 1 gram of total fat, and 4% iron.  I would call this a reasonably healthy cereal, and it is gluten free.Iam not impressed.  I wish I were.  It does not keep me from wanting to try other Nature's Path products, but Iam disappointed to find that I did not like this cereal after reading such wonderful feedback about it.Maybe I just don't like vanilla flavored cereals?

Very nice breakfast cereal; still maintains a great crunch when mixed with plain yogurt (my favorite way of eating it).Most important, this cereal is gluten free.  There are so few gluten free ready-to-eat cereals on the market.  This one gets an A+.

I found it as a sweet treat and with 7 grams of sugar it is no wonder. This cereal list a long list of ingredients that include whole corn meal, evaporated cane juice and  molasses. The box only seems to highlight two main points; that the cereal is Gluten-Free and organic. But there is also an appropriate warning that it is produced in a facility that uses peanuts, tree nuts and soy. I only added milk to the contents of the box and enjoyed the vanilla flavor and did not notice an aftertaste. I liked that it stays crunchy while in milk. This is not a cereal I would eat every day but as a treat. I would eat this again but I would not seek it out.

column9: Hard to tell this is gluten free
column10: This cereal has good texture, with decent crunch. Most gluten free products tend to be very crunchy which I like. The puffs remain crunchy after a few minutes in milk, but the flakes do not. I tried the cereal without milk first and found it to be lightly sweetened. I think kids would eat it, but it's not the candy in the box they'd normally like. I ate the cereal with sweetened vanilla almond milk and overall, the cereal is very good. If you have been recently directed to eat gluten free products, no need to fear. This cereal is quite comparable to any of the healthy cereals on the market, despite the lack of gluten. Recommended.

column9: Not bad, but has a weird aftertaste....
column10: I made the mistake of tasting a couple grains of this cereal before I put in a bowl with milk, and there is some kind of aftertaste, not sure what it is, but I wasn't a fan.  I had a small bowl and the cereal was fine, but still some kind of aftertaste that I couldn't really make out.  I liked the crunchy little balls and flakes probably best but with so many cereals that I really like, I would not choose this cereal over the others.  I did love the fact it was organic and natural, but the taste wasn't really something that I would crave or want to go back and buy again.

First, the box did not come 1/3 filled -- it's filled by weight but there is a difference between a full-to-the-top cornflake box, where the shape of the flakes enable them to stack themselves with lot of airspace in between, so they look like the box is way full--- and these various "Crunchy Vanilla Sunrise" shapes that do a great job of nestling themselves into one another and within all the other shapes -- so although there is a fully-filled box here, it just doesn't look like it.But the cereal is way too sweet -- I wanted to be able to taste the various flavors of the corn, quinoa, buckwheat and other grains in the ingredients, but instead my tastebuds were assailed by a cloying sweetness that was way too powerful. I added hot coffee to the cereal and that helped take some of the sweet edge off. I also tried mixing in my protein drink -- and that helped take some of the edge off the sweetness, but even so I did not get to taste the various flavors of all the healthy grains.The Gluten Free factor was favorably noticed -- amazaing how heavy wheat can be on the stomach and senses -- the (wheat and soy-free) ingredients this cereal brought lightness, even with the over-much sweetness.My final take on this is: reduce the amount of sugar (and perhaps even vanilla) in the formulation -- and I think you will then have a nice enjoyable, hearty-tasting cereal that will wake up the tastebuds.

column9: Better as a snack than as a breakfast cereal
column10: Nice vanilla flavor, lots of crunch, but the smaller bits get soggy quickly in milk.  The taste and texture remind me of Team flakes, which I don't think is made anymore.This is nice as a sweet snack, and would make excellent marshmallow Krispie treats.  It'd also be good crushed as a topping for ice cream or in a pie crust in lieu of graham crackers.  It's good when a food can do double-triple duty.

As Crunchy Vanilla Sunrise is a "health cereal," gluten-free and organic to boot, I'm guessing most prospective customers would be "health-conscious" and thus interested in the label's nitty (and, as required by law, its gritty). Do you care about sugar? The latest research says it is a bigger villain than previously thought, worse even than cholesterol and fat (well, "good" fat, anyway). This cereal provides 7 grams of sugar for each 2/3rds cup of serving meaning, for most people, a bowl of 1 1/2 cups (not much, mind you) would bring in 14 grams of organic evaporated cane juice (number two on the list of ingredients, which are listed in order of amount in the cereal).Of course, if you like a sweeter cereal, you might count this a strength and not a weakness. It's not like this is Trix or Cocoa Puffs or anything, where sugar gram totals are higher than Cheech and Chong on a Saturday night. To its credit, CVS provides 3 grams of dietary fiber and only 1 gram of fat (zero saturated or trans fats). And hey, it's gluten-free and offers a motley mix of corn, rice, flax, quinoa, buckwheat, and molasses. In fact, it looks like that hodgepodge my father used to create when he combined three or four cereals that were all nearing empty. (We cured him of the habit by refusing to eat the result.)Bottom line? If you like "healthy" with quotation marks (or an asterisk for the sugar), this might be your cereal. If, on the other hand, you're watching your pennies (economical this product is not) or carbs and sugar in an attempt to lose weight, consider the humble egg. Or old-fashioned oatmeal like Grandma ate. Flavor it not with sugar, maple syrup, or molasses, but with cinnamon, allspice, and cloves. Serve with morning paper.

I can't believe I'm writing a review for cereal of all things, but this stuff is THAT delicious.  I'm picky when it comes to cereal usually sticking to old traditional brands, afraid to try new ones because they are typically a disappointment.  I had the chance to sample this (dry) in a small cup at Costco, I was hungry and just saw it as a quick snack expecting it to taste like a mouthful of hay like most organic cereals.  Wow.... very surprised!  It seriously tastes like Rice Krispie candy, only a ton healthier.I immediately bought a box, it's just as delicious as a dry snack as it is with milk in a bowl.  It leaves a pleasant sweet vanilla type of taste in your mouth after each bite, and the various textures makes it more interesting.  The smallest pieces are the size of rice, and the ball things are the size of Kix cereal.  It's a nice light crunchy cereal that doesn't get soggy too fast.  Going to get a bowl now... :)

column9: For the healthy breakfast eater..... not my choice
column10: I'm not one for special cereals, and this one is considered organic and also gluten-free, while the flavor speaks of vanilla and it contains a certain amount of crunchiness.  The products are mostly organic, and there is quite a mixture.... Quinoa, rice, flaxseed, bran, cornmeal, etc., etc.When I look at the package of the product, it looks like someone mixed a whole bunch of different cereals into the box.  I never did approve of mixing cereals, and that is what this resembles.You have to acquire a taste for this.  There is more of a sweeter taste that I would not have selected.  It is acceptable, but nothing great.  For the more healthy conscious breakfast eaters, this would serve them well, but for me, it is not something I would purchase.  Rizzo

column9: Good Option For Gluten Free Cereal
column10: I really enjoy this cereal.  There are a variety of grains in it, like quinoa, buckwheat and amaranth.  The texture of the cereal is also varied, there are puffs and flakes.  I think it is the amaranth that gives this cereal a nutty taste.  It's not overly sweetened and has just a hint of vanilla, which I like.  I'd recommend this to anyone who is looking for a gluten free cereal.

column9: Could be worse, should be better
column10: I must start by stipulating that my body is gluten-tolerant and sugar-intolerant (adult-onset diabetes). 7 Grams of sugar in a 30-gram (2/3rds cup) serving size is IMO too much for a healthy cereal. And unless one is gluten-intolerant, gluten (a protein that is what makes grains nutritious) is a good thing. Sticking to objective matters, the vitamin content listed is 0%, 0%, and 0% of the official minimum daily requirement, and I presume if more were listed there would be more 0%. The exception is iron, with 4% (contrast the 45% from Special-K),Also leaving aside the rather loose legal requirements for labeling something "organic," the list of ingredients does not strike me as particularly healthy, beginning with cornmeal and sugarcane juice (called "cane juice"). I wonder what "organic molasses" is, while doubting it is a health(y) food and wonder what "natural vanilla flavor" is. I'd bet that there is little real/organic vanilla in the mix! I'm not sure what the protein source is, probably some quinoa, but the 2 grams (/30) is respectable.Turning to the highly subjective matter of taste, the vanilla flavor comes through, particularly in the variant on Sugar Pops, one of the three disparate textures included, along with flakes (texturally like Corn Flakes, and small textureless bits. This is the order, from top to bottom, that the textures separated out on the way to me.I liked Sugar Pops when I was a child (but put away childish things when I ceased being a child). The Nature Fresh pops taste sweet, though less sweet than I remember Sugar Pops tasting. I already said that the vanilla "flavoring" comes through. Some complain of an unpleasant vanilla aftertaste but I did not experience that. To me the taste was OK with no aftertaste.I don't see any reason for anyone who is gluten-tolerant to buy the expensive (and to me pretentious) sugarcane and cornmeal (these are the the main ingredients, though the list of ingredients also includes currently fashionable quinoa and flax seeds) mix of textures. There are breakfast "cereals" with organically raised components that are more nutritious and no more expensive.(I severely doubt that a box of Crunchy Vanilla Sunrise with provide any real persons 10 servings. "Serving sizes" are generally suspect, but for breakfast foods the usual one is a cup. Given that the pops that are tops or at least rise to the top have a lot of air in them, claiming the serving size is 2/3rds of a cup is particularly disingenuous.)

column9: I hated it, but Mom loved it.
column10: I thought this cereal was terrible. It has a very odd aftertaste, and to be honest, this is what I would imagine balled up pieces of paper soaked in milk would taste like. Very "cardboard-like." It also has that really strange, fake vanilla-like taste that a lot of the ultra-healthy and "organic" cereals have. For me, this is just further proof that these "healthy" cereals taste awful. I'll stick to the Cheerios and Special K, thanks!That being said, I'm still giving this two stars because my Mom LOVED it. Don't ask me why, because Lord knows I have no idea, but she thought it was great. When I asked her what exactly she liked about it, she state that she enjoyed the taste and the crunchiness. She thought the vanilla flavoring was good, and was surprised that I didn't like it as she felt it was very "true to taste." She also liked that it had so many healthy things in it, i.e. flax. She thought that for a "healthy" cereal, it was very tasty.I guess all things considered it just depends on your personal taste. I mean, it's food. What one person loves another person dislikes. Like I said, I thought it tasted like rolled up pieces of paper soaked in milk into which someone poured an artificial vanilla flavoring. She, on the other hand, found it tasty, crunchy, satisfying, and overall delicious. To each his own, I suppose. I personally won't be rebuying this one.

column4: Sir Charles Panther "Life is hard.  It's hard...
column10: The name: "Crunchy Vanilla Sunrise" evokes a lot.  The first word sets the tone, and unfortunately I tend to relate "crunchy" first with hippies, Earth shoes, organic detergent, underground homes, crystal-based religions, and a general flakiness.  Now one could argue that "flaky" and "cereal" is a good mental association, but I doubt the copywriters and marketers were thinking in this vein.  I think they were after the more visceral, literal, "Hey, Velma, by the great white beard of Odin, this here cereal is mighty crunchy!  I can hardly hear myself think!" outcome.  "Vanilla," on the other hand, is what got me to order this product.  I love vanilla, and had to try this out.  "Vanilla" had me thinking "deep, dusky flavor," as opposed to "dull," which the box's back panel tackles unflinchingly.  And then you get "sunrise."  Well, the mental association intent is evident here; it's all about setting a deep and contented feeling centered directly on the product, about the peace of morning and the promise of a new day, clear skies, golden light (see the box photo), bunnies, puppies, galactic serenity, etc.The package: the box I got is different than the official one shown here.  I prefer the box I got over the one shown--the front panel is oriented more to the customer, instead of oriented on the manufacturer.  If you're set on Nature's Path, then you'll find this product anyway; the company logo and name don't need to dominate the front of the box.  As for the back panel, I dunno.  What does "the sweet breeze of a Mexican sunset" have to do with breakfast cereal?  Is this a travel cereal?  And what exactly is a travel cereal, and how do I get it through customs?  And what of the photos of a rain forest, a beach resort, a Mexican air mail stamp, and a sun-worshiping woman sitting in the dirt?  Is this cereal best enjoyed in Mexico, in the dirt?  That, and there's bold language about the "unique nutritional profiles of ancient grains . . .," although there is no further specification on what those profiles are, and why they are so totally extremely good for you.I do note that the front of the box, the top and one side panel call this product "Crunchy Vanilla Sunrise," while the back-panel copy calls it "Vanilla Sunrise Crunch."  Which one is it?  I prefer the latter, actually.The flavor dry out of the box isn't bad, and it would be an okay bagged snack for a hike or for a school lunch.  It was better in milk, in my case the standard 2%.  The very first thing I noticed is that this cereal separates in milk.  Now me, I like a lot of milk, as I like that all-important crunchiness toned down a bit, and I like to drink the cereal-flavored milk when I'm done.  If you're a sparse cereal-milker, then this won't be a problem for you.  With more milk the Kix- and Krispies-like bits float, while the flakes sink.  You've got to actively stir and dredge the bottom of the bowl to get your fully mixed cereal bounty promised in the box photo.And the taste: I thought it was great.  Very nice taste, with just the right amount of vanilla coming through.  Dry or in milk, it is slightly sweet to begin with.  I added a little bit of Equal to sweeten it up a bit more.  The texture is a little screwy, with the crispies and flakes and puffs all mixing together, but once you start masticating, it's no longer an issue.Nutrition: I've provided a photo of the panel, so you sort it all out.  The one thing that I notice is that there are more than 100 calories in a single, tiny serving, and that's before you even add the milk.  No wonder it tastes sweet.  And it's officially and certifiably organic, etc.Bottom line: Sure, I'd eat this cereal again.  It's apparently good for me, which is a plus, and it tastes great.  But at more than $5 per box, and a small box at that, it's awfully spendy.

column9: A tasty dessert but way too sweet for breakfast
column10: I opened this gluten free cereal expecting a variation on granola.  Way too sweet and light to boot- more corn puffs and rice krispies meets a splash of flaxseeds. If I were to take this in the morning I'd go into insulin overdrive, even with milk to slow it down.  But I'd be crashing by mid morning and overeating at noon, both dangerous activities for gluten-free people in a non-gluten-free world.2/3 cup is counted as a serving although you will probably eat a full cup like most cereals since it is light, boosting the calories from 110 to 165.  Actually most will probably go over a cup. The fiber content of 3g per 2/3 cup is okay, but you'd do better with a green smoothie made with whole fruit, nuts and veggies.  There are 7g of sugar (11.5 if you take a cup)- organic evaporated cane juice and molasses are just as bad as high fructose corn syrup in terms of raising your blood sugar and blood insulin levels, except it won't have pesticide residues and you might pick up a hint of a mineral or two from the molasses.  It has 25g of carbs (37.5 per cup) which will quickly convert to sugar.Don't get me wrong, the stuff is tasty.  I tasted it then blew my diet with a large bowl of it. (Note to self: don't review Amazon food products on an empty stomach.) The corn puffs won't be GMO and the grains are organic.  But use it as a dessert. It isn't good for you, unless you are using it to replace Cocoa Puffs. If you want a good breakfast that will sustain you until lunch and avoids gluten, fry a couple of eggs sunny side up in coconut oil and serve over greens or tomato and nori.  Your blood sugar will thank you.  Save this for a treat, to deter you from your roommate's conventional cookies when your willpower is weak.

I was hesitant about any organic, gluten-free and anything my wife's latest health diet is for the week. I wanted to try out this cereal because I love any cereal that doubles as a granola. I loved it. It was sweet enough for kids who are used to sugary cereals but without the caloric and diabetic mess. It was best with almond milk, although greek yogurt was excellent with it as well. The best part? My wife loved it and is making it part of her everyday healthy diet, although I can't say much for whatever fad diet will come next week, she's sticking to this one. I give it one star less because there is not enough cereal in this tiny box.

I am a big fan of the Nature's Path's cereal in general, and this one is no exception. It is surprisingly sweet despite having only 7 grams of sugar per serving. The quinoa flakes are crunchy and unlike a lot of gluten-free cereals that I have tried, this one has a fair amount of fiber. Overall, I will buy this one at my supermarket when my freebie box runs out.

Nature's Path new breakfast product, Crunchy Vanilla Sunrise, is a good tasting cereal that is "gluten free."  It tastes lightly sweetened, a combination of corn flakes, crispy rice, and crunchy puffed corn. The crunchy and chewy texture is maintained in milk for several minutes even though the food is gluten free. The cereal is sweetened with cane juice and molasses. The ingredients include: corn, rice, flax, quinoa, buchwheat, and amaranth. There is 1g of fat (no saturated fat) 25g of carbs and 2g of protein per serving of 2/3 cup. There is an important warning that the cereal is produced in a facility that uses peanuts, tree nuts, and soy.Like many organic cereal products today, the price point is substantial for the 10.6 oz box. I ate the cereal with side dishes of Greek yogurt, blueberries and boysenberries, and walnuts. The cereal's flavor held its own against these other foods, and I will buy it in the future.

Despite the picture on the box, I was still surprised to pour this cereal into a bowl and find that it looked like an odd mash-up of Kix, rice crispies and corn flakes. But as soon as I took a bite, I was hooked! Mildly sweet and addictively crunchy, it is wonderful.From all appearances, the company seems to be exactly the kind of socially responsible business we like to support. They recycle, track their environmental impact, produce a strictly gluten-free product and use organic, non-GMO everything.I was very pleased and expect to get this again.

column9: Great tasting, but probably won't buy again...
column10: We love regular Mesa Sunrise, so we had to try the Vanilla version.  It has a good flavor and my daughter thinks it tastes awesome.  However, I probably won't buy it again because the mixture is mostly Gorilla Munch and Crispy Rice and there is not enough Mesa Sunrise (even less than the picture on the box shows).  We like Gorilla Munch and Crispy Rice, but I bought this because I expected Mesa Sunrise to be the main type of cereal in the mix.Also, even though the product is sold by weight, the packaging is rather deceptive as it is twice as big of a box than it needs to be.  The bag is half full, and that isn't just because of settling!  Expect perhaps 2-4 bowls per box depending on if it is adult or child portions.  We buy the regular Mesa Sunrise in, what Nature's Path calls, "ECO PACS"; following that logic, the packaging of the Vanilla Sunrise should be called "Anti-ECO."  Still, I give it five stars because it has a great taste, it just wasn't quite what we were hoping for!

I must confess, I am not a fan of this cereal by itself. However, I add it to tempered 70% dark chocolate, along with a handful of dry-roasted almonds, and it makes a delicious treat.In its natural state I find it overly sweet and artificial tasting.

column9: Good snack for later in the day
column10: According to the front of my package, Organic Crunchy Vanilla Sunrise mix contains lots of good stuff like corn, rice, flax, quinoa, buckwheat and amaranth.  OK, I don't know what the last one is (a combo of amaretto and absinthe?), but it sounds healthy.  Plus it's gluten-free.  I still don't know why this is a good thing, but I see this claim a lot, so I'm pretty sure the lack of gluten is a positive. The calorie count is 110 a bowl, according to the package, with 10 of those being from fat.  The overall flavor is vanilla, but as it says, you shouldn't confuse "vanilla" with "ordinary."  Fair enough.My first impression upon tasting the mix was that it was surprisingly sweet, but that's subjective depending on how sugary you like your breakfast.  The aftertaste wasn't bad, washed down with coffee.  I plan on finishing the box, but will have it as either a midday or evening snack, after my tastebuds have woken up a bit more.  Sunrise is a little early for me to consume something so sweet.

I love it! I consider the sweetness appropriately mild, and it works well with the cereal's crunchy texture.There are crispy flakes, puffed balls, puffed rice and little crunchy bits all of which keep their crunch until I'm finished. The subtle vanilla flavor is just right and it makes the leftover milk delicious, too.I love cereal, and in particular, I'm a fan of certain kid-targeted sweetened ones (such as the peanut butter cereal with a sea captain mascot). I can express in all fairness that this is not a sugary, jitter-inducing breakfast; Nature's Path Crunchy Vanilla Sunrise is more adult-friendly in that regard, and if I tried this when I was a child I would have loved it then too.I am willing to buy this cereal in the future, and I highly recommend that other cereal eaters try this one as well.

column9: Good for people with gluten intolerance and not so good for Pre-diabetics
column10: I have never written a review for cereal so here goes. I have enjoyed eating several different cereals made by Nature's Path.The price is a little high for me but I am excited to the company's committment to be organic ingredients and having a great source of fiber and very desirable ingredients such as flax, amaranth, quinoa.It tastes like it has a bit too much vanilla. I would prefer less pronounced flavors. The vanilla taste goes very well with bananas but sort of clashes with the strawberries and blueberries that I usually but on my cereal. I usualy eat cereal with greek yogurt and it seemed to go well with it. I will mix the rest of the cereal with another without so much flavor. I do love buckwheat and wouldn't mind more of a buckwheat flaver. Not so sure that I like to think that I am eating vanilla cookies when I am eating cereal.The sugar is 7 grams which is just a bit too sweet for me as I am a prediabetic. Cane sugar and molasses, even if they are organic are not great for diabetics and others who need to watch their carbs. I would like to suggest to the company to add a little banner on the cereals that are best for diabetics and pre-diabetic. I think that would be very helpful and might increase their sales.The nutritional pluses are many, this cereal is very low in fat, 1 gram, has no chloesterol, the sodium is 130 mg which is pretty good. But since I am seeking more fiber, I would pick one of the other cereals they make over this one because the fiber is only 3mg, it is too sweet for me and I need a higher protein cereal.

column9: This Will Not Be Making It Into My Breakfast Rotation
column10: We love granola and organic cereals in our house, and I have reviewed other types of cereals for Amazon before.  We have several boxes of Nature's Path cereals and granola in our pantry right now, but this one will not be kept in our rotation.  Let me start by saying that I appreciate the good-for-you ingredients that Nature's Path uses in their cereals.  They  are usually pretty low in fat, the sugar is not off the charts like most commercially prepared, highly sugared brands, and you can actually read the list of ingredient without finding lost of additives, preservatives, and just plain bad for you ingredients--they are spot on when it comes to that stuff.  The cereal ingredients read like a Who's Who List of great for you foods you should be eating.  It's just the taste of this cereal that has lead me to a less than stellar review.I tried some of the cereal before adding any milk to it, and my first thought was that the cereal had a very fake sugar smell to it.  The bigger puffs in the box reminded me of Cap'n Crunch and it was certainly not the taste I was going for.  When adding the milk, the cereal got soggy faster that I had hoped, and the flavor seemed non-descript.  I know the box says Vanilla Sunrise, but there was absolutely no hint of vanilla, and the after taste left me feeling like I ate some really fake cereal.  This is not what I am used to with Nature's Path products.I can highly recommend Nature's Path Love Crunch Premium Organic Granola, Dark Chocolate and Red Berries 11.5-Ounce (Pack of 6), a product I have already reviewed, Nature's Path Organic Acai Apple Granola with Pomegranate, 11.5-Ounce Boxes, (Pack of 4) and Natures Path Pomegranate Plus Granola (1x25lb)., but I can not recommend this cereal.

I love trying different healthy cereal options, and the latest to make its way to my cereal bowl is Crunchy Vanilla Sunrise from Nature's Path.  I found this to be a pleasant tasting cereal with a good crunch.  It is made almost exclusively of organic ingredients, and nothing on the nutrition label seems out of line.  Here's the bonus:  it is also gluten free.  I have a family member on a gluten free diet, and it is nice to have an option that is affordable, tastes good, healthy, and gluten free.  So you may be wondering, "Is there a downside?"  The only thing to be cautious about is the cost.  The box of cereal is only 10.6 oz., and it is not cheap (however nothing gluten free is).  Other than the cost, there's really nothing not to like.  I recommend this to anyone looking for something healthy, gluten free, and vanilla flavored.

I went on a gluten-free diet a while ago and one thing that didn't impress me, was just how expensive it all was, and how puny the boxes were. I'm sorry to say, but Nature's Path Crunchy Vanilla is yet another underfilled box of mediocre cereal with an oddly cloying vanilla-y aftertaste that tastes slightly burnt. Yes there are a number of different grains inside. Yes, the concept is a good idea, but taste is the most important thing for me, and this tastes bad. In fact, 20 minutes after I had it for breakfast, I still taste that weird vanilla flavor.I guess if you must eat gluten-free and the idea of a vanilla cereal is appealing, you might give this a whirl. But for me, when I buy a bag of cereal and the box is tiny and at least 1/3 air, then I feel that I've been cheated, regardless of possible explanations of settling. This box is puny enough as it is, without the underfilling.I didnt like it. It tasted bad, and when I buy cereal, I want a full box.

column9: A delicious vanilla cereal that's not just for breakfast!
column10: A warm, real vanilla breakfast cereal with a variety of crunchy textures ranging from flakes to puffs to crispies. Oh, did I mention REAL vanilla?? And organic?? AND....it's GLUTEN FREE! An amazingly tasty, organic, gluten free cereal! We are all entitled to our opinion, thus the variety of reviews. However, where a comparison was made between Special K (vitamins) and this cereal (lack thereof), I need to say that Special K is not organic. You can't really compare the two (again, just *my* opinion).This cereal rocks with soy milk, or if you really want an extra sweet treat, vanilla almond milk! We eat this straight up, right out of the box too. It's great as a little pick me up snack in the middle of the afternoon....anyway you eat Nature's Path Crunchy Vanilla Sunrise cereal, you can't go wrong.

I really enjoyed this cereal.  It has crispy flakes, seeds, puffs and other textures that make a nice combination.  One thing I especially appreciated was that the vanilla flavor was not overdone.  Other cereals say vanilla and then it is too much vanilla.  This vanilla was just right.  Another thing I appreciated was that the cereal is not hard on my teeth.  Some granola-type cereals are so crunchy and hard that I hurt my teeth.  This was the perfect texture. I recommend this product and will purchase it again.

This is a really delicious cereal.  Natures Path usually has good stuff, so I can't say I'm surprised, but I find myself eating this as a snack as well as for breakfast. I love the Vanilla flavor and it stays crunchy in milk just like Kashi lean does.  I would definitely buy this again.

First the box itself is rather plain upon first looking at it-that was my first impression.  The taste was not that special and the aftertaste in your mouth after was the worst-will not buy this product again!  Try something else!

I love this cereal.  I first had it at my sisters and now I am hooked.  I love the fact that it has good grains and that it is organic so this seems a good cereal (as cereals go).  I love the taste a little sweet and crunch.  And the price at $3.10 a box is really good.
A blend of Flax fakes, rice crisps and another puffed grain that is slightly sweetened. The tastiest of the GF that I have found--- only wish it was more widely available.

column9: A little too sweet and left a funny aftertaste
column10: This is an interesting cereal, but only won one one front:Texture: 5 out of 5 - the mixture of different textures in the cereal is a real winner, and it stayed crunchy in milkFlavor: 3 out of 5 - though the vanilla flavor was subtle, on the whole it was a bit too sweetAftertaste: 0 out of 5 - the cereal left an odd aftertaste behind after I finished it. The first time it happened I thought it might be fluke, so I gave it a couple more tries as different times of day - still the odd aftertaste was there.Unfortunately, this cereal was just not a winner.

column9: Who knew something that tastes so good could be so good for you?
column10: When I got ready to try this cereal, I got a bit nervous reading the box.  Clearly, a product with all organic ingredients, nothing artificial, that's high in fiber and has omega-3s was going to be good for me, but how would it taste?  At first bite I was very pleasantly surprised.  The cereal has a great, crispy-puffy texture and a vanilla sweetness that I'm pretty sure even kids would like.  It gives me energy to get through the morning and keeps me full til lunchtime.  It would be great as a snack or even a crunchy topping for vanilla ice cream.  I enjoy eating this every morning and will definitely buy this cereal in the future.

column9: Possibly the best `healthy' cereal out there right now...
column10: I'm still trying to figure out how this cereal tastes like a rice crispy treat.  I mean, this is healthy and delicious, and that isn't to say that other healthier cereals don't taste good, but this one is exceptional because it doesn't have that earthy `healthy' taste to it.  It tastes sugary and sweet and like dessert.  This cereal hits all marks for me.  It coats my mouth with wonderful sweetness and the contrasting textures are delightful on my tongue.  I love the rice puffs that pop in your mouth.  For a cereal that is gluten free, low in calories and sugar content, this is remarkable.  One of the best cereals that I have ever eaten, and sure to be a household staple here.  We love cereal, and my entire household agrees that this is TOP NOTCH.  Some may find the sweetness a little rich, and so a smaller bowl may be necessary, but a serving size does the trick, and thus the box can last a little longer.

A pleasant surprise! Something with a curiosity in it. Has a tip of sugar. You may need less even if your are diabetic.The photo of it on the box did not give me a hint of how it would taste, so I tried it with milk. It was great!For the elderly I feel it could have had a tiny bit less sugar. Great product though.

This cereal tastes very good. It has some fiber, but not a lot, which is good. Many people don't want high fiber cereal. Others do not want a low fiber cereal, so this one meets both requirements; it has just the right amount of fiber, 3g.My only complaint is that part of it is buffed balls, so the box does not have the same weight as other boxes of natural cereal. Otherwise, I highly recommend this cereal.
I have no problems with gluten or lactose,  this combo just tastes great.This cereal is healthy,  with great taste and texture. What more could you ask of a cereal?You want organic? It's that too!

column9: Overly sweet but otherwise tasteless and blah
column10: It's possible that this product is aimed at children: with its cloying super-sweetness and otherwise bland, cardboard-like taste, it resembles Trix, the cereal so loved by that Silly Rabbit. But the hype of the cereal seems aimed at adults, with its "Nature's Path" brand and claims of gluten-free whole grain goodness and flax seed. For me, the real question is, why bother? There are so many yummy gluten free cereals now on the market, my favorites being Trader Joe's varieties of GF granola, which are delicious, that this product will not be on my radar screen. It's just not tasty enough to compete.

column9: There are better choices out there
column10: This cereal is masquerading as healthy.  Yes, it is organic and gluten-free, but it also is a processed food containing a fair amount of sugar at 7g per serving (second ingredient is organic evaporated cane juice) and gets its fiber from added inulin (and maybe additional sweetening from this ingredient), rather than just from whole grains.  The major grain constituents of corn meal/flour and brown rice flour are not the healthiest grain ingredients but might be needed to get a decent gluten free cereal (this contains no oats, which are also gluten free).  The amount of fiber per serving is 3g, not too great for a healthy cereal.  This is not a fortified cereal, so Vitamin A, C and calcium are 0% and iron only 4% of RDA.The package is somewhat deceptive in that it lists a serving as having relatively low calories (110 calories), but the reason becomes evident when looking into the serving size.  The cereal serving size is 2/3c = 30g = 1.10 oz, which is smaller when compared to standard natural cereal serving sizes (which I have found to be more in the 1.5 to 1.8 oz range), so this is the reason that the calories appear lower.  Possibly this serving size may be more appropriate for children.  As an adult, eating only 1.10 oz of this cereal does not fill me up.The cereal tastes pretty good, if you like a sweet cereal, and I think kids would like this.  It appears to be a mixture of organic versions of Kix (hollow corn spheres), tiny Rice Krispies and some kind of fiber flakes, with tiny bits of other stuff (possibly sugar coated puffed quinoa etc).  Maybe it has a hint of vanilla flavor, but it mostly tasted sweet to me.  It was quite good with fresh sliced strawberries on top and regular milk.  The cereal did not appear as appetizing as the glossy photo on the package.The box is only 10.6oz, so it won't last long if increasing the amount per serving and thus is not the best value.  I suppose this cereal may be a good option for people who need a tasty/sugary gluten-free cereal.  But there certainly are healthier and cheaper options out there (even standard oatmeal).  Rated 2 1/2 stars, rounded down to 2 stars.

I was pretty excited about trying this product.  I like most of the nature's path products that I've tried but I try to avoid the products that contain natural flavors.  The only gluten free cereal they carry that doesn't contain natural flavors are their Peanut Butter Panda Puffs.  Of course Nature's Path makes way way way better cereal than the conventional brands, but I am very fussy about what I put into my body & don't want to pay top dollar for additives.At first bite I was disappointed.  My first thought was, "This doesn't taste like vanilla at all."  I kept eating & then thought it tasted odd. It is hard to describe but there is a slight lingering bitterness. I doubt I will eat this again.  To make matters worse, it is not filling at all.  I usually juice in the morning & find juicing is more filling than this.  Plus juicing is much more nutritious.  I also don't care for the addition of inulin or vitamin e.Last there is nothing like a cereal calling itself Crunchy Vanilla Sunrise & it doesn't even contain vanilla!  Nature's Path says (on the back of the box) "Please don't confuse "vanilla" with "ordinary."  Maybe we should ask Natures Path if they are confused about what real vanilla is.  Ingredients as per the box:  Organic whole grain corn meal, organic evaporated cane juice, organic brown rice flour, organic yellow corn flour, organic inulin, organic quinoa puffs, organic flax seeds, natural vanilla flavor (natural vanilla flavor does not equal organic vanilla from an organic vanilla bean), organic buckwheat flour, organic quinoa, sea salt, organic amaranth, organic molasses, tocopherols (natural vitamin E) (lets hope the E is from GMO free sources!).A much healthier gluten free option is to make your own hot cereal & add REAL organic vanilla.  My favorite is Organic Raw Sun Cured Whole Vanilla Bean Powder.  I use it all the time.  Cereal, tea, smoothies you name it!  If you have a food mill you can even make your own rice cereal by simply grinding the rice to flour & cooking it just as you would the hot rice cereal you buy in the store.  Oatmeal is another tasty option.  The bonus is not only does it taste amazing but in the end you save tons of money & eat organic.  It's a win win!

Other reviewers have gotten into more specifics regarding nutrition, so I'm not gonna flog a dead horse with any more specifics.  Here's the bottom line:This cereal is packaged in a way to give the impression that it is natural and therefore healthy.  It is NOT a very healthy option for your breakfast.However, despite the unfortunate attempts at deception from the packaging, I can say that this cereal was really tasty, so for flavor alone, it'll get 3 stars.I won't be buying it again though, not only because I don't want to support a company that charges a higher price for sugary cereal on the false basis that its somehow better for you than all those more common sugary cereals, but also because I probably only got two bowls of cereal out of this box and it's hardly worth the price for two days of breakfast.

OK - so I was expecting card board ... I like to joke about what my father-in-law once told me while he was attempting to diet:  here was his rule for staying thin, "if it tastes like card board it is OK; if it tastes good, spit it out!"  This stuff tastes great.  It is very crunchy, and has a wholesome sweetness to it.  I loved it, the kids loved it, and my wife loved it.  I ate it every day until the box was empty.  Will you like it?  I can't say, because taste is well ... a matter of taste.  So you can make a mental comparison; here are some of my favorite cereals:  shredded mini wheat, golden grahams, and grape nuts.

I love cereal--I mean, I can't believe I am saying this, but I actually love breakfast cereals more as an adult than when I was a kid. Sometimes, I have cereal for dinner when I am not feeling too hungry. I am more of a "Special K" kind of dude just to let you know and I am really not into all the "organic food" hoopla that has been making waves in the media for the past few years.Took a chance and got a new cereal that is "gluten-free" (whatever that meant) and is `USDA organic'. Again, I eat what I eat because I want to, and I try to maintain a balanced diet. I am not all into this obsessive healthy diet, but I have to admit I was very impressed with Nature's Path "Crunchy Vanilla Sunrise".I don't know how to start a review on cereal. Well, this stuff tastes really good and is lightly sweet (but it leaves a sweeter after taste). You can really taste the natural flavors around it. The corn, rice, flax, quinoa, buckwheat and amaranth are all blended together pretty well and the flavors do go well with each other. It has that `crunch' that I usually go for and while I don't have a kid, I can say that maybe a kid will like this cereal. I even topped it with some blueberries and bananas at times, and boy, it tastes even better. Also, one thing I look for is the fact that it does not get soggy for awhile after being immersed in milk. It kept its crunchy texture (but smooth) while I was eating it. One complaint, the vanilla taste is a little subtle, and I could taste more honey in it.Now keep in mind, I only had one bowl of this cereal to do this review, so just how I'll feel about it after repeat servings, is yet to be told. I cannot say anything about its "repeat servings" as of yet.Very impressed with this product and I think I may just have to use this as a snack even without milk. It is good....like what I like with my cereals. It is a little pricey at $ 10 a box, but hey, it is one of great quality. It is up to you if a cereal for $ 10 is worth it.

This cereal is far too sweet for me.  I was barely able to eat the first (and only) bowl I poured for myself.  Not wanting to waste it, I have been mixing small amounts in with my trail mix, but there is no way I could eat another bowl of this.Anytime the second ingredient listed on the box is a sweetener, in this case evaporated cane juice, I have to wonder what flavors they're trying to mask with the cloying sweetness.  With a combination of corn, brown rice, amaranth, quinoa, flax seeds, and buckwheat I think there would be plenty of potential for good flavor combinations.  Unfortunately, all I could taste was the sugar.

column9: Delicious, but less than half a bag each?!
column10: While I don't buy 'real' healthy cereals very often, I'm always up for trying new ones. And face it- when there's a cereal called Crunchy Vanilla Sunrise, it pretty much tells you that you're in for a good meal. With high expectations...I was right. So right, that I took care of the whole box within a day. No, THAT wasn't a very healthy thing to do, but my god was this cereal great. It looked like some kind of rabbit food when I poured some into a bowl, but upon taking the first bite, I was in love. Crunchy, but not super crunchy. Vanilla, but not super vanilla-y. Sunrise...well, the sun -was- shining when I was eating it!There are only so many things you can say about a food that you like in a review, because the only way if you know you'll like it is by getting some for yourself. Anyone who loves vanilla flavored cereals should like this stuff. It seems like a lot of people here aren't too big on the taste, but I didn't have any problems with it at all. As soon as my first bowl was over, I moonwalked back to the kitchen and poured another. It's a heck of a lot lower in sugar than nearly everything else I get, though I suppose health nuts will always find something to throw a fit about.I was on the fence on giving it 3 or 4 stars because I love the flavor so much, but there's one glaring problem. Someone posted an image above in the Customer Images section, and that's exactly how my cereal was as well. And if you're one of those people that really does go by the Serving Size listed on the size of the box, this stuff isn't going to fill you up very well. When you see how much you're getting by buying a pack of 3 here...for the price, it doesn't seem like a good deal compared to buying 2 bigger boxes of a similar cereal.Problems aside, if you don't mind buying this stuff in bulk, you should be happy.

column9: Very sweet vanilla taste overpowers this cereal
column10: I'd say if you love vanilla, you will surely gobble this dish up!  But for me, I found the vanilla flavor too overpowering.  Even with today's sugary cereals, my favorite being Frosted Flakes, I can still taste the milk over them.  But with this Nature's Path cereal, even with a lot of milk, all I could taste was vanilla.

column9: Yummy Yummy for my Tummy Tummy
column10: To put this simply, this breakfast cereal is absolutely delicious.  I at times become dubious with all natural and organic products, because natural and organic might be good for you but it doesn't equate to good taste.  However this cereal is really very tasty and it is healthy.  In addition, it really isn't loaded with calories and sugar.  A plus is this product is also cholesterol and gluten free.This cereal is a combination of puff rice, corn (?) flakes and puffed oats (?).  The flavor is rather sweet and no too much of an overbearing taste of vanilla.  The box displayed the cereal with bananas, so I decided to eat mine with bananas and use almond soy milk. YUM!!! Wow, what a real treat this cereal is. Again it is nice that this natural and organic breakfast cereal doesn't taste like cardboard.The one set back is the size of the box; it is barely 11oz and not for nothing but the bag was just about half full.  I can maybe understand Nature's Path wanting to make a smaller package for cost and profit but fill the bag up.  I do not believe my bag was 10.6oz.  I suppose that is the price of eating well.
