Maybe that is why this country has such an obesity problem.  I digress, this is an excellent tasting product and if I was certain my next box would be more than half full, I would grab it in a heart beat.

Though I don't need to eat gluten free foods, I know people who do and can remember a time when there were less choices and those on a gluten free diet had to settle. Those days are long gone. Nature's Path Crunchy Vanilla Sunrise is gluten free, organic, free of synthetic pesticides and herbicides, free of irradiation, and even is packed in an Enviro Box. And the list of "good" stuff goes on and one.But what about the taste? My first impression is that it's overly sweet, sure to be a hit with kids. As I finished off the box, I got more used to the sweetness and it became less obtrusive. Sprinkling a handful of unsweetened blueberries on top of my bowl of cereal actually hit the spot quite nicely.The cereal is pleasantly crunchy and its variety of shapes and textures and cereal types adds some visual interest also. As I reach the bottom of the box, I ponder whether I would buy a new replacement box. Since the taste of this crunchy vanilla sunrise is more OK than outstanding, I'd probably only buy it if it could be had for a outstanding sale price.

column9: Disappointed by the overly sweet taste and vanilla aftertaste.
column10: I'm already a fan of the Nature's Path organic cereals but have not seen this one in the store.  I don't know if that means it is a new product or just that my mega-monopoly chain (the only grocery chain we have in town) just doesn't stock this one.  I have tried four or five of the different varieties of Nature's Path and have enjoyed them with varying degrees of success.  I'm sorry to say this is the one I like least and I'm disappointed.First off, there are only 10.6 ounces of cereal in the box.  Compared to the normal 14 ounce weight in other products by this brand that makes this box a little short on quantity.  I think that is probably because of the puffed grains which take up more volume in the box.  There are puffs, flakes, and grain/seed shapes.  The  impression I got with the first bite of dry cereal was *sweet*.  In fact, very sweet. The sweetness is sprayed on each component in the mix and adds up to more sweet taste than I like.  The smell I got was *vanilla*.  Once I poured the milk on my 2/3 cup portion size the cereal stayed crunchy for quite a long time, but eventually it did get soggy.  I think that's simply something you have to accept with flake shapes in a cereal.  I thought it was too sweet and the vanilla flavoring left a decided aftertaste which is rather unpleasant.This is a gluten free cereal which can be very important to people with gluten intolerance or allergies.  I'm seeing more and more cereals with this attribute so that's got to be a very good thing.  The numbers on this cereal aren't very impressive otherwise.  The grain mix is organic whole grain corn meal, organic brown rice flour, organic yellow corn flour, organic quinoa puffs, organic flax seeds, organic buckwheat flour and organic amaranth.  In addition to the organic evaporated cane juice there is also organic molasses.  I have to admit to not knowing what organic inulin is.  At 110 calories per 2/3 cup serving that is neither good nor bad, it has 12g of whole grains of the recommended 48g per day, again, neither good nor bad.  Total fat is 1g, but the vitamin and mineral counts are either very low or non-existent.  It is certified USDA Organic and the company is going out of it's way to promote the family farms in rural communities.  All very good, but it doesn't actually make this particular cereal taste very good.I buy other Nature's Path cereals and enjoy them very much.  This one does not have that holding power to keep away hunger until lunch time that I'm looking for.  For me it tastes too sweet to eat as a snack dry from the box plus some of those seeds are itty bitty, so I'll finish off this box as a breakfast food in a bowl with milk, a dollop of yogurt and some fresh fruit and then go back to my other varieties that I like more.  And the aftertaste is really quite pronounced.  That I don't care for at all.EDIT:  I looked up organic inulin and found that it is an organic agave sweetner.  Yikes!  THREE sweetners in this cereal??

I eat cereal every day and always look for different varieties which are low fat and with new flavors so I was excited to get these. First Amazon does not ship dry packaged goods well. This is one of several boxes of food that has arrived at my house either crushed or in crumbs. After getting beyond the look, the flavor left a bitter after taste. I enjoy vanilla, but I suspect that the extract in the cereal created this effect. The cereal itself includes flakes, rice crisps and puffs-too much going on for one cereal. The manufacturer needs to stick with one look and perfect that.All in all I would not recommend this cereal. There are better ones out there and for less money too.

I wanted to like this cereal--it has fiber and whole grains and no gluten and and and. It consists of little flakes sort of like Special K, little vanilla "cocoa puffs" style spheres, and Rice Krispies dealies. It has 7 grams of sugar per serving, which is more than the 3 grams nutritionists recommend, but far less than many other cereals. Only 3 grams of dietary fiber (from gas-producing inulin--not a natural foodstuff, btw) and 2 of protein are kind of measly for this kind of cereal, but the biggest drawback for me is the vanilla flavor--it tastes off--like cheap, fake vanilla, although the ingredients list says it's "natural vanilla flavor."Nature's Path? Hmm--not exactly the Road Less Travelled....

column9: Crunchy, lots of different textures, but a bit too much vanilla
column10: I LOVE cereal! I also like vanilla and frequently put a splash of vanilla extract in my coffee.Although this cereal sounds perfect, I didn't like it that much.  It wasn't bad, but it was not my taste.  I am giving it 4 stars because, although I didn't like it there is nothing inherently bad about it and taste is so subjective.Anyway, here are some pro and cons (really? pros and cons about a cereal...it can be done)Pros:Crunchy, softens slightly in milk (yet doesn't turn into a slushy mess)Widely varied textures that make it really nice to chewGluten free for those on a restricted dietCons:Taste was a bit too vanilla for meSticky when eaten dry out of the box (not great for snacking)

The mail lady delivered my sample box of this cereal just as we were finishing lunch, so my husband and I both had some for dessert.Some reviewers have commented on a burnt flavour: I think they're tasting the buckwheat. Buckwheat is not my favourite grain and it was really rather potent as I started eating the bowl, but seemed to wear off as I got close to done eating. My husband noticed that the coating on the cereal wore off and left his water all flavourful that he poured on his (I had mine with soy milk). The cereal didn't have much taste outside of the sweet coating; I did not find that it was too sweet too start with. I couldn't taste any vanilla at all. My husband thought the sodium content was a bit excessive (130mg per serving).I do think it's a bit overpriced for what you get and the fact that it's really not *that* impressive of a taste. I really like the Mesa Sunrise corn flakes and was expecting something a little more akin to that, so in that regard I was disappointed. Still, this wasn't horrible cereal. I wouldn't go out and buy it, but I would eat it again were it to be at someone's house, because with all the grains it's still a better option than most highly refined commercial cereals.

column9: Good, not great - would probably buy again....
column10: I have to eat gluten free, so this was something I was looking forward to.  It was good, but not great, in my opinion.  Somehow, the little crunchy balls did not go well with the flakes - it was like I'd mixed two different cereals.  Some people may not mind that at all, I just happen to prefer the same texture in a breakfast cereal.I liked that the ingredients were (typical of Nature's Path) a cut above most anything found on regular grocery store shelves.  And the fact that it's organic is a huge plus.The subtle vanilla flavor was not overpowering, and the cereal did not require anything else on it (extra sugar, maple syrup, etc.).  I happen to use vanilla flavored almond milk, and the extra vanilla flavor was not too much.  Regardless of what it's in (milk, nut milk, soy milk, etc.), it is great all by itself.Would I buy it again?  Yes, for variety.  But I purchase several Nature's Path products in the large eco-packs to save time and packaging, and even if these become offered in the large eco-pack bags, I don't expect to be buying that much at a time.  Again - nothing at all wrong with them - actually quite good - it's just not going to be my favorite breakfast cereal.

column9: Yummy, but with a bit of an after taste.
column10: This is a gluten free product.  I have never had a gluten free product nor do I have any medical need for one.This was a yummy, crunchy cereal.  As an out of the box snack, it was a little sticky, so be prepared to have to wash your hands or have wipes.  It held up well in milk, but by the end of the bowl (which was the recommended size) it was getting a little soggy.The cereal does have a very strong, but not unpleasant, aftertaste of vanilla.  This was less noticeable in milk than from the box.  If vanilla is not your thing, you probably wouldn't like this.  But if you like vanilla, you will.  I would get this again, even though I do not need gluten free food.

Nature's Path "Organic Crunchy Vanilla Sunrise" is a delicious cereal.Unfortunately cereals are not healthy, but as far as cereals go this is one of the better ones.The sugar to fiber ratio is 2.3 to 1 (7 grams of sugar for every 3 grams of fiber).  The "best" cereals are about 1:1.  As a rule of thumb I won't eat anything with a sugar to fiber ratio higher than 3 to 1, so Crunchy Vanilla Sunrise qualifies as acceptable.If you are going to eat cereal, this is a good organic choice.I'm very impressed by Nature Path's program to buy land and allow organic farmers to use the land for free.The primary ingredient in Crunchy Vanilla Sunrise is corn. ("organic whole grain corn meal")  Followed by sugar and then organic brown rice flour.  There are eleven more ingredients and none of them are "incomprehensible chemical names".  The only potentially "bad" ingredient is "natural vanilla flavor" (which technically could be darn near anything).All in all, a fairly good cereal with a very nice flavor.  Enjoy it in moderation.

column9: Good Taste, Lower Protein, Lower Sugar, Higher Price, Gluten Free!
column10: This is a good tasting cereal with lots of nice crunch. Compared to a granola or GoLean Crunch, it gets soggy a little faster, on par with a regular flake cereal, such as Special K. But other than that, it is a nice addition to a  gluten free pantry.  I added dried cranberries, and thought it tasted good.We don't have to be gluten free, but we try to cut down here and there. I use soy milk on my cereal, and I'm going to compare Crunchy Vanilla Sunrise to my favorite cereal, GoLean Crunch, by Kashi.Vanilla Sunrise is quite a bit more expensive than GoLean Crunch. The boxes are about the same size, but one Sunrise holds 10.6 oz, while GoLean holds 15 oz, which means there was a bit of empty space in the Sunrise box. (I realize that, from the grocer's point of view, they like having boxes approximately the same size.)I compared amazon prices for the two cereals (which of course can change): 3 boxes Sunrise cost $0.35 per ounce. 4 boxes of GoLean cost $0.22 per ounce.Here's the comparison of some nutrition amounts for one cup of Sunrise to one cup of GoLean. You can compare these numbers to your favorite cereal:Calories:  165 Sunrise,  190 GoLeanSodium:  195mg Sunrise,  100mg GoLeanCarbohydrates total:  37g Sunrise,  37g GoLeanCarbohydrates from sugar:  10g Sunrise,  13g GoLeanProtein:  3g Sunrise,  9g GoLeanOverall, this is a tasty cereal and I like having the occasional gluten free choice.

With so many options for breakfast fare, it's great to see more available in gluten-free.  This one is packed with very healthy grains such as quinoa and actually tastes good.  It has a lot of vanilla flavor, which may or not be a hit for you, I found it a little overly cloying with milk but overall a pleasantly tasting cereal for one so healthy.  Great for snacking on its own or even better in the traditional milk added breakfast, and would be especially good with fruit added.

column4: Eustacia Vye "a lover of books and everything...
column10: The first thing that came to mind when I opened this box, is that the cereal looked like a mixture of Kix, rice crisps, and corn flakes.  Unlike those serials, Nature's Path Crunchy Vanilla Sunrise is very tasty. The sweetness with hints of vanilla is yummy.  Plus, unlike most "crunchy cereals" this one is nut free (but made in a factory where nuts are used).. an added bonus for those who can't have nuts.My only gripe about this cereal is that it is very sweet... almost too sweet.  The main ingredients are corn and sugar.  At 7g of sugar per 2/3 cup, I find it too sugary for a healthy cereal.  Because of the sugar content, I will probably pass in the future as I prefer Annie's Cinna Bunnies if I need a sugary treat.

I am a big fan of eating cereal any time of the day, especially for breakfast. It's fast, convenient, and a healthy start to the day. I was excited about tasting this cereal because it is gluten-free and contains quinoa, which Dr. Oz says is a must for any diet. On first inspection, the cereal looks as if it's a combination of Corn Pops, Rice Krispies, and Wheaties. It has a lot going on in one box. In terms of taste, it has a vanilla flavoring that lingers in your mouth long after you have eaten it. Not very appealing! As for  the nutritional value, I was surprised at the lack thereof. Comparing Original Special K (serving size is one cup) to the Crunchy Vanilla Sunrise (serving size is 2/3 cup) without adding any milk, SK has 15% Vitamin A of the daily recommended amount and CVS has 0%. As for vitamin C, SK has 35% and CVS has 0% and sugars SK has 4g and CVS has 7g. It doesn't look like the Crunchy Vanilla Sunrise is all that healthy. Overall, if you like the taste, it's probably better than eating a sugary cereal; however, I wouldn't buy it.

With the typical Kellogg's or Post cereal, the choice mostly depends on taste.  With Nature's Path cereal, other considerations come into play.  This cereal is produced using no synthetic pesticides or herbicides, using no irradiation, contains no artificial preservatives or additives, and no genetically engineered seeds or ingredients.  It was produced on farms that use enriched drought resistant soil, produce less soil erosion, less groundwater pollution, and practice improved farm biodiversity.  If supporting products of this type matters for you, then you will probably be predisposed to buy this cereal.  Still, though, in the end it has to taste good if you are going to continue buying it.  I think it does taste very good.  The best way to describe the taste is as being like rice krispies, but with a strong vanilla flavor.So, if the price seems reasonable and you want to support this type of product, you won't find yourself sacrificing taste.

column9: Changed their formula: taste like Vanilla & Cornmeal
column10: I love Nature's Path, however with this cereal I am not disappointed, but I am not impressed either.First off, if you take a look at the pictures, you see will see a good mix of Corn, Rice, Flax, Quinoa, Buckwheat & Amaranth. However, it appears that when Nature's Path change the look on their boxes, they also change their formula. Mines was about 70% cornmeal, 30% everything else. I have uploaded a photo so hopefully you can see what I saw (should be one of the very last photos in the gallery).Because mines was 70% cornmeal, the cereal DID taste like vanilla but it had a cornmeal aftertaste. If you take a long time with your cereal, slowly the vanilla transfers onto the milk, and the cereal mostly take like cornmeal.Now if you like the taste of corn, that's fine. But I was expecting more flavors particularly the flax and amaranth, but those flavors were lost in the mix.This product IS however 100% organic except for natural vanilla flavor, sea salt, and tocopherols (natural vitamin E). Compare to other cereals, it is low in calories (110), contains no cholesterol, and is high in fiber (12% of your daily values). However, because it is organic with very little added to it, it is low in nutrition compare to other non-organic cereals such as special K. It only has 4% iron (surprisingly, Vitamin E is not listed as a nutrition even though it is listed as an ingredient).Other pros of the cereal is that it contains 0.15g of Omega 3 per serving, which is 11% of the recommended daily value of 1.3gIt is also gluten-free for those who can't consume gluten as well as certified USDA organic. My cereal box expired Nov 02 2012.The box says that Nature's Path change their boxes by making their packages smaller to reduce 10% of their impact on the planet by saving on water, energy and paperboard. However, I am also 100% convinced that their also change their formula to include more of the cheaper cornmeal and include less of the more expensive ingredients.

column9: whole corn grain? call it cornmeal!
column10: This is marketed as a whole grain gluten free cereal. Sounds healthy and yummy and hip, right? Wrong! It is corn (not organic!!!) + evaporated cane juice + some other thing in trace amounts. Might as well call rice crispies a whole grain cereal and an excellent source of iron. Taste was just ok, nothing special. Not buying it. Ever.

I like the flavorful aspect of this cereal.  The individual flavors blended well, but the burst of vanilla was a surprise.  I think the kids might even like the flavor enough to not even realize this is a healthy choice.  With so many "empty" choices out there, this is the great alternative.  A healthy good tasting breakfast cereal is now not an oxymoron.

column9: Lots of sugar for a "Healthy" Cereal
column10: Okay so I got this because I was hoping for a healthy good tasting cereal.  Though I don't really buy into the gluten free hype (because I'm not allergic to wheat which is the only real reason to go gluten free) I figured that since I like Vanilla this might be a good option.Okay so first of all this is a cereal that is heavy on the sugar for something that looks "healthy" and for something with all of that sugar it certainly doesn't taste as good as it seems like it should.  This is like a grown up's kiddie cereal.  If you like it then go ahead and buy it, but don't believe that it's an overly healthy choice.  There are far tastier healthier choices on the market to go for.  This isn't something that I will be purchasing in the near future.

column9: Another Great Natures Path Gluten-free product!
column10: This is a delicious cereal.  crunchy and flavorful.  I would recommend it if you are on a Gluten-free diet or not!  : )

With the name "Crunchy Vanilla Sunrise" and touting various whole grains, I expected more of an "adult" cereal--wholesome and natural.  I was a little surprised to open it and see the air-puffed cereal.  If I can compare the cereal to other common ones, it's like a mix of Kix, Rice Krispies, and flakes all mixed together with vanilla flavor and a crunch. It does taste good, and I'm sure kids would like it.  In fact, it seems like their market should be for kids with health-conscious parents.I'm glad that Nature's Path is making a cereal using some less common grains (even though corn still is at the top of the list).  All the grains are organic and non-gmo.  This cereal is gluten-free, and I promise you won't miss the wheat.It has 7 grams of sugar per serving, which may be fine for some people, but it's too sweet for me.  It's sweetened with evaporated cane juice and molasses. I think they could cut some of the sugar and still have a delicious cereal because of its natural vanilla flavor.Try and see if you like it, but just don't expect a granola-like cereal.

Nature's Path is a family-owned organic food company. This cereal is their all-organic, gluten-free breakfast cereal. It has a nice, healthy mix of grains, but the real downer is the taste. Somehow, their many ingredients do not add up to a robust and pleasing taste. Instead, the cereal has the taste and texture of wet cardboard.It is a healthy cereal, and anyone who has Celiac disease would probably move to have it. But, really, there are better choices out there.

column9: Needs more protein and a better flavor.
column10: My kids have to eat gluten-free, so we're always interested in trying new Gluten-free products. They were excited about this one and they both loved the flavor. Personally, i thought it had a good vanilla flavor, but just as strong was the flavor of flax seed and cardboard. Bleh.It's also frustrating that it only has 2 grams of protein per serving. That is no where near enough to sustain kids for longer than a half hour, so in addition to the cereal i still have to fix them something else with protein in it! When will breakfast-makers realize that MORE protein is ESSENTIAL for the morning meal?? This is a constant gripe of mine though, and not exclusive to this product.I DO appreciate the high quality of the ingredients that ARE present in the cereal and the low amount of sugar in it.Overall, it is a quality product from a GOOD company. But while it has an "okay" flavor, it just doesn't have enough substance for me to buy it again for my family.

This is pretty tasty- very sweet infact with a hint of vanilla so depending on your taste that may not be a good thing. It's supposably healthy oraganic/glutten free. I would not recommend it as your everyday cereal, but all in all its yummy and the entire family liked it. We ate it dry as a snack, on icecream in yogurt ect...give it a try.

All these cereals are basically the same.  While I wasn't blown away with this cereal I liked the vanilla touch.  If you are looking for a Certified Gluten-Free, USDA Organic, Casein-Free, Soy-Free product then you will be happy with Nature's Path Crunchy Vanilla Sunrise.  I think it is too expensive as listed at $.42/ounce however.  So for that reason I gave it only 3 stars.
I asked hubby what he thought about product and he about ate it all before I could sample.  It is yummy. We are regular consumers of this brand and this flavor did not disappoint.

column9: Allegedly organic cereal with mediocre taste and texture
column10: Nature's Path Crunchy Vanilla Sunrise doesn't quite live up to its name. Certainly, there is some vanilla flavor, but it is very light and doesn't stand up to milk. There is also some crunch, but not a lot. The defining texture is more "sticky" than crunchy.All in all, it's pretty bland and uninteresting but not terrible. I suppose that if you are looking for cereal that is "organic, Non-GMO Project Verified" and full of "whole grain goodness", your options may be limited.

column4: T. Lee "God has died lots of times, but someo...
column10: This is a pleasantly vanilla-tinged breakfast cereal.  Organic and gluten free, at about $3 per 10oz box it may not be for everyone, but for those who need to worry about gluten, this cereal is definitely not a trade-off on taste.  I like the texture too, with a satisfying crunchiness that's filling.  I definitely recommend giving this a try.

I really did like this one for it has my two favorite things when it comes to a cereal: Crunchy & Sweet. I didn't think the flavor was too overdone and I could taste the vanilla just fine. In fact I tend to eat cereal with soy milk and sometimes even vanilla soy milk so I really got a huge shot of vanilla. My hubby really liked it as well and he tends to like super sugar sweet cereals and thought this was just right maybe not even sweet enough for him. This might not be for everyone since people tend to like different things but I everyone in my home really enjoyed it and so might you.

This cereal reminded my kids of Rice Crispies in terms of flavor. It has flakes that resemble Corn Flakes, puff balls that resemble Kix, and rice puffs that resemble Ricke Crispies. The kids thought they were okay, but I am sure the flavor could definitely grow on them over time. They didn't reject eating it.I really enjoyed the flavor. It was slightly sweet with a subtle vanilla flavor. I honestly liked them more for a dry snack in place of granola as opposed to having them with milk. In fact, adding in a few almonds this became a definite replacement for granola in a pinch.If you are already a eater of more healthy cereal - this will be right up your alley. If you are looking to do a diet change from some of the more traditional (high sugar, highly processed) cereal - it may take a few tries to get your palate used to the flavor. Would definitely recommend at least giving it a try. Especially if you like a slightly sweet cereal as opposed to more sugar coated sort of cereals.

This cereal has a good flavor of vanilla without being overwhelming. I have had their granola before and it was a little too noisy and crunchy for me but this cereal is just a nice amount of flakes and puffs to be filling with a good texture, without feeling like your chewing forever at a loud decibel. It's not gonna rock your breakfast world but it is good nutrition when your a mindless morning zombie.

I really enjoyed going through a box of Nature's Path Crunchy Vanilla Sunrise.  It is low in sugar and yet still very sweet.  While I'm not sure I tasted any vanilla in there, it was still pretty good.  It contains good ole flakes, small crunchies and mini-kix like cornballs.  Interestingly enough it also has Omega-3.  For a healthy, yet good tasting cereal, give Nature's Path a try today!

I was drawn to this cereal because it is a Nature's Path product.  Ienjoy their Flax Plus Multibran Flakes on a daily basis, so Iconsidered a 'crunchy vanilla' variety a welcome change of pace.  Bothproducts are touted as being whole grain, and both were advertised asorganic.A visual inspection of Vanilla Sunrise tipped me off to the play.While the multibran flakes are an earthy brown, the sunrise spin is asyellow as, well, the sun.  It seemed weaker in comparison.The first bite of Sunrise sealed the deal.  While Flax plus tastesvaguely of a piece of bread, sunrise tastes like sugar cane.  Thismight work if I was a kid switching down from Cocoa Puffs, but myadult tongue felt somewhat burned by the sunrise.To their credit, crunchy vanilla sunrise is crunchy (although the flaxplus I'm sticking with is also suitably crunchy--without the addedsugar.)  Not recommended.

I decided to give this healthy cereal a try although I am a sweet cereal lover. I recognized corn puffs and crisped rice; not sure what grain the flakes were. Overall the cereal stayed crunchy in milk and had a light vanilla taste without being overly sweet. The price is comparable to other organic products and seemed to be a better price than other GF products I've seen on the shelves. I was disappointed to see it was process in the same plant as peanuts/treenuts so those with allergies will have to skip Vanilla Sunrise. I give it 3 stars as good but just not my cup of tea.My 20yo dd poured herself a bowl and was like WOW!!! *****so that averages it out to 4 stars.

column4: David G. Schwartz "I like reading more than w...
column10: I tried Nature's Path Crunchy Vanilla Sunrise courtesy of Amazon Vine and really enjoyed it. There's lot of variety in the cereal, with all sorts of granola and cereal-type pieces. I'm not skilled enough at forensic cerealogy to identify all of them, but I do know enough to say that they all tasted great. This is a great breakfast treat, and it even works as a snack if you are so inclined.

column9: Delicious gluten-free cereal - would definitely recommend!
column10: Organic Crunchy Vanilla Sunrise cereal from Nature's Path is GLUTEN-FREE and delicious!  It contains corn, rice, flax, quinoa, buckwheat & amaranth - 110 calories in a 2/3 cup portion, with little fat some sodium (130mg), 25g carbs, 3g of dietary fiber, 2g of protein and 7g of sugar.  The second ingredient is organic evaporated can juice, so that tells you a bit about the yummy sweetness: I ate this cereal with a bowl of lightly sweetened, vanilla coconut milk from TJ's, and found the total sweetness to be a bit too much for me in the morning: I would recommend this with unsweetened coconut milk or regular skim milk.This crunchy cereal is delicious, and is something I would make part of your diet as a snack, or as an occasional breakfast food- I try to eat more protein in the mornings to start my days off right (hello eggs!), so I would not recommend this to eat daily, but if you miss cereal and want to know of a good gluten-free cereal to satisfy your cereal craving, this is it!  This would be great if you added a sliced banana to it also: would definitely recommend Nature's Path Crunchy Vanilla Sunrise: yum!

column4: Marshall Carter "Ornery Gamer, Fiend Club Member"
column9: Good-tasting cereal, but not quite as healthy as advertised...
column10: To start, let's just get the fact that I like the Nature's Path Crunchy Vanilla surprise out of the way. It's good stuff and I finished the box off a good bit more quickly than I did with the last few boxes (other cereals). It has a sweet, light vanilla taste that actually had me looking forward to breakfast, and that's a good thing (I very often skip the meal, and that does me no favors). I know some say that it's way too  sweet for them, but if your idea of what a breakfast cereal ought to be isn't a bowl full of unsweetened nuts and twigs, this isn't all that terribly sweet. Slice up half a banana and go to town...as far as cereals go, it's a satisfying breakfast (or snack). Kids would likely be a fan of this cereal as well, so there's a bonus.Now, now that I've got how it tastes out of the way, Nature's Path loses a star on the nutrition side of things. Yes, this is a gluten-free cereal that could prove to be a great alternative for this with gluten sensitivity. It's also organic, so you know that the crops that went into making this were grown without pesticides, chemical fertilizers, etc. Unfortunately, organic and gluten-free does not amount to being healthy. There's not much fiber here (3g) and it's an unfortified cereal, so there's also a lot of vitamins that you're missing here. The serving size is also rather small, making the 7g of sugar start to loom a bit more menacingly. 7g isn't too awful, but if you're eating twice the serving size (and I have to admit, that's what I did), then 14g is a whole lot worse.All-in-all, Nature's Path Crunch Vanilla Sunrise is a good-tasting, kid-friendly cereal that's ultimately not as healthy as its marketing would seem to imply. While there are definitely less healthy options out there, this isn't quite the healthy breakfast option you were looking for.

This is a good cereal. I've had others by this brand, and like them as well. Not as crazy about the vanilla in my cereal, and probably won't get this exact one again - but that is a personal preference. I would definitely recommend it to anyone who likes the vanilla idea.

column9: Kids wiped out the box for breakfast
column10: Four girls vs. One box of Crunchy Vanilla Sunrise. Box looses. They loved it. As with all of the Nature's Path products, the ingredients are wholesome and safe as long ss you do not have tree nut allergies. Goes well with milk but tastes better ... in my opinion with soy because of the vanilla flavor.
I wasn't expecting much from this cereal, but it actually turned out to be very delicious AND it kept its crunchiness! I will be buying this cereal again.

column4: J. Rose "JR From the Ball so Blue"
column9: Tasty, delicious start to your day
column10: Nature's Path is a brand I know and trust. Very tasty breakfast surprise. Very vanilla, very crunchy and full of good nutrition. Recommend

column9: Smells delicious and tastes just as good
column10: This is an unusual-looking cereal, but it's absolutely scrumptious! I didn't think it needed any sweetener added, which is unusual. VERY highly recommended!

My son recently began eating gluten-free, and he enjoys this cereal. I am happy about the contents. I like him to start the day off with whole grains. Also, I enjoy the cereal. It tastes and smells a lot like vanilla wafers, which are a favorite of many childhoods. This will become a regular purchase for our household.

The cereal seemed to be overly sweet and more "kiddie" like than expected.  It is a healthier alternative to mainstream cereals for those who prefer a sweeter cereal, maybe a good middle ground.  The cereal was well received and eaten quickly by hubby and the kids (we normally eat organic or Kashi cereals).  I found it to be overly sweet and not very filling.  The bag was only 1/2 full so a little disappointed there as well.  Alternatively, Nature's path makes several organic cereals (without the corn puffs) they sell in a bag at Walmart (sadly not at Target or other stores, I prefer to shop at) that taste good and seem to be a much better bang for your buck.  They still are not as good for you as many other cereals but I feel that they are much better than eating typical kids cereals and good to mix with a healthier one or even for a kids snack.

This cereal is like crack for me. Very sweet, and I could eat half the box in one sitting if I had no self control... Which I kind of did when I first got it in the mail. (I've cut out a lot of added sugars from my diet, so when I have products like this, it tastes even sweeter to me).What I don't like: it's not very filling. I've had plenty of other cereals where I can snack on them without  milk, and after a certain amount, I'll be satisfied. But with this particular product, I am never satisfied and I still feel hungry... Even half a box later.With that said, would I buy this? No. I need foods that will leave me feeling full, and alas, it is too sweet for me to eat on a daily basis.

column9: kix + rice crispies + corn flakes + sugar + vanilla
column10: This cereal looks like someone mixed together kix, rice crispies, and corn flakes. It tastes like they did that, then added sugar and some vanilla. I found it to be both very sweet (the second ingredient is sugar) and not very filling. It turned to mush within about five minutes, too, so unless you're a power-eater, it'll be soggy goop by the end of the bowl.I know that 'contents may settle', but the bag inside the box was only half full, which seemed a bit laughable. Based on what i poured in my cereal bowl, which i admit is far larger than the 'serving size' of 2/3 of a cup, each box contains about four breakfasts. If, however, you only eat 2/3 of a cup of cereal each morning, the box will last you much longer. (The ridiculously small serving size also explains why a cereal that tastes like it's mostly sugar only has 7 grams of sugar per serving.)There are precious few gluten-free cereals on shelves, but there has to be at least one that's better than this.

column9: two out of three kids like it
column10: It's made by the same folks that make the very sweet organic cereals like Gorilla Munch so I expected it to be excessively sweet, but to my surprise, I found it a bit less sweet than most granola.It's a mix of granola-like chunks and cereal-like flakes, with a mild vanilla flavor.One kid was meh, two were enthusiastic.

column9: Average cereal, nothing to write home about
column10: Let me first say that my wife loved this cereal, while I only had one bowl and left the rest to her. She liked the sweetness at first, though soon she was mixing it with other less-sweet organic cereals for better balance.It had too much vanilla for my taste. I like vanilla, but not as the primary flavor in a cereal. I expected it to be a bit more subtle.If you really like vanilla, and like sweet cereals, you may enjoy this one. If, like me, you prefer your breakfast cereal to have a heartier taste, I would not recommend it.

column9: The hippie love child of Kix, Bran Flakes, and Rice Crispies
column10: If that is at all possible, that's what you have here. Good assortment of texture and crunch; the flavor is light, and not too sweet. This is a good addition to your organic cereal portfolio.

column9: A bunch of different cereals in one box
column10: My sister-in-law is gluten free so I'm always on the look out for products she can eat whenever she comes for a visit. As more and more people are developing gluten sensitivity, it's nice that companies are producing more products that are gluten free. The cereal tasted pretty good. It has a hint of sweetness and vanilla. Honestly, it seemed a little bit like cereal on steroids, there were flakes, rice puffs (think rice crispies), little balls, etc. It kind of seemed like someone went through a cereal bar and just added a scoop of everything and mixed it up in the same box.I'm not sure that I'd buy it again though. Flavor-wise it was decent. It wasn't my favorite, but it wasn't bad. I liked that it's organic and G-free.

I found this surprisingly good, it didn't have that "I'm such a good health food that I taste like bamboo and cardboard" flavor. It doesn't go soggy in the first 30 seconds which is REALLY nice. And because it's gluten free, I didn't bloat out like when eating Kashi and other wheat cereals. And I found it just right sweetness-wise, not sure why other reviewers were coming down on it for that. Sweetness is subjective and I probably tolerate a higher level, so for comparison, I can eat Honey Nut Cheerios all day, but if you give me regular Cheerios then I need a bit of sugar or at least a banana thrown in there. If you prefer straight Cheerios out of the box, then you may find this a bit too sweet, but it's not like Frosted Flakes, lol.This is good, definitely one to buy again, although the selling price is a tad high becasue you only get 10 ounces in a box. But good food costs, so I guess I wouldn't expect this to be a buck a box. Enjoy!

We look for a few things when picking out a breakfast cereal: ingredients (whole grains, particularly, minimal anything else, and none of the really bad stuff); crunch, flavor, and ability to hold most of its texture in yogurt or soy milk.Nature's Path Crunchy Vanilla Sunrise was a pleasant surprise. It's really good!We don't insist on organic foods, but, for those who do, this is organic. We don't need a gluten-free diet, but for those who do, this cereal claims to be gluten-free.Here's a quick listing of ALL the ingredients listed on the box (and I'm removing the word "organic," just to save typing time--they're all prefaced by "organic" except for the ones with a hyphen before the name:whole grain corn mealevaporated cane juicebrown rice flouryellow corn flourinulinquinoa puffsflax seeds-natural vanilla flavorbuckwheat flourquinoa-sea saltamaranthmolasses-tocopherols (natural vitamin E)That's it. Pretty good, eh? 110 calories for 2/3 cup. 130 mg sodium, 70 mg potassium, 3g dietary fiber, 7g sugarsThe cereal has a lot of puffs and so is pretty lightweight--but still filling! It's basically puffs (of 2 sizes) and flakes, and they're all crunchy and tasty. They hold most of their crunchiness in a bowl of soy milk (though not overnight, which I found out the yucky way) and on top of yogurt (as long as you don't mix it in and leave it for a few hours, like when you take it to work for lunch).This was a really good change of pace from our usual favorite granola!

I enjoy eating healthy but I am by no means a "health-nut". Recently, I had a friend visit who is glueten free and I tried very hard to find a cereal that we could both eat as I find it wasteful to buy two completely different cereals. I found this one and thought I would give it a shot because it has a lot of the ingredients that I love. It was great! The taste was sweet with a hint of vanilla without being too powerful. I loved the crunch and it kept me full for awhile. I had my friend try it when she came to visit and she loved it! She even said that she wants to get some for herself when she gets home.As you might have noticed, I have rated the cereal with four stars. While everything I have stated is true, I really like it, there is a bit of an after-taste that isn't exactly enjoyable. Of course, I can get past this and my friend did as well. Still, for the amount that they are charging, I expected it to be flawless.

Simply put, I liked this cereal. It is dense enough so it doesn't float on top of the milk, but also stays crunchy for the whole bowl. I also liked the flavor...sweet without being overpowering, but no obvious vanilla flavor. I liked the texture as well, and, unlike some other cereals, it didn't destroy the roof of my mouth. GF was an added bonus.For me, the only drawback was that I couldn't share it with Mrs. Boilermate. She has a peanut allergy, and this is processed on machinery that also processes products containing peanuts.

There's nothing good about this cereal.  It's just a bunch of crunchy puffed rice tossed in with some flakes.  It's tasteless.  It's been sitting up in the cubboard waiting for me to throw it away because I won't eat the rest.  Not worth the calories, when there are other, better cereals out there to start my day with.The ceral box came inside another box, but apparently, a heavier box was thrown on top of it, because the cereal box came crushed with the inside wrapper popped open.  Not sure that this is a product that will ship well.

column9: Light Cereal with a Weird Sweet Taste
column10: I was excited to try Crunchy Vanilla Sunrise because I'm always looking for nutritious breakfast cereal options.  However, this one was a disappointment.  The cereal isn't very filling, despite it's mix of whole grains.  It also has a really strange overly sweet taste.  The taste is very much like an artificial sweetness, which I didn't enjoy, and I felt like it was still there after I added milk.

I do not have a gluten intolerance, so eating gluten-free cereal is not necessary for me personally. I do, however, attempt to eat as healthy as possible and that often means trying foods that are slightly outside of the box for me. I loved that this cereal contained such a great mix of healthy organic grains (quinoa, buckwheat, and amaranth), and that the nothing inside had been genetically modified. That was was enough to get me to try it.The taste is amazing! It's sweet without being too sweet, had a great crunch and stayed crunchy even after sitting in almond milk for a few minutes. The cereal pieces were so close to some of my favorite childhood cereals...in appearance, texture, and taste that I would have no problem feeding this to my son. It was like Kix, Rice Krispies, and Corn Flakes combined to make a healthier cereal. It's awesome!Calories are lower than most other cereals, yet I still felt full a couple of hours after having a normal-sized bowl and a banana. The sodium and sugar are both at good levels, and all of the minimal ingredients are easy to understand.Though no one in my family NEEDS to eat gluten free, we'll definitely continue to purchase this cereal. I was very impressed.

column9: (4.5 stars) Lifts my mood like the morning sunrise
column10: Every Nature's Path product I've had has been great and their Organic Crunchy Vanilla Sunrise cereal is no exception. Featuring about four different shapes and textures into on cereal make for an interesting dining experience, and quite a tasty one at that. With a light vanilla flavor, it's sweeter than I was expecting, this is more for the consumer with a sweet tooth of which I am on occasion, but it isn't so sweet that you'd want to sprint to the nearest dentist after eating. This would be a great cereal for kids as a replacement for the unhealthier cereals marketed for children out there, the only downside is the box screams healthy and not "Kids, eat me!" All organic and natural, the ingredient list a dream; I love when I know what everything actually is. Nature's Path is a product of the USA and the box is made from 100% recycled paperboard, which makes this recycler happy.Here's a glance at the more important nutritional facts:Serving size: 2/3 cup (Seems a bit measly but fairly normal in comparison to most other cereals, which are usually 3/4 cup, but it's about the amount I generally have for breakfast anyway.)Calories: 110 with just the cereal, only 10 from fat.Total fat: 1 gram, no evil fats like saturated or trans, but no polyunsaturated or monounsaturated, which are good for you, either.Cholesterol: ZilchSodium: 130 mgTotal Carbohydrates: 25 gramsDietary Fiber (included in Total Carbs): 3 grams (Could be better but better than a lot of cereals.)Sugars (included in Total Carbs): 7 grams (Not bad, not bad at all. Ideally, one shouldn't have more than 6 g for breakfast, but what's one gram? ;P)Protein: 2 gramsThe cereal is also gluten-free and contains 11% (.15 grams) of omega 3 fatty acids per serving.No real added vitamins to speak of.So, would I buy this again? Heck yeah. The blend of flavors, from the vanilla to the added sweetness to the flakes to the Kix-like spheres, it's one of my new faves. Topped with slices of banana, it lifts my mood like the morning sunrise. :D

Crunchy Vanilla Sunrise is quite a name to live up to. Unfortunately, it fails to live up to the high standards set by branding (and really, most any name). Given the name and a glance at the picture I was expecting some cereal that had granola type chunks mixed in with other stuff, but a heads up to others that might be confused - it does not contain anything resembling granola. It also tastes almost nothing like vanilla, mainly like sweet corn puffs.I am not taking any stars for my own confusion, as I eat lots of different types of cereals. (grapenuts are great (not sweet), but so are Reeses' pb puffs (very sweet). The main problem with this cereal seems to be the target audience, its trying to please the sugar lovers, and the health conscious people at the same time, and that's a hard target audience.The positives:- lives up to the crunchy name- Has decent quality ingredients (especially compared to the vast amounts of junk out there)- Organic and Glutten free- Big kids might like it, (but hard to see them dropping an even sweeter cereal for this one)The negatives:- Lots of sugar (both cane juice - second right behind corn - and molasses) you can taste it- Brings me back to the basic concept - a healthy cereal - but it's  basically organic corn puffs with cane juice and brown rice flour - which are at the low end of whole grains, and comes with just 3g of fiber. Basically the healthier ingredients are sprinkled in. A bit of quinoa, a bit of flax.So basically, if you get your kid to replace Corn Puffs with this, they'll be a bit better off.Yeah, this cereal suffers from an identity crisis. It's not healthy enough for health conscious, and its not marketed or inexpensive enough for a wider audience. Call them glorified corn puffs.

Nature's Path is certainly on the right path when it seems like half of my friends are going gluten-free. When you consider that certain people even though they may think it wise to ween off the wheat substance would find it very difficult because breakfast cereal is such a large part of their diet (guilty), it makes even more sense. Crunchy Vanilla Sunrise fits very nicely in the growing niche market. And it does so with style. This is a tasty cereal and since it's organic and has relatively low amounts of sugar, it's also healthy. The only problem is the weight. This is a light cereal (I guess gluten is really heavy) and thus makes the cost per ounce high. There are more important things than cost, however, and if health is one of those for you, this is a great addition to your cereal box collection.

The best thing I can say about a cereal that comes into my house is I didn't get too much of it because my girls ate it before I could. This cereal has whole grains and natural sweeteners. No one in our family is on a gluten free diet. But, for those who are, here is a natural cereal that doesn't cost an arm and a leg like many other gluten free products. And, it tastes delicious.

column9: Tasty, Nutritious, what could be better?
column10: What do I like about this product? Truth in advertising....It's crunchy -  and stays crunchy in milk. It has a clear vanilla flavor - pure, not artificial tasting. It is healthy and compares well with other similar products in terms of sugar, fiber and general nutrition guidelines. It tastes great and I found myself eating it for breakfast and later on as a inter meal snack. Recommended!

Sweet and crunchy and hard to believe that it's gluten-free!  I like the variety of textures since gluten-free is often sort of lacking in the interesting texture area, and found this cereal great with milk, kefir, or yogurt.  It's also great plain with some roasted almonds as a very satisfying snack mix.  I also used it as a crunchy topping for oatmeal!  Yum!

As luck had it, this cereal arrived the week I had 6 family members visiting - running the gamut from ages 7 - 82.  Most had at least one bowl, and it was well received.I like the fact that it is quite light as cereals go.  Very flavorful, seemed to hold up to milk well, and did not leave an overly full feeling.  Once or twice I grabbed an handful as a quick snack and I enjoyed it dry as well.My sister liked the flavor and consistency - though for her she felt it was a bit lightweight.  So, she mixed in a bit of traditional granola and felt it was the perfect balance.

Was not sure what to expect when ordering and was pleasantly surprised. The texture mixed well with milk keeping a nice crunch. The taste was not over bearing within any of the flavors but a nice mixture of flavors. Was saddened when I came to the end of the box. Would order again.

Wow, I would never have guessed this is gluten free!  It is really quite delicious, not overly sweet, and is nice and crunchy.  It does contain flakes, but not too many which is a bonus for me because I am not keen on cereals that consist predominantly of flakes.  The taste and texture is a great combination and that it is gluten free is just a bonus.

If you are looking for an organic cereal that is gluten free, this is the one you want to try.  This cereal is very good and very filling.  It has a good amount of whole grains in it including quinoa, the super grain.  Enjoy a bowl of this crunchy and sweet cereal.  It's a great way to start you day.

Nature's Path has some wonderful products and I have to say I count this among them. I have had their "Leapin Lemurs" cereal (because I am a kid at heart & we call one of our cats a Lemur).Great price here on Amazon at 3.50 a box. The organic ingredients, gluten free nature, and Omega-3 content are all pluses. No fat, no cholesterol, low sodium and carbs & high fiber are all added pluses. The vanilla (natural) flavour is strong (and welcome to me) but as you chew it, it changes...less vanilla more a light coffee flavour--but that could just be my tongue and brain.The one drawback (if you see it as one) is the lack of added vitamins you get in processed big-company cereals. But let's be honest: if you take a vitamin with your breakfast, do you really need one IN your breakfast. And I guess the different shapes (grains) of the cereal don't stay mixed all that well--so a good shake before pouring helps.A good cereal if you like a sweet start to your morning that is still good for your OR for your young graduates from the cartoon-on-the-box cereals who balk at "healthy" cereals.

I'm a big cereal eater. But as I have gotten older, I have strayed from things that taste cloyingly sweet ... and sorry to say this is one of those cereals that I just couldn't enjoy. I couldn't put my finger on the taste for quite sometime but now I know exactly what this cereal tastes like to me -- Crunch n' Munch. This cereal doesn't have a vanilla taste at all, it seems way too artificial and leaves a slight aftertaste. My husband doesn't agree, that is why I am giving this review four stars. He loves it thought it had a great balance and seemed very different and satisfying from the usual Raisin Brand that sits on our shelf. Another thing of note that we both liked is that this cereal does hold its crunch in milk better than most.

This cereal has a nice crunch to it. When you soak it in milk, all the different parts soften to around the same level, so you don't have that one hard little kernel of a piece that sticks in your teeth.Further, it tastes good. Sweet, but not obnoxiously so, this is a mighty pleasant cereal.It's the kind of cereal that you would gladly introduce to a friend or invite to visit you in a cabin you've rented. If this cereal were music, it would be some early Elvis Costello, or maybe that "California" song they used to play at the beginning of The O.C.It's joyful in that same kind of way.

I ***LOVE*** this cereal!....and I really don't even like cereal.There is no overpowering taste; it is sweet, but not overly sweet or sugary-sweet tasting like many/most sugar cereals, but it has that "naturally sweet" kind of taste. I've allowed two of my gluten-free friends to try it and neither have complained or had issues with it (one is borderline celiac). Anyone can enjoy it (including me: she who doesn't like cereal and who is not gluten intolerant).There is a nice crunch and when eaten with soy (plain soy) milk, there is a nice balance and it just has that perfect crunch....except if you forget about it for several minutes, then it becomes soft - but not soggy. I couldn't seem to stop myself from eating it. There is a bit of a variety of texture because of the multi-grains and shapes/tastes of the cereal itself (i.e. it isn't just flakes or "balls" of one kind of grain). I think that is why it tastes so great is because of the combination of what is inside, the mix...the perfect mix of flavours (along with the use of soy milk instead of cow's milk) that makes it a great cereal one doesn't want to stop eating. Seriously: if I didn't exercise self-control, I would have eaten through the whole box in one (maybe two days)....and that is saying something coming from me.

column9: Different textures makes this buyer weary.
column10: The cereal leaves both soft and crunchy textures. Silly me didn't realize this on checkout, but I was nearing cereal depletion so I needed to replenish.The taste is more bland than flavorful, and I don't think I'm digging the two textures very much. There are puffs mixed in with the crunchy oaty textures, and, honestly, the puffy portions could be left out for all I care.

column9: Very tasty, filling and stays crunchy in milk!
column10: I love vanilla, I choose it over chocolate.  The vanilla taste is perfect in this cereal!  It's low cal, full of healthy goodness, and stays crunchy in milk, which I love!  My biggest peeve is when a cereal goes soggy faster than you can eat it.There is a nice ratio of different pieces to this cereal.  There are little corn puffs, flakes, Rice Krispie type pieces, and little pieces of buckwheat.  I can taste the Rice Krispie type pieces the most.  This stuff isn't too sweet, which is nice because I'm not a sweet breakfast fan.  I have actually used it as a snack as well.There are 110 calories in 2/3 Cup, which satisfies me.  With 3g of dietary fiber, it makes the carbs come out to 22g per serving.  There are no artificial additives in here, like high fructose corn syrup.  They use evaporated cane juice as the sweetener. Less than 1g of fat per serving makes this a wonderful breakfast treat.A gluten free cereal that contains .15g (11% of the recommended daily value) of Omega 3 and 2g of protein is a hit on my list.  I have tried several different kinds of cereal by this brand, and have enjoyed all of them.  I have found a new favorite!

column9: Sweet, pleasant taste. Crunchy but not gritty.
column10: I eat a lot of high fiber cereals and am accustomed to the crunchy, grainy texture the healthy, whole grain cereals usually have. The Nature's Path Crunchy Vanilla Sunrise wasn't like that. No gritty, grainy feel. It had a sweet, pleasant taste with a hint of vanilla. I could taste the corn puffs more than the other grains. I eat my cereal with milk and this held up well and didn't get soggy.While I didn't mind the sweetness, at 7g of sugar per 2/3 cup (the serving size listed on the box), a normal portion probably has double that amount. The cereal provides 3g of dietary fiber per serving but no soluble fiber.Overall, I liked it a lot. Would I eat it again? If it were on sale I would buy it. I don't need to eat gluten free and wouldn't spend the extra to buy a product that was. For those that need gluten free, this is a cereal I would recommend they try.

I'm usually not the type that enjoys the super-organic items that are heavy in flax seed and what not.  I try them off and on -- my girlfriend stocks our cupboards and I get hungry -- but I often don't turn back to the items, surprised at what I found.The exception is this cereal.  I thoroughly enjoyed it and thought that it tasted like a 'normal' cereal you might pick up that's not as healthy as this one.  The vanilla is faint but noticeable, and the cereal lacks the incredibly grainy taste that you can sometimes get by mixing in all of these types of things.On the other hand, my girlfriend said she felt that it was, "too sweet for a granola cereal."So I believe these two points best illustrate its use-case.  For someone like myself -- an individual transitioning to a healthier diet or looking to get a healthier cereal without all of the stereotypical 'healthy taste' -- it's absolutely delicious.  For someone how regularly enjoys bowls of just normal granola or granola cereal, it may come off as a bit sweet.

This is a regular puffed cereal with vanilla flavor. It is crunchy and has organic texture. Overall, this is a blend of light sweetness and vanilla. I recommend adding one cup of milk to 1.5 cups of cereal with sugar if you like extra sweetness.

column9: Very good cereal.  I'm eating it as I type this review
column10: This is a very tasty cereal.  I'm not familiar with Nature's Path cereals, but this is hitting a lot of high marks for me; there is, for example, cane sugar instead of the less desirable high fructose corn syrup.It also has the bonus of not getting too soggy too fast.  I've had the cereal sitting in lactose-free milk for about 10 minutes, and there is (surprisingly) some crunch left in the cereal.  Although I'm not going to run the test too much longer; the cereal is disappearing faster than the crunch disappears.Altogether, a winner!  It's very, very good and it is something I definitely would get again.  I assume because of the careful attention to details on the ingredients, it's going to be in the natural foods department in the supermarket.  I'm going to look for it again.  It's that good and good for you.Solid recommendation for the Nature's Path Crunchy Vanilla Sunrise.  BTW, I threw in a handful of blueberries.  That made it even healthier.

column9: Organic, gluten-free and tasty?  Can it be?
column10: As a big fan of Nature's Path products, I was excited to try a new flavor from them.  But gluten-free and breakfast cereal aren't a normal combination for me.  Further, the list of ingredients they were bragging about; "flax, quinoa, buckwheat, amaranth", did not exactly make me think "yum".But you know what- its super tasty!  If anything it reminded me of the breakfast cereals of my youth (probably because the second listed ingredient is "organic evaporated cane juice" (aka sugar)- so vanilla and sweet are the two dominant tastes.  There is a good amount of fiber (12% of Daily Value per 2/3rd of a cup- lol does anyone really eat that little?).Downsides are the tiny box (10.6 ounces!) that goes pretty fast (because its so tasty).  Also for those with allergies, the cereal is produced in a facility the uses peanuts, tree nuts and soy.But with the Amazon three pack, the size of the individual boxes isn't as much of an issue.  For a super sweet and tasty gluten free breakfast cereal, this one is hard to beat.

If you dislike sweet cereals, take a pass on Nature's Path Organic Crunchy Vanilla Sunrise.  My wife took one taste and pronounced it unpalatable.  Given that I prefer sweet cereals, I was surprised to find that a serving of CV Sunrise has over 4g less sugars than my favorite cereal.  It also has slightly more calories and more calories from fat, with over 1.7 times the total fat of "my" cereal.  Continuing the comparison, a serving of CV Sunrise has over 28mg more sodium, over 26mg less potassium, the same total carbohydrate, about .74g more dietary fiber, about .3g more protein, no Vitamin A vs. 15%, and 4% iron vs. 25%.  Although claiming to be "a good source of fiber", a serving of CV Sunrise yields only 12% daily value.  I agree with other reviewers that the suggested serving size is quite small for an adult breakfast.  I also agree with those who fail to detect much vanilla flavor, an impression supported by "natural vanilla flavor" appearing well down the listing of ingredients.  But CV Sunrise does not disappoint in the "C"!  This is one CRUNCHY cereal, and its puffs keep it crunchy through the last spoonful.  I find its combination of large puffs, small puffs, and flakes more interesting than distracting.  As with many cereals, the cost of CV Sunrise would deter my having it on a regular basis, but it's not bad as a sweet, crunchy cereal.

This is a strange cereal. My daughter described it as rice crispies, corn flakes, and peanut butter panda puffs all thrown together. It tastes pretty good. My main complaint is that this is not a hearty cereal. It has decent nutrition, but I prefer a cereal that will keep me full a while. It makes a great snack, but for me, not a daily food.

Unlike the Quaker Oat squares I recently reviewed (q.v.) (thanks, Vine, for giving me breakfast stuff!), when Nature's Path says vanilla, they MEAN vanilla. Bold, brash, and almost creamy, if you can imagine that in a puffed-grain cereal (I can't either, but it's the only way I can think of to describe the forwardness of the vanilla here). But then there's that "puffed-grain cereal" thing. You get to thinking that a puffed grain is a puffed grain, whether it's rice or quinoa. Lemme tell you something, bub: that ain't true. While the texture here is consistent despite the variety of grains, this has a lighter (forgive me for using this phrase, which I despise, but I can't think of another that makes sense) mouth feel than your good old fashioned rice krispies or whatever.[amusing note: Chrome's spell-check-error-on-a-real-word of the day: quinoa.]I powered through this box in two days, despite knowing that I wouldn't be having it again for a while (save these last Vine reviews of breakfast stuff I'm going low-carb for a spell). Been mulling it over ever since, and I can't think of a better-tasting cereal I've ever had. But to be on the safe side, since I don't remember all the kinds of sickeningly-sweet cereal I ate as a kid (as a yardstick, when I was growing up, we still had sugar smacks, sugar corn pops, and all the other cereals that compared to today were paragons of truth in advertising), I'll say this one's definitely in the top five. Were I not going low-carb I would be perfectly content to eat this stuff for breakfast every day for the rest of my life. It's THAT good. *****

this tea is lovely - not too overpowering in flavor and not too weak either - it has a pleasant aroma and tastes wonderful - i am happy with this product and will order more tea from them in the future!

Its always cheaper when I buy them from Amazon's subscribe and save program.......and THE SHIPPING IS FREE......WONDERFUL!!!!

Excellent taste  I will purchase again price right  fast shipping  I have shared it with others the best flavor peppermint coffee I have tasted

I guess this coffee is good. I bought it for a Christmas present. Hopefully the person will enjoy it. Tis the season for giving...
My husband is a "cinnamon snob".  This is the only cinnamon he will use. He loves it in his oatmeal. He goes through a jar of it every 2 weeks. That's a lot of cinnamon.
i love this butter. it's better than regular butter and makes eggs or anything else taste great. Plus it's organic with higher levels of Conjugated Linoleic Acid (CLA). A must in every home, i think

My friend Kevin and I are root beer connoisseurs.  We must have tried over 50 different brands, some great, Salty Dog, many ok and a few horrid (who'd a thunk).  Meanwhile, we found the Boylan's brand of delicious root beer and, angelic voices singing, Boylan's Creamy Red Birch Beer.  Nuttin' like it.  Never disappoints.  Difficult to describe.  Not too fruity, not a false red taste.  Not root beer, not bitter, not overly sweet.  A satisfying taste, a unique flavor found nowhere else.  We immediately decided it was the champagne of root beer even though there's that sub-category of birch beer.  I gotta try more birch beers but have yet to get my hands on a creamy red birch beer.  There's undoubtedly some out there.  Lemme at them.  Meanwhile, for the last 6 or so years we've reveled in this beverage, happily purchasing it for about a buck fifty a bottle from one of two stores in town.  Now I see neither store carries it any longer.  A sad day.  I'm hoping to find another retailer in San Diego who does.  Meanwhile, I'm gonna order some from Amazon.  Drink hearty me maties.  Ain't nuttin' like it.  Everyone we've turned on to it recognizes the high quality, special taste treat.  Lovely.

This stuff is a New Jersey classic, spicy wintergreen with vanilla overtones, excellent out of the frosty glass bottle or a unique treat as a float with mint chocolate chip ice cream!  I wish they sold this flavor in more locations!

I bought this for my son for Christmas.  He tasted this when we were away and loved it.  I could not find it locally so I purchased it here.  Sounds like an odd way to buy a beverage, but when you can't find it.....!  This product is true to the taste of Birch Beer. Arrived without any damage. A bit pricey for soda, but it was a surprise gift.

I love this stuff; fortunately for me, it is available locally, so I drink some every week.  I've become very addicted to it.  I also love ginger beer, but when I have a choice, I usually pick up a bottle of birch beer.  I've yet to try the original flavored one, but I see it is available here so I'll have to try it.  This is a pretty good deal, as the only other online retailer I've found only sells 6-packs ($19.32 includes shipping) or 24-bottle cases.  Those cases cost $27.99 plus $24.12 S/H, so 12 for $30 and free shipping on Amazon is close enough.

column9: Root Beer lovers will like it, Birch Beer lovers will worship it!
column10: I couldn't find this product anywhere in stores in CT or New York City.  That qualifies it in my book as really "hard to find"!  This has the distinctive taste of birch beer without the edge that can be found in some birch beers.  The taste is simply superlative!  As other reviewers have noted, it's slightly less carbonated than most sodas, but it's a full bodied, sweet, and glowingly red.  I love this stuff!  It doesn't have the mildly spicy taste of the Boylan's regular Birch Beer, which I also love.  This is different, it's a smoother but just as tasty a drink.  I give it 5 stars.  To me, and I've had a lot of these premium sodas, this is the best in class.  As another reviewer noted, and I agree, It has a "champagne" quality to it in that it's taste and precise carbonation give it a very refined quality you generally don't find in soda.It's simply the best tasting soda I have ever had.  Hard to pick between this and Boylan's regular Birch Beer which is spicier and slightly more bubbly, but also an outstanding soda.  Love it, love it, love it!  I highly recommend it!
They use real ingredients and cane sugar- and it shows! I could drink my way through a case of this in one sitting.

I had never even heard of birch beer, much less tried it, until I ran into the Boylan's Creamy Red Birch Beer... and I have to say that it is great. Smooth taste that delights the palate with just the right touch of sweetness. A new fave in my household. Try it !
Not bad-tasting at all, but not a very defined taste, rather muted in fact.  If you like sparkling drinks rather than true carbonation, this one's for you.

I ordered Boylan's Birch Beer June 7th sent an email after 2 week to them through Amazon never received a reply. Amazon should auto delete this order because of no action by Boylan's for 30 days.The really sad part of this story is that they make really super great Birch Beer soda.I have since been able to find Boylan's in a local store here in Florida.

column4: Shawn K. Hall "Mr. or Mrs. Hall"
column10: I rated SeaAloe a five because of the health benefits, the company is another matter. SeaAloe, previously named SeaSilver, helped get me back on my feet after back surgery and a rough time with Sciatica and Fibromyalgia. It was a miracle to me, after spending over a year in bed.I don't eat right, I admit it. This a terrific product, especially if you have poor eating habits. The taste of this product is tolerable (it's not great), compared to so many others I've tried. The company claims this is the exact same formula as SeaSilver but I have noticed a slight taste difference.When I first began taking SeaSilver (SeaAloe), I didn't really notice a huge difference in my health, until I stopped taking it. While I appreciate knowing when my product has shipped, I like ordering through Amazon because I trust them.SeaAloe arrived packaged well (complete with styrofoam peanuts, which isn't environmentally friendly) and arrived within four-days of placing my order.I really love this product and have found the health benefits to be worth the cost. After combining SeaAloe with plenty of exercise, I sleep better and my quality of life has drastically improved. I was in pretty bad shape, when I started taking it. I decided to give it a try because I had nothing to lose and everything to gain.

I have only been taking this supplement for a few days, so I'm not sure how helpful this review will be, maybe I will update it after taking it for awhile. First, the taste is really good, for a supplement. It taste like slightly sweetened cherry extract, with a flat (nothing there) aftertaste. I was suprised for a liquid supplement it has no bitter or mineral taste. I could take it every day easily. And I do like that it is a whole food and not a man made supplement.  What I don't like about it is that it doesn't list how much of something you are getting or the daily percentage of RDA. I don't think it has been evaluated by consumer labs - I didn't see it listed, but then again I didn't sign up. I don't like how it is marketed, you can sell it yourself, and I tend to distrust home marketing businesses. I'm not sure I like that it has D'Arco in it, the lady at the health food store said that it has no known side effects or contraidictions, but I have seen online reports of possible effects.  As for effectiveness, I have only been taking it for a very short time, so the review is not complete. But, I have noticed my skin is firmer, and I have a healthy pink glow to my face. This usually happens if I am taking a good antioxidant. I haven't noticed any increase in energy. There does seem to be a slight decrease in joint pain (D'Arco is supposed to be good for inflammation). My gums look healthier, but I have also been using Biotene mouthwash. So I guess what I am saying, is take at your own risk, or do more research. Maybe there are better liquid supplements out there, with no herbs in them. Even herbs that have no reported side effects, sometimes have bad effects for me.

column9: Topo Chico beats any other mineral water brand
column10: I love Topo Chico. Topo Chico on ice with a squeeze of lime is extremely refreshing. It feels like you are drinking a drink.I prefer Topo Chico over any mineral water out there.Yes, I pay good money for water from Mexico. Hands down, it's the best!

Topo chico  some lime and salt over ice is fantastic....we also make a summertime drink out of it tall glass salt rimmed full of ice with a shot of vodka or tequila a couple of oz of zing zang or your favorite bloody marry mix some lime juice and top off with Topo Chico garnish with a lime we call it a Fizzy Marry
